It is as wide of a palm as it is of a seat, our members are different from yours. There is no similarity here. Let the Christian heart be ashamed of having such an idol within itself. Consequently, he considers that heaven is all the saints; In fact, the earth is also taken for all those who inhabit it: May all the earth worship you. If we are correct in saying: May the whole earth adore you, thinking of those who inhabit it, we are equally correct in saying: "All the heavens uphold you", thinking of those who live there. For the saints themselves, who live on earth, trample it with their flesh, but with their hearts they live in heaven. It is not in vain that they are exhorted to lift up their hearts and, once they have received the exhortation, they respond that they do so; Nor is it in vain that getting up is done in the direction of the head. Signifying this, the Apostle says: If you have been raised with Christ, seek the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God; Taste the things above, not those of the earth. Of them, as soon as they announce the word of God, it is said: The heavens narrate the glory of God. 15. Return, then, with me to the face of the heart. You have to prepare this. It is the inner man in which Christ dwells provisionally by faith. There he must dwell with the presence of his divinity, one in palmo suo, quam laus in sessione sua, disparia membra nobis fecit. There is no similarity. Erubescat ergo tale idolum in corde christiano. Proinde caelum accipe pro omnibus sanctis. Quia et terra dicitur pro omnibus qui sunt in terra: Omnis terra adoret te (Ps 64,4). Yes bene dicimus secundum eos qui habitant in cáelo, Omnis terra adoret te: bene dicimus etiam secundum eos qui habitant in cáelo, Omne caelum portet te. Ñon enim frustra admonentur sursum habere cor, et cum admoniti fuerint, ita esse responder: aut frustra [371] sursum versus ad caput eminet: et ea significatur dicitur, Si consurrexistis cum Christo, quae sursum sunt quarite, ubi Christus est in dextera Dei sedens; quae sursum sunt sapite, non quae super terram (Col 3,1 et 2).

once we have known the breadth, length, height and depth, and we have also known the surpassing charity of the knowledge of Christ, so that we may be filled with the fullness of God. If, then, you do not dislike this way of understanding, apply yourself to understanding that width, length, height and depth. Do not wander with your imagination through mundane spaces or the grandeur of this huge mass, but understandable with the mind. Look within yourself for what I am going to tell you. Breadth consists of good works; length, in long-suffering and perseverance in good works; the height, in the expectation of eternal goods, in view of which you are exhorted to have your heart lifted up. Do good and persevere in good works, thinking about the benefits of God. Consider earthly things as nothing, lest, if this earth is disturbed by any scourge of that wise man, you will dare to say that you have served God in vain, that you did good works in vain and persevered in them in vain. When you did good, there was breadth in you; by persevering in it, length; but when you seek the earthly you lack height. Now consider the depth: it is the grace of God in the mystery of his will. Who knew the mind of the Lord? Or who was his advisor? Listen also: Your judgments are an unfathomable abyss. 16. This life consists in doing good, in perseverance in it, in hoping for good things from above and in the mysterious bestowal of the grace of God, all of which is wisdom and not infidem: ibi habitaturos praesentia divinitatis suae, cum cognoverimus quae sit latitudo, longitudo, altitudo, profundum; cognoverimus etiam supereminentem scientiae caritatem Christi, ut impleamur in omnem plenitudinem Dei (Eph 3,17-19). Nunc ergo si tibi intellectus hic non displicet, advoca te comprehendcre latitudinem, longitudinem, altitudinem, profundum. Non discurras imaginatione cogitationis per spatia mundana, et per molis huius tam magnae comprehensibilem granditatem. In attends to you quod dico. Latitudo est in bonis operibus; longitude est in longanimitate ct perseverantia bonorum operum; altitude is in supernorum exspectarione praemiorum; propter quam altitudinem tibi dicitur ut sursum cor babeas. Bene operare, et in bonis operibus persevera, propter benefit Dei.

Terrena pro nihilo aestimes, ne cum tibi aliquo sapientis illius flagello ierra ista fuerit perturbata, dicas te sine causa Deum coluisse, sine causa bona opera fecisse, sine causa in bonis operibus perseverasse. Doing cnim bona opera, quasi habuisti latitudinem: persevering in eis, quasi habuisti longitudinem: sed terrena conquirendo, non habuisti altitudinem. Attende profundum: gratia Dei est in occulto voluntatis eius. Quis enim cngnovit sensum Domini? aut quis consiliarius eius Fuit? (Rom 11:34). I'.t, ludicia tua sicut tumba abyssus (Ps 35,7). CAPUT XV.—16. Crucis quattiior dimensions.—Hanc conversationem bene operandi, in ea perseverandi, superna exspectandi, gratiam Dei occulte dandi, sapientia, non stültitia; nec reprehendendi- quare alius sic,

sanity; It consists of not criticizing God, because one goes here and another there, since there is no iniquity in him. All this, I repeat, accommodate it to the cross of your Lord. If it was in his power to die or not to die, it was not without reason that he chose that type of death. If it was in his power to die or not to die, how could it not also be in his power to die in one way or another? Not without reason, then, did he choose the cross, in which he would crucify you for this world. On the cross, the width corresponds to the transverse stick, to which the hands are nailed, as a sign of good works. The length corresponds to that part of the wood that goes from the transverse stick to the ground. There the body is crucified and in a certain way remains standing, symbolizing perseverance. The height corresponds to what goes from the transverse stick upwards, a symbol of the expectation of celestial goods. And the depth? Doesn't it correspond to the part that is nailed to the ground? This is how grace is: hidden and hidden12. You don't see her, but what you see emerges from her. After what has been said, if you have understood everything, not only with intelligence, but also with action - since good intelligence belongs to those who put it into practice - then apply yourself now, if you can, to achieving the knowledge of the charity of Christ, which surpasses all science. When you have achieved this you will be filled with the fullness of God. Then the face to face will take place. You will be filled with the fullness of God; That is, you are not going to fill God, but God will fill you. Seek in him, if you can, a corporeal face. Let the trifles of the gaze alius autem sic disappear now; non enim est iniquitas apud Deum (2 Par 19,7, et Rom 9,14): hanc ergo conversationem, si placet, coapta etiam cruci Domini tui. Non enim frustra talem mortem elegit, in cuius potestate erat vel mori vel non mori. Si in potestate erat mori et non mori, quare non in potestate sic vel sic mori? Nonfrustra ergo cruzem elegit, ubi te huic mundo crucifigeret. Nam latitudo est in intersection transversum lignum, ubi figuntur manus: propter bonorum operum significationem. Longitude is in ea parte ligni, quae ab ipso transverso ad terram tendit. Ibi enim corpus crucifigitur, et quodam moda stat: et ipsa statio perseverantiam significat. Altitudo autem in illo ligno est, quod ab eodem transverso [372] supernorum exspectatio. Ubi profundum, nisi in ea parte quae terrae defixa est? Occulta est enim gratia, et in abdito latet. Non videtur, sed inde eminet quod videtur.

of the mind. The child throws away his toys and learns to handle bigger things. We are also like children in many things. And when we were more so than we are now, the elders put up with us. Seek peace and sanctification with all, without which no one will be able to see God. This, then, is what cleanses the heart; there is present the faith that works through love. Consequently: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
Topic: The beatitudes (Mt 5,3-10). Date: Between the year 405 and 411, or at the end of his life. Location: Unknown.

1. Your charity has heard the holy Gospel at the same time as I. May the Lord help me so that, when speaking to you about the chapter we have read, what I tell you is appropriate for you and bears fruit in your customs. Everyone who hears the word of God must think that what he hears in it will happen. Do not seek to praise the word of God with your tongue and despise it with your life. What he says feels soft when you listen to it; How much greater will that softness be in a corporal. Iam tollantur nugae a mentis aspectu. Abiciat puer parvulus ludiera, discat tractare maiora. Et nos in multis parvuli sumus: et cum plus quam sumus essemus, a maioribus tolerati sumus. Pacem sectamini cum omnibus, et sanctificationem, sine qua nemo polerit videre Deum (Hebr 12,14). Hac enim et cor mundatur; quia ibi est fides quae per dilectionem operatur. Hinc, Beati mundicordes, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt. IT IS RAÍ OR
DE OCTO SENTENTIIS BEATITUDINUM EX EVANGELIO (Mt.

1. Sanctum evangelium audivit nobiscum caritas vestra: de ipso capitulo quod recitatum est loquentes nos ad vos adiuvet dominus, ut ea quae dicimus apta sint vobis, et fructificent in moribus vestris. Omnis enim auditor verbi dei cogitare debent, secundum hoc quod audit debené evenire; nec quaerat verbum dei laudare lingua, et vita contemnere. Si enim quae dicuntur suavia sunt cum audiuntur, quanto suaviora debent esse cum

once done! We preachers are the sowers, you are God's field. Let the seed not perish; bear fruit and become mine. Together with me you have heard Christ, the Lord. When the disciples came to him, he opened his mouth and taught them these words: 'Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven, and what follows.' His disciples having approached him, the one and only true Teacher taught them, telling them what I have briefly recalled. You too have approached me so that, with his help, I may speak to you and teach you. Can I do anything better than teach what such a great Master has said? 2. Be poor in spirit, then, so that the kingdom of heaven may be yours. Why do you fear being poor? Think of the riches of the kingdom of heaven. Poverty is feared; There is fear, yes, but of evil. For after the poverty of the righteous will come great happiness, because there will be complete security. Here, on the other hand, the more wealth increases—so-called, without being so—, fear also increases and ambition does not end. You can introduce me to many rich people: but can you introduce me to one who has security? He burns with the desire to possess and trembles at the possibility of losing what he has possessed. When is such a slave free? He is a slave who serves any matron and is he free who serves greed? Blessed, then, are the poor in spirit. Who are the poor in spirit? Not the poor in wealth, but in desires. He who is poor in spirit is humble; and God fiunt? Similes enim nos sumus seminantibus, vos autem agri dei estis: non pereant semina, fructificet messis. Dominus Christum audistis nobiscum, cum accessissent ad eum discipuli eius, aperiens os suum docebat eos dicens: beati pauperes sipritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum caelorurn (Mt 5,2-3), et reliqua. Accedentes ergo ad se disciples suos magister unus et verus docebat ista dicens quae commemoravimus breviter. Et vos accessistis ad nos, ut ipso adiuvante loquamur vobis, etczemamus vos. Quid melius facimus, quam cum ea docemus, quae tantus magister exponens dixit? 2. Estote ergo pauperes spiritu, ut vestrum sit regnum caelorum. Quid timetis esse pauperes? Cogitate divitias regni caelorum. Tímetur paupertas: timeatur, be wicked. Nam post paupertatem iustorum veniet magna congratulations, quia plena securitas; hic autem quanto magis augentur divitiae quae vocantur et non sunt, et timor augetur, et cupiditas non finitur.

Potes mihi daré divites multos: unum mihi securum will I give potes? Ardescit, ut adquirat: tremit, ne perdat. When liber is talis servus? Servus est, qui servit qualicumque dominae: et liber est qui servit avaritiae? Beati ergo pauperes spiritu. What is it, pauperes spiritu? [679] Pauperes voluntatibus, non facultatibus. Ule enim qui spiritu pauper est, Possibly, Saint Augustine mentioned all the beatitudes here and a later copyist replaced them with the et reliqua. This is what D. MORIN thinks in Miscellanea Agostiniana 1,627.
The Beatitudes

He listens to the groans of the humble and does not reject their supplications. The first recommendation that the Lord made in the Sermon on the Mount was humility, that is, poverty. You can find a pious man with an abundance of earthly goods, but not puffed up with pride. You can find another man in need, who lacks everything and rests in things that are nothing. This one has no more hope than that one. He is, in fact, poor in spirit because he is humble; This one, on the contrary, is poor, but not in spirit. That is why Christ the Lord, when he said: Blessed are the poor, he added in spirit. Therefore, do not seek to be rich, those of you who have listened to us and are poor. 3. Listen to the Apostle, not to me. Look what he said: Great gain is the piety that is satisfied with enough. We brought nothing into this world and we can take nothing from it. Having food and shelter, let us be content. For those who want to become rich—he did not speak of those who are, but of those who want to become so 2—fall into temptation and into the trap and into many foolish and harmful desires, which plunge men into death and perdition. Greed is the root of all evil. Many, because they desired it, strayed from the faith and ended up in many pains. When you hear the word “riches” it sounds sweet. But are these others sweet: do they fall into temptation? Or these: many foolish and harmful desires? Are the names of death and perdition sweet? And the coming to give in many humilis est: et audit deus gemitus humilium, et non contemnit preces eorum. Inde coepit dominus commendare sermonem suum, ab humiiitate, id est a paupertate. Invenis hominem religiosum, abundantm bis rebus terrenis, nec tamen inflatum superbia. Invenís hominem egentem, nihil habentem, et in rebus nullis sedentem. Non magis iste spem habet, quam ille: Ule est enim pauper spiritu, quia (628) humilis est; This autem pauper est, et non spiritu. Ideo dominus Christus cum dixisset beati pauperes, addidit spiritu. Quicumque ergo nos audistis et pauperes estis, nolite quaerere divites esse. 3. Audite apostolum, non me, videte quid dixerit: est autem, inquit, quaestus magnus pietas cum sufjicientia. Nihil enim intulimus in hunc mundum, sed nec auferre aliquid possumus. Victum et tegumentum habentes, his contenté simus.

Nam qui volunt divites fieri—non dixit, qui sunt, sed, qui volunt fieri—qui ergo volunt divites fieri, incidunt in templationem, inquit, et in laqueum, et desideriamulta stulta et noxia, quae mergunt homines in interitum et in perditionem. Radix est enim omnium malorum avaritia, quam quidam appetentes a fide erraverunt, et inseruerunt se doloribus multis (1 Tim 6:10). Quasi dulce nomen, est, quando audiuntur divitiae. Incident in temptationem, never sweet nomen est? Desideria fine stulta et noxia, never sweet nomen est? Interitus et perditio, never sweet nomen est? Inserted doloribus multis, nunquid This textual nuance is not uncommon in Augustine. See also sermons 2? A,2 (= POUT 12); 61.10; 177.6; Ewrmion to Psalm 136:14,

pains? Do not be seduced by a false good that carries with it so many true evils. With these words the Apostle addressed himself not to the rich, but to those who are not rich so that they do not want to be what they are not yet. Let us now see what is best for those whom he found to be already rich. We have said what needed to be said. Those of you who have heard it are poor. But if there are rich people among those present here, let them also listen to the blessed Apostle. 4. Writing to his disciple Timothy, he exhorted him, among other things, to the following: Command the rich of this world. The word of God found them already rich. If he had found them poor, he would have told them what he mentioned above. Command the rich of this world not to behave arrogantly, nor to put their hope in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God who abundantly grants us all things to enjoy. Be rich in good works, give easily, distribute, store up for yourself a good foundation for the future, to achieve eternal life. Let's reflect a little on these brief words. First of all, he said: Command the rich not to behave arrogantly. There is nothing that engenders pride as easily as riches 3. If the rich man were not proud, he would trample on riches and depend on God. The proud rich man does not possess, but is possessed. The proud rich man is like the devil. If he does not have God, what does the proud rich man have? 4 He also added this: dulce nomen est? Non te seducat unum falsum bonum, ut haereas tot veris malis. Quia veto his verbis beatus apostolus non est alloquutus eos qui divites sunt, sed eos qui non sunt, ne velit esse quod non sunt, videamus etiam quibus conveniat eos quos iam divites invenit. Diximus vobis quae diganda fuent, vos qui pauperes estis audistis; si qui autem hic divites estis, eundem ipsum beatum apostolum audite. 4. Sctibens ad Timotheum discipulum suum, Inter cetera quae illum monuit, etiam hoc dixit: praecipe divitibus huius mundi. Iam verbum dei divites eos invenit: nam si pauperes eos invenisset, illa dixisset quae iam commemoravi. Praecipe ergo divitibus huius mundi non superbe sapere, ñeque sperare in incerto divitiarum, sed in deo vivo, qui praestat nobis omnia abundantr ad fruendum. Divites sint in operibus bonis, facile tribuant, communicent, thesaurizent sibi fundamentum bonum in futurum, ut apprehendant vitam [680] veram (1 Tim 6:17-19). Considermus paululum pauca verba ista.

Ante omnia, inquit, praecipe ditivibus non superbe sapere. Nihil enim sic generat superbiam quomodo divitiae. Dives si non fuerit superbus, calcavit divitias, (629) suspendit se ad deum; dives superbus non possidet, sed possidetur. Dives superbus similis est diabolo. Dives superbus quid habet, quando deum non habet? Adiecit etiam: Thought often repeated by the saint. See Supplementary Note 34: Pride and Riches vol. VII p.756, See the note to the sermon 53,6.

And do not put your hope in the uncertainty of riches. He must possess riches knowing that they are perishable. Possess, then, what you cannot lose. After having said: And do not put your hope in the uncertainty of riches, he added: But in the living God. Riches, in fact, can perish; May they perish in such a way that they do not ruin you! The psalm speaks and laughs at the rich who puts his hope in riches: although man walks in the image of God. Indeed, man was made in the image of God; recognize, then, that it has been done, lose what he himself made and remain what is the work of God. Although man walks in the image of God, he worries in vain. What does it mean to worry in vain? He accumulates treasures and does not know for whom. This is what the living warn about the dead; They observe how the children of many do not possess the property of their parents, but either waste what was left to them in lust, or lose it by being the object of slander. And, what is more serious, while one searches for what one has, the one who has it also perishes. Many lose their lives for their wealth at the hands of others. What they had, they left it here. With what face will they present themselves before God, if they did not do what he had commanded? May your riches be true: God himself, who gives us things in abundance for us to enjoy. 5. Be rich, he said, in good works. Riches are manifested there; sow in that field. The Apostle spoke of such works when he said: Let us not tire of doing good. In due time we will harvest. Sow; He does not yet see what he must expect in incerto divitiarum. Sic debent habere divitias, ut sciat posse perire quod habet. Habeat ergo quod perse non potest. Cum ergo dixisset, ñeque sperare in incerto divitiarum, adiecit, sed in deo vivo. Divitiae quippe possunt perire: et utinam sic pereant, ut non te perdant. Alloquitur et irridet psalmus divitem sperantem in divitiis: quamquam in imaginem dei ambulet homo (Ps 38,7). Factus est enim utique homo ad imaginem dei; sed agnoscat se quod factus est, perdat quod ipse fecit, et maneat quod eum deus fecit. Quamquam ergo in imaginem dei ambulet homo, tamen vane conturbabitur. Quid est, vane conturbabitur? l'hesaurizat, et nescit cui congregavit ea (ib.).

Viventes attendunt ista de mortuis: vident multorum mortuorum bona non possideri a filiis eorum, sed aut luxuriando I will lose quod eis dimissum est, aut per calumnias amittere; et, quod est gravius, dum quaeritur quod habet, perit et qui habet. Multi occiduntur propter divitias suas. Ecce quod habebant hic dimiserunt: quando quod iussit inde non fecerunt, qua fronte ad eum exierunt? Sint ergo tibi divitiae verae: ipse deus, qui praestat nobis omnia abundantr ad fruendum. 5. Divites sint, inquit, in operibus bonis. Ibi appareant divitiae, ibi seminent. De talibus enim operibus loquebatur idem apostolus, ubi ait: bonum autem facientes non deficiamus: tempore enim metemus (Gal 6,9).

obtain; create and cast the seed. When the farmer sows, does the farmer already see the harvest gathered? He throws the wheat stored with fatigue and care from one side to the other. He entrusts his seeds to the earth, and you do not entrust your works to him who made heaven and earth? So be rich, but in good works. Give easily, distribute. What is repartan? Do not own alone. You told us, oh Apostle!, and you taught us to be sowers; also show us the harvest. He showed it. Listen to what it is. Miser, do not be lazy to sow. Listen, I repeat, what is the harvest. He added something more by saying: Be rich in good works, give easily, distribute. With this he has done nothing more than invite them to throw the seed; They will also say what they are going to collect. Lay up for yourselves a good foundation for the future, to attain eternal life. This false life in which riches cause delight is temporary. Therefore, after this one must reach the true one. You love what you own; put it in a safer place so as not to lose it. If you love wealth, whoever you are, surely all your concern will be not to lose what you possess. Hear some advice from your Lord. This place on earth is not safe; transfers everything to heaven. You wanted to entrust to your most faithful servant what you had accumulated; rather entrust it to your Lord! 5 Your servant, even if he is faithful to you, may lose it unintentionally; but your God can lose nothing. Whatever you entrust to him you will have with him when you have him. Seminent: nondum videt quod adquisiturus est: credat et spargat. Nunquid enim agricultural seminator, iam videt segetem collectam? Tanto labore fmmentum et tanta cura reconditum eicit et proicit. lile credit semina sua terrae: tu opera tua non credis ei qui fecit caelum et terram? Ergo divites sint, sed in operibus bonis. Fucile tribuant, communicent. Quid est, communkent? Non soli habeant. Dixisti, o apostóle, et docuisti faceré sementem: ostende et messem. Ostendit. Audi et messem. O avare, noli piger esse seminare: audi, inquam, et messem. Adiungit enim, cum díxisset, divites sint in operibus bonis, facile tribuant, communicent; quia hoc solum dixit, ut spargant, deben [681] dicere quid colligant. Thesaurizent, inquit, sibi fundamentum bonum (630) in futurum, ut apprehendant veram vitam. Transitura est false vita, ubi delectant divitiae. Ergo post istam vitam veniendum est ad veram vitam. Amas quod habes: hoc tutiore loco pone, ne perdas.

1. It usually worries many, dearly beloved, that our Lord Jesus Christ, having said in the Sermon on the Mount: Let your light shine before men, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven, then said: Take care not to do your good works before men to be seen by them. This causes, in effect, confusion in the mind of one who is short of intelligence, and, certainly desiring to obey one precept or another, he fluctuates between diverse and adverse thoughts. One cannot obey a single master who orders contrary things ii 1 at the same time, just as no one can serve two masters, according to the testimony of the Savior in the same sermon. What, then, is to do the indecisive soul that considers that it cannot obey and at the same time fears not to? If you expose your good works to the public light so that they can be seen by men, in order to fulfill what is commanded: Let your light shine before men so that they can see your good works.

If you do your works and glorify Your Father who is in heaven, you will consider yourself guilty of having acted against the precept that says: Take care not to do your good works before men to be seen by them. And if, on the contrary, out of fear and caution he hides the good that he does, he will judge not to serve the one who commands and tells him: Let your light shine before men so that they may see your good works. Listen, therefore, to Paul, servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, segregated for the Gospel of God; He fulfills and teaches one thing and another. See how his light shines before men so that they may see his good works: We recommend ourselves, he says, to every conscience of men in the presence of God, And in another place: We take care to do good, not only before God, but also before men. They were listened to for their evil. But when the fullness of time came, what was predicted was fulfilled: And it will come to pass that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. And later, since the Jews themselves, even those who had believed in Christ, looked with evil eyes on the Gentiles who had received the Gospel, they maintained that it should not be announced to those who were not circumcised. Against them the apostle Paul presented this testimony: And it will come to pass that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved, immediately adding, to convince those who did not want the Gospel to be preached to the Gentiles, the following: How will they call on him in whom they have not believed? Or how will they believe in him of whom they have not heard? How will they hear if no one preaches to them? Or how will they preach if they are not sent? He said: How will they call on him in whom they have not believed? This is the reason why you did not receive first the prayer and then the symbol, but first the symbol to know what you are to believe, and then the prayer in which you know who you are to invoke. The symbol, therefore, relates to faith; prayer, to supplication, since whoever believes is heard through his invocation. 2. There are many who ask for what they should not, because they do not know what is best for them. Whoever invokes God must be careful of two things: asking for what he should not and asking for it from whom he should not. There is nothing to ask from the devil, idols and demons. If you have to ask for something, you have to ask it from our Lord Jesus Christ; to God, father of prophets, apostles and martyrs, to

the father of our Lord Jesus Christ, to the God who made heaven and earth and all that they contain. But we must guard against asking for what we should not. If you ask for the human life that we must ask for from mute and deaf idols, what do you live for? The same thing if you ask God the Father for the death of your enemies, what does it profit you? Did you not hear or read, in the psalm that speaks of the detestable traitor Judas, what the prophecy says about him: May his prayer be counted as sin? If, then, you rise up to pray evil for your enemies, your prayer will turn into sin. 3. In the holy psalms you have read how the person who speaks in them launches many and serious imprecations against his enemies. And certainly, someone will say, the person who speaks there is fair. Why then does he wish such evils upon his enemies? He does not desire them, but foresees them; It is the prophecy of the one who announces, not the vote of the one who wishes evil. The prophets knew in spirit to whom evils were going to befall and to whom good things were going to happen, and they said this using prophecy, as if they desired what they foresaw. You, on the other hand, how do you know that the one for whom you ask evil must not be better than you? "But I know, you say, that he is evil." You also know that you are just as much as he is. Although it may be bold on your part to judge another person's unknown heart, you know with certainty that you are evil. Do you not hear the Apostle say: I was first a blasphemer, a persecutor and a harmer, but I obtained mercy?

Saints, do you have debts? "We have them too." «You too? God save you from it, Lord 7. Do not do this injury to yourself. «I do not insult myself, but I tell the truth. "We have debts." If we say that we have no sins, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us. Although we are baptized, we have debts. Not because something was left unforgiven in baptism, but because as we live we contract others that must be forgiven every day. Those who die after being baptized, without any debt they ascend to God, without any debt they leave. Those who continue in this life after being baptized contract something due to their mortal fragility, which, although it does not cause shipwreck, should nevertheless be reduced. Because if the water is not reduced in a ship, little by little it penetrates as much as is necessary for it to sink 8. This is praying: bailing out the water. But we must not only pray; You must also give alms, because when you bail out the water to prevent the ship from sinking, you act with your voice and your hands. We act with the voice when we say: Forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors. We act with our hands when we do this: Break your bread with the hungry and shelter the homeless in need in your house. Keep alms in the heart of the poor and she herself will pray to the Lord for you. 12. Although by the washing of regeneration all sins were forgiven us, we would find ourselves in great distress. I do not want you to consider yourselves righteous, as if you did not have to say: Forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors. Even abstaining from idolatry, astrology and witchcraft 9; even moving away from the deceptions of heretics and schismatic divisions; even without committing homicides, adulteries and fornications, thefts and robberies, false testimonies and other things - and I am not referring to those that lead to death, which necessarily require separation from the altar 10 and ties here on earth that entail others in heaven, with extremely dangerous and deadly effects, unless unleashed on earth they are also unleashed in heaven; Even if we abstain from all that has been said, man does not lack ways of sinning. He to whom you say: Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven, is the one who grants it to you. Don't think it's impossible. I know, I know, I have proven that there are Christians who love their enemies. If it seems impossible to you, don't do it. As a first step, believe that it is possible and pray that God's will be fulfilled in you. What benefit do you get from the evil of your enemy? If I had no evil, I would not be your enemy. Wish him good, wish him to abandon evil and he will cease to be your enemy. It is not, in fact, his human nature that is the enemy, but his guilt. Is he your enemy because he has soul and flesh? It's like you: you have a soul, he has one too; If you have meat, so does he. It is consubstantial to you; You were made of like earth, you were animated by God one and another. 1. The order of your instruction requires that you learn first what you are to believe and then what you are to ask.' This is what the Apostle says: It will come to pass that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. The blessed Paul took this testimony from the prophet because through him these times had been foretold in which everyone was to call on the name of the Lord: Whoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. And he added: How are they going to call on him in whom they have not believed? Or how will they believe in him of whom they have not heard? How are they going to hear if you don't preach to them? Or how can they preach if they are not sent? So the preachers were sent and preached Christ. With his preaching the people believed; hearing, they believed; believing, they called upon him. Since it was said with all reason and truth: How are they going to call on him in whom they have not believed?, for this very reason you have learned before what you should believe and today you have learned to call on him in whom you have believed. 2. We have already talked about daily bread, because in this life it is necessary for us to make this request. 8. Forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors. When, if not in this life, is such a request necessary? In the other we will not have debts. What are debts, but sins? You are going to be baptized and all your sins will be forgiven; not a single one will remain. If you have ever done something bad in deed, word, desire or thought, everything will be erased. Therefore, it would not be necessary for us to learn and say this petition: Forgive us our debts, if we had complete security against sin in the life after baptism. But, above all, let us fulfill the following: Just as we forgive our debtors. You, especially those who are going to obtain the cancellation of your debts, try not to hold anything against anyone in your hearts, to leave there peacefully, as free and absolved of everything; nor begin to want to take revenge on the enemies who had previously wronged you. Forgive as you are forgiven. God has insulted no one, and yet, even though he owes nothing, he forgives. If he who owes nothing to be forgiven, forgives everything, with how much greater reason should he who has been forgiven forgive? 9. Do not lead us into temptation; but deliver us from evil. Will this also be necessary for the afterlife? Needless to say, don't let us fall into temptation, where it cannot exist.

In the book of holy Job we read: Is not man's life on earth a temptation? What then is it that we ask? That? Listen. The apostle James writes: Let no one, when he is tempted, say that he is tempted by God. It refers to that evil temptation by which each person is deceived and remains subject to the devil; this is what he called temptation. There is another temptation that is also called testing; Of this it is written: The Lord your God tempts you to know if you love him. What does it mean to know? To let you know, because he already knows it 10. God does not tempt anyone with that temptation by which one is deceived and seduced, but he certainly abandons some, through a deep and hidden judgment, to it. Once he has withdrawn, the tempter knows what to do. If God abandons him, he finds no one to resist him and, immediately afterwards, he becomes the possessor. So that God does not abandon us we say: Do not lead us into temptation. Each one, says the same apostle James, is tempted, carried away and flattered by his concupiscence; then, once lust has conceived, let sin stop; sin, in turn, when it has been consummated, engenders death. What did he teach us with this? May we fight against our lusts. Through baptism, in fact, your sins will be forgiven; However, the lusts with which you will have to fight will remain, even after having been regenerated. The battle will remain within you. Do not fear any external enemy: defeat yourself, and the world is defeated. That

Therefore, retain this prayer that you must proclaim in public within eight days 2. Those of you who did not know the Symbol well, learn it, you still have time. On Saturday you will have to give it from memory in the presence of all attendees; It is the last Saturday, the one on which you are going to be baptized. Eight days from today you will have to recite by heart this prayer that you received today. 2. The prayer begins like this: Our Father who art in heaven. We have found a Father in heaven, let's see how we live on earth. He who has found such a Father must live in such a way that he is worthy of reaching his inheritance. All together we say: Our Father. How much goodness! The emperor says it and the beggar says it; Both the servant and his master say it. Both say: Our Father who art in heaven. They recognize that they are brothers when they have the same father. Let the lord not consider it unworthy of his person to have as a brother his servant, whom he wanted to have as a brother Christ the Lord. 3. We continue saying: Let your name be hallowed. Your kingdom come. The sanctification of the name of God consists of pulos suos et fideles suos hanc Orationem. Spem habemus obtinendae causae nostrae, quando talis iurisperitus nobis Preces dictavit. Assessor I'atris, sicut confessi estis, qui sedet ad dexteram Patris: ipse est advócalas noster, qui futurus est iudex noster. Inde enim venturus est iudicare vivos et mortuos. Tenete ergo et hanc Orationem, quam reddituri estis nd octo dies. Quicumque autem vestrum non bene Symbolum reddiderunt, habent spatium, teneant: quia die sabbati audientibus ómnibus qui adelunt reddituri estis, die sabbati novissimo, quo die baptizandi estis. Ad octo autem dies ab today die reddituri estis hanc Orationem, quam liodie accepistis. CAPUT II.—2. Omnium unus pater.—Cuius caput est, Pater noster, qui es in caelis. Invenimus Patrem in caelis: attendamus quemadmodum vivamus in terris. Sic enim debent vivere, qui invenit talem Patrem, ut dignus sit vinore ad eius hereditatem. Dicimus autem communiter, Pater noster. How dignified!

Hoc dicit imperator, hoc dicit mendicus; hoc dicit servus, hoc dicit dominus eius. Simul dicunt: Pater noster, qui es in caelis. Intellegunt ergo se esse fratres, quando unum habent Patrem. Sed non dedignetur fratrem habere servum suum dominus eius, quem liatrem voluit habere Dominus Christus. [394] 3. Prima et secunda petitio.—Sanctificetur nomen tuum, deci2

May we become saints, since his name has always been holy. We also wish for his kingdom to come. It will come even if we don't want it; But wishing and praying for his kingdom to come is nothing other than wishing that he would make us worthy of it, lest—God forbid—it come, but not for us. We delight in the law of God according to the inner man. Then his will is done in heaven. Mus is compared to heaven: Venial regnum tuum. Sanctificatio nominis Dei est, qua efficimur nos sancti. Also the coat? Our sustenance consists of food and drink; the coat, in the dress and on the roof. Man desires nothing more, because the Apostle says: We brought nothing into this world, nor can we take anything from it. Having sustenance and shelter, we must be happy. Let greed disappear, because nature is rich. Therefore, if it refers to daily food, since what we say can reasonably be understood like this: Give us this day our daily bread, let us not be surprised that, by naming only the bread, everything necessary is included. This is also how Joseph's invitation is understood when he said: These men will eat bread with me today. Why would they only eat bread? In truth, by saying only bread the other things were implied. In the same way, when we ask God for our daily bread, we ask him for what is necessary for our flesh on earth. But what does the Lord Jesus say? Seek first the kingdom of God, and the rest will be given to you as additions. Give us today our daily bread: it can also be perfectly understood as referring to the Eucharist, daily food. Those already baptized know very well what they receive and how good it is for them to receive this daily bread, necessary for this life. They pray for themselves, to become good and to persevere in goodness, in faith and in a holy life. This is what they desire, this is what they ask for, because if they did not persevere in the holy life they would be separated from that bread. What does it mean, therefore, Give us this day our daily bread? Let us live in such a way that we are not separated from your altar. Also the word of

God, who explains himself to you day by day and in a certain way distributes himself to you, is your daily bread. 2. Therefore, brothers, if, being evil, we have a good Father, it is so that we do not always remain in evil. No one who is evil does good. Why do men full of vanity say to me: "If you want, you can save yourself"? Heal me, Lord, and I will be healed. We were created good by him who is good. You don't look for the doctor to hurt yourself; but once you have been hurt you look for someone to heal you. Everyone who asks receives, he who seeks finds and to him who knocks it is opened. First of all, these words present a difficulty that must be resolved to the best of our ability. We know that many ask and do not receive, they seek and do not find, they knock and it is not opened to them. How then does everyone who asks receive? In effect, all of this, although it appears formulated three times and in three different forms, is reduced to a single request. Ask, seek, knock is equivalent to ask. We know this from that reasoning of the Lord who says: If you, being evil, know how to give good things to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him? He does not say: to those who seek or to those who call, but he summarized the three things in one when saying to those who ask for them. 3. With the same word, however, he could not heal the stomach of his most beloved disciple, a soul alone with his own and, for him, with his words, a brother. However, he tells him: Don't drink water for now, but pour yourself some wine because of your stomach and frequent ailments. What I have said regarding that which I wanted to warn your charity about is enough, so that you do not laugh or think badly of those who perhaps have asked and have not received, or those of you who perhaps have asked and did not receive faint, or so that those who ask and receive do not arrogantly put themselves before those who do not receive. 7. What does it mean, then, that absolutely everyone who is one of his own asks and receives, seeks and finds, knocks and it is opened to them? If this were not true, I would not say the Truth: Everyone who asks receives. What is this? Where is it located? Let's look in this same chapter; maybe we will find in it what we are looking for. In him you have it; yes, you have it in him. Let us recognize ourselves in the text that speaks of soinquit, erat ex eo quod audieratis eum infirmatum Fuisse, nam et infirmatus est usque ad proximum mortis (Phil 2,26-27). Quid magnum erat Paulo apostólo eum quoque verb sanare, nec permittere usque ad mortis proximum pervenire? Sed deus, inquit, misertus est eius, non solum autem eius, sed etiam mei, ne tristitiam super tristitiam haberem (Phil 2:27). Videtur quia volebat eum sanum fieri. Si volebat, utique et orabat, et tamen orans non impetrabat. Vix tamen quando impetravit, gratias egit, quia vel vix impetravit. Blessed Timothy consilium dat medicinale. Paraliticum vetustum verb erexit. Stomachum karissimi et unianimis et, sicut ipse appellat, germanissimi discipuli sui eodem verb sanare non potuit. Et tamen ait: Noli usque adhuc aquam bibere, sed moderate vino utere propter stomachum et fre[8i8Jquentes tuas infirmitates (1 Tim 5,23).

Quid est ergo illud, quod omnes omnino qui sunt eius petunt et accipiunt, quaerunt et inveniunt, pulsant et aperietur eis? Nisi enim esset aliquid tale, non diceret veritas: Omnis enim qui petit accipit. Quid est hoc? Ubi invenitur? In ipso capitulo quaeramus, ne forte ibi quod quaerimus inveníamus. bad guys He says, then: If you, being evil, know how to give good things to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give good things to those who ask him? He called our Father good and us evil. What to say then? The supreme God, the good Father, is the Father of the evil ones? We cannot deny that it is, even if it seems absurd. The Truth Speaks: If you, being evil—why do we contradict the Truth?—know how to give good things to your children... We give our children good things, which, however, do not make them good. If, then, we cannot give them goods that make them good, even though they are goods, what remains but to ask God for the goods that make us good? He was pointing to us when he said: Being bad. However, our Father showed himself to us as extremely good: the one who is in heaven. Don't we feel ashamed of being bad having such a Father? Would he have wanted to be the Father of bad men if he had wanted to leave them in evil, if he had wanted us to remain bad forever? If we are bad and we have a good Father, let us ask for this, let us seek this, let us call for this: may he, good, make us good so as not to have bad children. To what extent does one become good now? How far? No matter how great his progress, he must fight against ambitions, he must fight against concupiscence. No matter how much he progresses, even if someone is at peace with all the things that are inside or outside him, he will have the war in himself, he must fight the battle in himself, nor should he abandon the combat, which is contemplated by those who are willing to help those who are

strives now to crown the winner. Someday all disagreement and all quarrels will have passed—because we are nothing else; Our weakness and our quarrelsomeness do not constitute a contrary nature, but in a certain way weakness is our accustomed nature. In paradise we were not like that; Nothing of ours offered us resistance. We abandon the one with whom we lived in peace and begin to be at war with ourselves. This is our misery. It is a great thing not to be defeated in this war during your life. It is impossible for us to lack enemies in it. There will be a last life in which we will have no enemy, neither internal nor external. As the last enemy, death will be defeated. Then we will dwell happily in the house of God and praise him forever and ever. Amen.

CAPUT I.—1. Centurionis humilitas.—Audi[415]vimus, cum Evangelium legeretur, fidem nostram in humilitate laudari. Ad domum quipa ] Hic deest fragmentum, ut videtur in MA 1,711.

He said that he would go to the centurion's house to heal his son, and he replied: I am not worthy that you should come under my roof, but say a single word and he will be healed. Declaring himself unworthy, he became worthy; worthy of Christ entering not into the walls of his house, but into his heart. But he would not have said it with such faith and humility if he did not already carry in his heart the one he feared would enter his house 1. In fact, it would not be a great joy for the Lord Jesus to enter the interior of his house if he were not in his heart. He, a teacher of humility by word and example, sat at table in the house of a certain proud Pharisee, named Simon. And while he was reclining in his house, there was no place in his heart where the Son of Man would lay his head. 2. For this very reason, the Lord, as can be deduced from his words, dissuaded a certain arrogant man who wanted to follow him from being his disciple. Lord, he says, I will follow you wherever you go. And the Lord, seeing the invisible part of his heart, said to him: The foxes have dens and the birds of the air have nests, but the son of man has nowhere to lay his head. Which means: There are bends in you - this would be the foxes -; pride exists in you—this would be the birds of the sky—. But the Son of man, who is simple against duplicity and humble against pride, has nowhere to lay his head. The very reclining of the head, not its erection, is a school of humility. He dissuades him who wishes to follow him and attracts him who pe Centurionis cum se promitteret Dominus Iesus iturum, ut puerum eius sanaret, ille responderit: Non sum dignus ut sub tectum meum intres: sed tantum dic verbum, et sanabitur (Mt 8,8). Saying se indignum, praestitit dignum; non in cuius parietes, sed in cuius cor Christus intraret. Ñeque hoc diceret cum tanta fide et humilitate, nisi illum, quem timebat intrare in domum suam, corde gestaret. Nam non erat magna felicitas, si Dominus Iesus intraret in parietes eius, et non esset in pectore eius. Magister quippe humilitatis et verbo et exemplo, discubuit et in domo cuiusdam pharisaei superbi, nomine Simonis (Luke 7,36). Et cum in domo eius recumberet, non erat in corde eius ubi caput Filius hominis reclinaret. 2. Superbus a discipulatu Christi rejections. Vita animae, Deus.—Ita enim quemdam superbum, quantum intellegitur ex verbis ipsius Domini, ultro secum iré cupientem, a suo discipulatu revocavit. Sequar te, Domine, ait, quocumque ierís.

Et Dominus in eius corde invisibilia videns: Vulpes, inquit, foveas habent, et volatilia caeli nests: Filius autem hominis non habet ubi caput suum reclinet (Luke 9,57-58). Hoc est, Habitant in te insidiae sicut vulpes, habitat superbia sicut caeli volatilia: Filius autem hominis simplex contra insidas, humilis contra superbiam, non habet ubi caput suum reclinet. Et ipsa reclinatio capitis, non erectio, humilitatis magistra Idea always present when Augustine speaks of the centurion; see sermons 62 A, l (= MORIN 6); 77.12; Enarration to Psalm 38:18.

He refused to do so. In the same place he says to another: Follow me. And he: I will follow you, Lord, but allow me to go first to bury my father. He looked for a certainly pious excuse and, therefore, he became more worthy of having such an excuse rejected and the call being more firmly maintained. It was a pious thing he wanted to do, but the Master taught him what he should put first. He wanted him to be a preacher of the living word to make those who were to live alive. To fulfill that need there were others. Let the dead bury their dead, he said. When infidels bury a corpse, they are dead burying the dead. His body lost its soul; Their souls lost God. As the soul is the life of the body, so God is the life of the soul. As the body expires when the soul abandons it, so the soul expires when it abandons God. The abandonment of God is the death of the soul; The abandonment of the soul is the death of the body. The death of the body is of necessity; that of the soul depends on the will. 3. So the Lord was sitting at table in the house of a certain arrogant Pharisee. I was in his house, as I said, but not in his heart. However, he did not enter the centurion's house, but he possessed his heart. Zacchaeus, however, received the Lord into his house and into his soul. His faith manifested in humility is praised. He said: I am not worthy that you should come under my roof. And the Lord: Truly I tell you that I have not found such great faith in Israel; Israel according to the flesh, but this one was already an Israelite in the spirit. The Lord had come to carnal Israel, that is, to Est. Revocate ergo istum iré cupientem, trahit alium recusantem. Eodem quippe loco ait carem: Sequere me. Et ille: Sequar te, Domine: sed sine me primo iré et sepeliré patrem meum (Luke 9,59). Pie quidem excusavit: et ideo dignior cuius excusatio removeretur, vocatio firmaretur. Pium erat quod volebat faceré: sed docuit magister quid debenret praeponere. Volebat enim eum esse vivi verbi praedicatorem, ad fazandos victuros. Erant autem alii, per quos illa necessitas impleretur. Sine, inquit, mortuos sepeliré mortuos suos (ib., 60). Infideles corpse quando sepeliunt, mortui mortuum sepeliunt. Illius corpus animam perdidit: illorum anima Deum. Sicut enim vita corporis anima est: sic vita animae Deus. Sicut exspirat corpus, cum animam emittit: ita exspirat anima, cum Deum amittit. Deus amissus, mors animae: anima emissa, mors corporis. Mors corporis necessaria: mors animae voluntary. 3.

Centurionis fides in humilitate.—Discumbebat ergo Dominus in domo pharisaei cuiusdam superbi. In domo eius erat, ut dixi; et in pectore eius non erat. In huius vero Centurionis domum non intravit, et pectus possedit. Zacchaeus vero Dominum et domo suscepit, et animo (ib., 19,6), Huius tamen fides in humilitate laudatur. Dixit enim, Non sum dignus ut sub tectum meum intres. Et Dominus, Amen dico vobis, non inveni tantam fidem in Israel (Mt 8,8.10): secundum carnem. Nam et iste iarn Istaelites erat secundum spiritum, Venerat Dominus ad Israelem camalem,

the Jews, to first look for the sheep lost there, that is, in the town in which and from which they had taken flesh. I have not found such great faith there, says the Lord, We can measure the faith of men, but as men; He who saw the interior, he whom no one deceived, bore witness to the heart of that man when he heard the words of humility and pronounced the sentence of healing. 4. How did you reach that conclusion? I also, he says, who am a man under authority, have soldiers in my power and I say to this one: "Go", and he goes; and another: "Come," and he comes; and to my servant: "Do this," and he does it. I have power over those placed under my command and I have another power that is placed above me. «If then, he says, a man under authority, I have power to command, what can you not be able to do, whom all powers serve? This was a gentile man, for he was a centurion. The Jewish people already had soldiers from the Roman Empire at that time. There he served as a soldier, as far as possible a centurion: subject to a power and having power himself. He obeyed as a subject and governed his subjects. The Lord - this must be understood perfectly by your charity - although he was part of the Jewish people, was already announcing the future Church throughout the entire world, to which he was going to send his apostles. The Gentiles did not see it and believed; The Jews saw him and killed him. Just as the Lord did not enter the centurion's house with his body, and yet, absent in the body and present by his majesty, he healed his faith and his house, de id est, ad Iudaeos, ibi primum quaerere oves perditas, in quo populo, et de quo populo etiam cotpus assumpserat: [416] Non ibi inveni tantam fidem, ipse dicit. Possumus metiri fidem hominum, sicut homines: ille qui interiora cernebat, ille quem nemo fallebat, perhibuit testimonium cordi hominis, audiens verba humilitatis, pronuntians sententiam sanitatis. CAPUT II.—4. In centurione Gentes figuratae.—Unde autem hoc praesumpsit? Et ego, inquit, homo sum sub potestate constitutus, habens sub me milites; et áico hüic, Vade, et vadit; et alii, Veni, et venit; et servo meo, Fac hoc, et facit (ib., 9). Potestas sum quibusdam sub me positis, positus sub potestate quadam super me. Si ergo ego, inquit, homo sub potestate, iubendi habeo potestatem; quid tu possis, cui omnes serviunt potestates? Erat autem iste de Gentibus: erat quippe centurio.

Iam Iudea gens habebat militem Romani imperii. Ibi iste militem agebat, quantum agere centurio poterat; et sub potestate, et habens potestatem; subditus oboediens, subditus regens. Dominus autem (quod intendat praecipue necessario Caritas vestra), quamvis in populo Iudaico esset, iam pronuntiabat Ecclesiam toto orbe terrarumfuturem, in quam erat missuius Apostólos: ipse a Gentibus non visus et creditus, a Iudaeis visus et occisus. Quomodo enim domum huius Dominus corpore non intravit, et eius tamen fidem áteme ipsam donum absens

In the same way, the Lord himself was only bodily in the Jewish people; In the other towns he was neither born of a virgin, nor suffered the passion, nor walked, nor endured human weaknesses, nor did divine wonders. He did none of these things in the other towns, and yet what was said about him was fulfilled: The people whom I did not know served me. How, if the knowledge was lacking? After hearing, he obeyed me. The Jewish people knew him and crucified him; the world of the earth heard and believed. 5. This as a bodily absence and presence of his power in all peoples, he also signified it in that woman who had touched the hem of his dress, when he said to her, asking: Who touched me? He asks as if he were absent; As soon as you are present, heal, the crowd oppresses you, the disciples tell him, and you ask: Who touched me? As if he walked in such a way that he could not be touched by anyone, he said: Who touched me? And them: the crowd oppresses you. It is as if the Lord said: "I seek him who touches, not him who oppresses" 2. This is what his body is like in the present time, that is, the Church. It is touched by the faith of a few and oppressed by the mob of many. As his children you have already heard that the Church is the Body of Christ and, if you want, you are yourselves. The Apostle says it in many places: Through his Body, which is the Church. Also: You are the body of Christ and his members, praesens maiestate sanavit: sic et idem Dominus in solo Iudaeo populo corpore Fuit; apud alias gentes nec de virgine natus est, nec passus est, nec pedibus ambulavit, nec humano pertulit, nec divina mirabilia fecit. Nihíl horum in ceteris gentibus: et tamen de illo ímpletum est, quod dictum erat, Populus quem non cognovi, servivit mihi. How do you know if you don't know? In auditu auris oboedivit mihi (Ps 17,45). Iudaea gens cognovit, et crucifixít: orbis terrarum audivit, et credidit. CAPUT III.—5. Mulier tangens fimbriam Christi, cum eum turba premit.—Hanc quodam moda absentiam corporis sui et praesentiam virtutis suae in ómnibus Gentibus, et in illa muriere significavit, quae fimbriam vestimenti eius tetigerat, cum requirit dices: Quis me tetigit? Tanquam absens, requirit: tanquam praesens, sanat. lurbae te, inquiunt discipuli, comprimunt, et dicis: Quis me tetigit? (Le 8,43-48). Quasi enim sic ambularet, ut a nullo prorsus corpore tangeretur, ita dixit, Quis me tetigit? Et ílli, Turbae te compreprimunt.

Et tamquam diceret Dominus, Tangentem quaero, non prementem. Sic etiam nunc est corpus eius, id est, Ecclesia eius. Tangit eam fides paucorum, premit turba multorum. Corpus enim Christi esse Ecclesiam, tanquam filii eius, audistis: et si vultis, ipsi estis. Apostolus multis locis hoc dicit: Pro corpore, inquit, eius quae est Ecclesia (Col 1:24). Et iterum: Vos autem estis corpus Christi et membra (1 Cor 12:27). Si ergo corpus eius sumus, quod tune! This is the constant interpretation of the saint. golds. If, then, we are his body, what his body then suffered at the hands of the crowd, his Church suffers the same. It is oppressed by the multitude and is touched by few. The flesh oppresses her, faith touches her. Raise your eyes, then, I beseech you, you who have something to see. You have, in fact, something to see. Lift up your eyes of faith, touch the end of the hem of your garment and it will be enough for your salvation. 6. Observe that what you heard in the Gospel as future then, is now something present. Therefore, I say to you, that is, by the celebrated faith of the centurion, as strangers in the flesh, but of the family in the heart. For this reason, he said, many will come from the east and the west. Not all, but many; but, yes, from the east and the west. Through these two parts the entire globe of the earth is designated. Many will come from the east and the west and will sit at table with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven. Instead, the children of the kingdom will be cast into outer darkness. The children of the kingdom are the Jews. Why children of the kingdom? Because they received the Law, the prophets were sent to them, among them the temple and the priesthood existed, which celebrated the figures of what was going to happen. But they did not recognize the presence of the things they celebrated in figure. The children of the kingdom will go, he said, into the outer darkness. There will be crying and gnashing of teeth. We are seeing the reprobation of the Jews; We are seeing Christians called from the East and the West to a certain banquet corpus ipsius in turba patiebatur, hoc patitur Ecclesia ipsius. A turbis premitur: a paucis tangitur. Caro eam premit, fides tangit. Erect igitur oculos, obsecro vos, qui [417] habetis unde videatis. Habetis enim quod videatis. Erigite oculos fidei, tangite extremem fimbriam vestimenti, sufficiet ad salutem. 6. lmpletum nunc quod in Gospel praedicebatur. ludaei quare filii regni.—Videte quod audistis ex Gospel tune futurum, tune praesens est. Ideo, inquit, dico vobis: propter laudatam Centurionis fidem, tanquam alienigenae carne, domestici corde. Propterea, inquit, multi ab oriente et ocidente venient. Non omnes, sed multi: tamen ipsi ab oriente et occidente: istis duabus partibus totus orbis designatur. Multi ab oriente et occidente venient, et recumbent cum Abraham, et Isaac, et Iacob, in regno caelorum: filii autem regni eicientur in outer darkness (Mt 8,11-12). Filii autem regni, ludaei scilicet. Unde filii regni?

Quia Legem acceperunt, ad quos Prophetae missi sunt, apud quos templum et sacerdotium Fuit, who celebrated figures omniumfuturum. Quarum enim rerum figures celebraverunt, praesentiam non agnoverunt. Filii ergo regni ibunt, inquit, in outer darkness; ibi erit ploratus et stridor dentium (ib., 12). Videmus Iudaeos reprobates, videmus Christianos ab oriente et occidente The translation assumes in the Latin text nunc instead of tune, because the meaning requires it and it is in the Maurines. heavenly, so that they sit at the table with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, where bread will be justice and drink will be wisdom. 7. Pay attention, then, brothers. You are part of this people, predicted even then and now converted into a present reality. You are certainly one of those who have been called from the east and the west to sit at the table of the kingdom of heaven, not in the temple of idols. Be therefore the body of Christ, not oppression to the body of Christ. You have the hem of the dress to touch and heal the bleeding of blood, that is, the flow of carnal pleasures. You have, I say, the hem of the dress to touch. Consider that the Apostles are the garment that adheres to the sides of Christ by the fabric of unity. Among these Apostles was the least and last, Paul, as he himself says: I am the least of the Apostles. The last and lowest part of a dress is the border. The border is looked at with contempt, but touching it produces salvation. Until this moment we suffer hunger, thirst, we are naked and we are whipped. Is there anything behind and more despicable than this? Touch it if you suffer from blood flow; From him whose garment it is will come strength that will heal you. A border suggested itself to the touch when it now read: If anyone were to see another who has knowledge sitting at table in a temple of idols, would his conscience not be moved to eat meat sacrificed to idols, since it is weak? And because of your knowledge, brother, the weak for whom Christ died will perish. How do you think that men can be deceived with simulacra, giving the imprevocatos ad quoddam convivium caeleste, ut recumbant cum Abraham et Isaac et Iacob; ubi pañis iustitia, ubi potus sapientia. CAPUT IV.—7. Reprehenduntur in idolio convivantes cum Paganis.— Attendite ergo, fratres: hoc enim estis, ex hoc populo estis, iam tune praedicto, nunc praesentato. De his utique estis, qui vocati sunt ab oriente et occidente recumbere in regno caelorum, not in Templo idolorum. Estote ergo corpus Christi, non pressura corporis Christi. Habetis vestimenti fimbriam, quam tangatis, ut a profluvio sanguinis, id est, carnalium voluptatum fluxu sanemini. Habetis, inquam, vestimenti fimbriam, quam tangatis. Vestem putate Apostólos, sub texture unitatis adhaerentes lateribus Christi. In hic Apostolis erat tanquam fimbria minimus et novissimus Paulus: ipso diceme, Ego sum minimus Apostolorum (1 Cor 15:9). In veste novissimum et minimum, fimbria est.

Fimbria cum contemptu aspicitur: sed cum salute tangitur. Usque ad hanc horam et esurimus, et sitimus, et nudi sumus, et colaphizamur (ib., 4,11). Quid tam exttemum, quid tam contemptibile? Tange, si fluxum sanguinis pateris: exiet virtus de illo cuius vestis est, et sanabit te (cf. Mt 9,20-22). Fimbria tangenda mode proposebatur, quando ex eodem apostólo legebatur: Si enim quis viderít eum qui habet scientiam, in idolio recumbentem; nonne conscientia eius, cum sit infirma, aedifkabitur ad manducandum idolothyta? Et peribit infirmus in tua scientia, frater, propter quem Christus
The faith of the centurion and the hemorrhagic woman

sion that they are venerated by Christians? "God, they say, knows my heart." But not your brother. If you are weak, avoid a worse illness. If you are strong, take care of your brother's weakness. Those who see this are driven to other things, so that they not only want to eat there, but also want to sacrifice. Behold, brother, because of your knowledge the weak perish. Listen, brother; If you despised the weak, do you also despise the brother? Wake up. What if you sin against Christ Himself? Pay attention to what under no conditions can you despise. In this way, by sinning against your brothers and striking their weak conscience, you sin against Christ. Go, then, those who despise this, and sit at table in the temple of idols; Could they not be people who oppress instead of touch? And, once you have sat down at that table, come and fill Church 4; They will not receive salvation, but instead they will cause oppression. 8. "But I am afraid, you say, of offending my superior." Certainly fear that and you will not offend God. You who fear offending someone greater than you, take care lest there be someone even greater than the one whom you fear offending. Do not offend someone who is superior to you; It's a fair thing. This is the rule that is proposed to you. Is it not evident that he who is greater than others should in no way be offended? Consider now who is older than you. The first place is occupied by your father and mother if they are

good educators, if they nourish you with Christ. They must be listened to in everything and their every order must be obeyed. They are served in everything if they do not order anything against someone who is greater than them. "Who is, say you, greater than he who begat me?" Who created you. Man begets, God creates. Man does not know how he engenders, he does not know what he is going to engender. He who before the existence of him whom he made saw you to make you, is certainly greater than your father. The country itself be greater than your parents themselves 6, to the point that they should not be listened to when they order something against it. And if it orders something against God, it should not be obeyed either. If, then, you want to be healed, if after suffering the issue of blood, if after suffering twelve years in that disease, if after having spent all your property on doctors without having regained your health, you want to be healed once and for all, oh woman, to whom I speak as a figure of the Church!, this your father orders and your people order that. But your Lord says to you: Forget your people and your father's house. In exchange for what good, what fruit, what reward? Because the king, he says, desires your beauty. You want what he did, since to make you beautiful he loved you while you were ugly. For you, even unfaithful and ugly, he shed his blood; He restored you faithful and beautiful, loving in you what are his gifts. What did you contribute to your husband? What did you receive in dowry from your former father and people? Perhaps something other than the lusts and rags of sins? He threw away your rags, tore your dress

CAPUT V.—8. Maioris alicuius metu recumbentes in idolio. Observantia in maiorem quemque sil ordinata.—Sed timeo, inquies, ne offfendam maiorem. Time prorsus, ne offendas maiorem; et non offendis Deum. Who enim times, ne offendas maiorem, vide ne forte sit maior isto, quem times offendere. Maiorem certe noli offendere. Haec tibi regulate proponitur. Nonne manifestum est, eum minime offendendum, qui maior est ceteris? Discuss never your elders. Primi tibi sunt pater et mater: si recte educators, si in Christum nutrients; audiendi in omnibus, obtain-

perandum eis in omni iussione; contra maiorem nihil iubeant, et serviatur illis. Quis est, inquis, maior eo que me generavit? lile qui te ipsum creavit. Generat enim homo, creat Deus. Unde generat homo, nescit: quid generaturus sit, nescit. Ule qui te vidit ut faceret, antequam esset quem fecit, certe maior est patre tuo. Abiecit pannos tuos, discidit cilicium tuum: misertus est, ut ornaret; ornavit, ut amaret. CAPUT VI.—9. Scandalum fratri, peccatum est in Christum.—Quid plura, fratre;? Nonne hoc dicebamus, quia corpus Christi premebatur, et non tangebatur? Tolerabat ille prementes, quaerebat tangents. Those of you who also suffer from this disease, also touch that hem of the dress in this matter. The same Apostle says: Every soul is subject to the Higher authorities, since there is no authority that does not come from God. As many as there are, they have been established by him. Whoever resists authority, resists divine ordination. But how to behave if you order what not to do? In this case, he despises authority, out of fear of authority. Consider the hierarchy that exists in human things. If the attorney orders something, shouldn't it be done? But if he orders something contrary to the order of the proconsul, by not doing so, you do not despise the authority of the first, but choose to serve the elder. In such a case, the minor should not be angry if the elder has been preferred. If sometimes the same consul orders one thing and the emperor another, who will hesitate to serve the latter, contrasting him with the former? Therefore, if the emperor commands one thing and God another, what do you think should be done? "Pay taxes, obey me." "It is fair, but not in the temple of idols." It is prohibited in the temple. Who prohibits it? A greater authority. «Forgive me, but you threaten me with jail; he, however, with eternal fire. It is the divina Scriptura est. Observantia potestatum ordinata.—Numquid in superbiam vos erigimus, aut dicimus vobis ut adversus potestates ordinatas contemptores skis? Non hoc dicimus. Qui et hinc aegrotatis, tangite et hinc fimbriam illam vertimenti. Ipse dicit Apostolus: Omnis anima potestatibus sublimioribus subdita sit: non est enim potestas nisi a Deo. time to assume your faith and make it a shield in which all the fiery darts of the enemy can be extinguished. 14. A powerful man lies in wait for you and plots something against you; Sharpen the razor to shave your hair, not to cut your head. You have heard what I have just said in the psalm: Like a sharp razor you have devised a deception. Why did he compare the deception of a powerful evildoer to a razor? Because it only applies to what is superfluous to us. As on our body the hair seems a superfluous thing and is shaved without detriment to the flesh, in the same way consider as a superfluous thing what the angry powerful man can do to you. It takes away your poverty, does it take away your riches? Your poverty and your riches are in your heart. He could take away your wealth, he could cause you harm; perhaps he had a license to injure the body. Also this life, for those who think of the other; This life too, I say, must be considered among superfluous things. The martyrs also despised her. They did not lose their lives; On the contrary, they conquered it. 15. Be safe, brothers; Enemies are not allowed to act against the faithful beyond what is useful to be tested. Be sure of it, brothers; no one says anything else. Unload all your cares on the Lord; Throw yourself into his arms with all your being. He will not withdraw so that you fall9. He who created us gave us minatur guarantees. Hinc iam tibi assumenda est fides tua tanquam scutum, in quo possis omnia Ígnita iacula inimici exstinguere (Eph 6,16). CAPUT IX.—14. Dolus potentis mali novaculae comparatur.—Sed insidiatur contra te potens, et molitur contra te potens: acuit novaculam unde capillos radat, non unde caput incidat. Quod dixi, moda audistis in Psalm: Sicut novacula acuta fecisti dolum (Psalm 51,4). Quare dolum potentis mali novaculae comparavit? Quia non admittitur, nisi ad superflua nostra. Sicut capilli in corpore nostro tanquam superflui videntur, et sine detrimento carnis raduntur; sic quidquid potest tibi faceré iratus potens, inter superflua tua numera. Tollit paupertatem tuam: numquid tollit divitias tuas? Paupertas tua, divitiae tuae in corde tuo. Superflua tua potuit tollere, damno potuit afficere, permissus et usque ad laedendum corpus. Etiam ista vita, cogitantibus aliam vitam; ista, inquam, vita inter superflua deputanda est. Nam et martyres contempserunt illam. Non vitam perdiderunt, sed vitam acquisierunt. CAPUT X.—15.

Securitas piorum sub Dei praesidio.—Certi estote, fratres, inimicos non admitti adversus fideles, nisi quantum prodest tentandis et probandis fidelibus. Certi estote, fratres, nema aliud dicat. Omnem See in Confessions VIII 11,27 the same thought and almost identical expression: «Why do you lean on yourself, since you cannot stand? Throw yourself into Him, do not fear, for He will not turn away so that you fall; Be sure, and He will receive you and heal you.” These are reflections with which Augustine encouraged himself to give himself totally to God. even on our own hair. Truly I tell you, he affirms, all the hairs of your head are numbered. If God counts our hair, how much more will he who knows our hair count our customs! See that God does not despise even your most insignificant things. If I despised them I would not create them. In fact, he created these our hairs that are numbered. "They certainly exist, you will say, but perhaps they will perish." Hear also his word on the matter: Truly I say to you, not a single hair of your head will perish. Why do you fear a man, you, man, who are in the bosom of God? Try not to leave such a bosom; Whatever you suffer in there will be your salvation, not your perdition. Did the martyrs endure the dismemberment of their bodies, and do Christians fear the difficulties of Christian times? Whoever offends you now, does it with fear. He does not tell you clearly: "Come to the temple of the idols." He does not tell you openly: "Come to my altars, feast there." And if, after being told, you don't want to go, regret it. Make an accusation, present a complaint: "He didn't want to come to my altar, he didn't want to come to the temple that I worship." Say it. He doesn't dare, but he treacherously plots other things. Prepare your hair, because he sharpens the razor. It is going to take away what you have that is superfluous, it is going to shave off everything that you will have to leave behind. If he can, let him take away from you what must remain. What did the powerful one take from you that harmed you? What took you courage? The same as the petty thief; the same as the locksmith; putting a lot, the same as the skipper.

And even if he were allowed to kill the same body, what does he take from you but what the robber took? By calling him a "robber" I have honored him. Indeed, every robber is a man. It took away from you the same thing as a fever, a scorpion, a poisonous mushroom. All the power of those who are angry against you consists of that: doing what a mushroom does. A man eats a poisonous mushroom and dies. Look at the fragility of human life. Since you must abandon it sometime, do not fight for it so hard that you yourself are abandoned. 16. Our life is Christ. Focus your attention on it. He came to suffer, but also to be glorified; to be despised, but also to be exalted; to die, but also to be resurrected. The task awaits you, look at the reward. How do you want to reach with fine hands where you can only reach after a lot of work? You fear losing your money because you acquired it with great effort. If you didn't get that money that you ever have to lose, at least when you die, without effort, do you want to achieve eternal life without any fatigue? Get attached to it, because once you achieve it after much sweat, you will never lose it. If you have affection for what you acquired after much effort, but which you must sometime lose, how much more should those other things of perpetual duration be desired? 17. Do not believe their words nor be afraid of them. They call us enemies of their idols. May God grant us and put everything in our power, as he has put those idols that have already been broken into pieces. To your charity we say: "Do not do such things if you do not have authorization to do them." Is

If it happens that in another place heretics are punished by law because of the evil and fury of their violence, then they say that we constantly seek to cause them inconvenience in order to achieve their extermination. Furthermore, they think that we are always and everywhere on the hunt for idols and that, once found, they are destroyed no matter where. All this because God wanted laws to be promulgated against the pagans; better, in their favor, if they understood it. The same thing happens with them as with children without much judgment who are playing with the mud and getting their hands dirty. When the pedagogue arrives with a stern air, he removes the mud and puts the codex on them. In the same way, God wanted to frighten, through the princes who are subject to him, foolish and childish hearts, so that they throw the clay from their hands and do something useful. What does it mean to do something useful with your hands? Share your bread with the hungry and bring the needy homeless into your house. However, the children evade the teacher's presence, they sneak back into the mud and, when they are caught red-handed, they hide them so that he does not see them. Why do they say that we break their idols everywhere? Are there not places, visible to our eyes, where there are idols? Do we perhaps not know where they are? But we do not destroy them, because God has not given us the power. When will it be granted? When the owner of those places is a Christian. In our specific case, this is what the owner wanted it to do.
