Frange esurienti panem tuum, et egenum sine tecto induc in domum tuam (Is 58:7). Et tamen pueri evadunt ab oculis paedagogi, et redeunt ad lutum furtim; et quando inveniuntur, abscondunt manus, ne videantur): quia ergo voluit Deus, putant nos ubicumque quaerere idola; qua cum invenerimus, in omnibus locis frangere. Quare? Non ante nos sunt loca, in quibus sunt? Aut verignomus ubi sint ista? Et tamen non facimus: quia non dedit in potestatem Deus. When dat Deus in potestatem? Quando christianus erit cuius res est. Mode factum voluit cuius res est. If nollet ipsum locum I will give Ecclesiae, et tan-
The faith of the centurion and the hemorrhagic woman

possession there were no idols, I think that then Christians, with exquisite delicacy, should help that absent Christian soul who wants to give thanks to God in his land and does not want there to be anything that offends God. But in this case there is something more: he gave those places to the Church. Were there going to be idols in the very possession of the Church? Behold, brothers, what displeases the pagans. They think it's not enough that we don't remove the idols from their villages, that we don't destroy them, and they even want us to keep them in ours. We preach against idols; we eliminate them from hearts. We are persecutors of idols, we confess it. Are we, perhaps, their conservatives? I don't do it—destroy them—where I can't. I don't do it where its owner would complain; where, on the other hand, he wants it done and is grateful for it, he would be guilty if he did not do it.

The centurion prayed to the Savior for the health of his son. The Lord promised that he would come in person to save him. But he, as I said, with fervent humility and humble fervor, replied: Lord, I am not worthy that You should come under my roof. He declared himself unworthy of the Lord entering under his roof. And yet, he would not have said these words if the Lord had not already entered his heart. 1 Then he added: But say one word and my son will be healed. I know who I'm talking to; say a word, and what I desire will come true. And he added an extremely pleasant and true comparison. For I too, he says, am a man, while you are God; I am under authority, while you are above all authority; I have soldiers under my command, while you also have angels, and I say to this one "Go" and he leaves; and that "Come" and comes; and my servant “Do this” and he does it. Your servant is every creature; You only need to command, so that what you command is done. 2. And the Lord warned: Truly I say to you, I have not found such faith in Israel. You know that the Lord took flesh from Israel, from the lineage of David, of which was the Virgin Mary, who gave birth to Christ. He came to the Jews, showed them his face of flesh, his mouth of flesh turned to their ears, the form of his body appeared before their eyes. With his presence the promise made to the Jews had been fulfilled. It had been promised to the parents, it was fulfilled in the children. This centurion, however, was strange, he belonged to the Roman people, he exercised the profession of soldier there and his adventurous faith.

1. Napigantes in saeculo.—De kctione recentissima sancti Evangelii, donor Domino, alloquor vos, et in illo exhortor, ut contra tempestates et fluctus saeculi huius non dormiat fides in cordibus vestris. Non enim revera Dominus Christus mortem habuit in potestate, somnum non habuit in potestate; et forte Omnipotentem navigantem somnus pressit invitum. Christ is awake in you, your faith is awake. The Apostle says it: Through faith Christ dwells in your hearts. Therefore, Christ's dream is also a sign of some mystery 1. Navigators are the souls that pass through this world on a tree. That nave also represented the Church. Each one, in fact, is a temple of God and each one navigates in his heart. If your thoughts are right, you will not be shipwrecked. 2. You heard an insult, behold the wind. You got angry, that's the wave. As the wind blows and the waves rise, the ship is in danger, your heart is in danger, your heart fluctuates. Having heard the insult, you want to take revenge. You took revenge and, giving in to someone else's insult, you were shipwrecked. What is the cause? Because Christ sleeps in you. What does it mean: Christ sleeps in you? You forgot Christ. Awaken, therefore, to Christ, remember him, let him be awake in you: think of him. What did you want? Revenge you. Has it escaped your memory that he, when he was crucified, said: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do? Whoever slept in your heart did not want to take revenge. Wake him up, remember him. To remember him is to remember his word. To remember him is to remember his precept. If Christ is awake in you, what do you say inside? Who am I to want revenge? Who am I to make threats against a man? Maybe I will die before I take revenge. And if I leave this world inflamed with anger, yearning and thirsting for revenge, he who did not want to take revenge will not receive me. He will not receive me who said: Give and it will be given to you, forgive and you will be watched fides vestra. Apostolus dicit: Habitare Christum per fidem in cordibus vestris (Eph 3, 17). Ergo et somnus Christi signum est sacramenti. Navigantes sunt animae in ligno saeculum passersby. Etiam navis illa Ecclesiam figurabat. Et singuli quippe templa sunt Dei, et unusquisque in corde suo navigat: nec facit naufragium, si bona cogitat. 2. Excitandus Christus inter irae tempestates.—Audisti convicium, ventus est: iratus es, fluctus est. Vento igitur fiante, fluctu surging, periclitatur navis, periclitatur cor tuum, fluctuat cor tuum. Audito conviction vindican desideras: et ecce vindicatus es, et malo alieno cedens, fecisti naufragium. Et quare hoc? Quia dormit in te Christus. Quid est, dormit in te Christus? Oblitus is Christum. Excita ergo Christum, remembere Christum, evigilet in te Christus: consider illum. Why are you volleying? Vindicari.

Excidit tibi, quia ipse cum crucifigeretur dixit: Pater, ignosce Mis, quia nesciunt quid faciunt? (Le 23,34). Who slept in corde tuo, noluit vindicari. Excite illum, collect illum. Memory ipsius, verbum ipsius: memory ipsius, iussio ipsius. And you say apud te, si vigilat in te Christus: Qualis ego homo, qui voló vindicari? Qui sum ego, qui in hominem exsero comminationes? Morior forte antequam vindicer. will forgive Therefore, I will calm my anger and return to the stillness of my heart. Christ gave orders to the sea and prosperity occurred. 3. Contemplate how doves enjoy being in society: everywhere they fly together, they feed together, they do not want to be alone, they enjoy communion, they maintain charity, they murmur moans of love, they give birth to their children with kisses. When pigeons, as we frequently observe, dispute among themselves over their niches, they are in a sense waging a peaceful dispute. Do they separate after having disputed? They fly together, they feed together and their disputes are peaceful. See the dispute of the pigeons. Look at the dispute, but note that it is a dispute between doves, not wolves. Then he added: Yero, do not consider him an enemy, but correct him like a brother. The dove loves even when it disputes; The wolf hates even when he flatters. Possessing, therefore, simplicity

Sollemnitas martyrum, dilectissimi, qua passionis eorum memoriam celebramus, ad imitandum nobis proponitur, ut, si quid forte durae temptationis acciderit, usque in finem perseveremus, ut salvi esse possimus, Saint Augustine refers to the traditional custom then of celebrating funeral banquets, either in honor of deceased relatives, now in honor of the martyrs, together to his memories. It was not unusual for such meals to end in drunkenness. All this led Augustine to prohibit them in Hippo, as had already happened in other parts of the Catholic world, such as in Milan, by the work of Saint Ambrose (Confessions VI, 2,2). Augustine's opinion and behavior in this regard can be read in Letters 22 and 29. Regarding the same, you can see in F. VAN DER MEER, Saint Augustine, Shepherd of Souls, the chapter: "Funeral Banquets" p.633ff. The Latin term coronator appears for the first time in Augustine. We will also find it in sermon 116,7.

The Lord wanted it to remain hidden when it was going to take place, so that men always wait prepared for what they do not know when it is going to come. But, whether it is near or far away, as I said, the end of this temporal world, the end of each individual man, by which he is forced to pass from this life to another adequate to his merits, thinking about the brevity of this our mortality, cannot be far away. Each of us must prepare for when our end comes. The last day, in fact, will not bring any harm to those who, thinking that each day is the last for them, live in a way of dying peacefully; to him who dies day by day so as not to die eternally. Thinking of these things, how the holy martyrs heard the word of the Lord saying: Behold, I am sending you out like sheep in the midst of wolves! How firmly they had been strengthened so that they should not be afraid of this! Were those who then heard these words of the Lord going to remain here until the consummation of the world? These words: I am with you until the consummation of the world, not only did they hear them, we also heard them. And if we did not hear them then in our science, we heard them in their prescience. Therefore, to live safely like sheep in the midst of wolves, let us keep the commandments of the one who exhorts us to be simple as doves and clever as serpents. Simple as doves: let us harm no one; cunning as snakes: let us take care that no one harms us. But you won't be able to take precautions to avoid being harmed unless you know where you can be harmed. There are those who fight with great resistance for temporary things. CAPUT I. — 1. Timore timor pellendus.—Admonent nos eloquia divina, quae lecta sunt, timendo non timere, et non timendo timere. Advertistis, cum [427] sanctum Evangelium legeretur. Dominum Deum nostrum antequam pro nobis moieretur, firmos nos esse voluisse: sed admonendo ne timeremus, et admonendo ut timeremus. Ait enim: Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt, animam autem non possunt occidere

He feared: Vero fear him, he said, who can kill both soul and body in Gehenna. Therefore, let us fear so as not to fear. It seems that fear corresponds to cowardice; Fear seems to be typical of the weak, not the strong. But see what the Scripture says: The fear of the Lord is the hope of strength. Let us fear so as not to fear, that is, let us fear prudently, so as not to fear fruitlessly. The holy martyrs, on whose solemnity this Gospel was recited, feared did not fear: fearing God, they disdained men. 2. What has man to fear from men? And what can a man terrify another man with? It terrifies him by saying: I will kill you. And he is not afraid that perhaps he will die first, while he threatens. He says "I'll kill you"; but who says it and to whom does it say it? I listen to two, one who threatens and another who fears; one of them is powerful and the other weak, but both are mortal. Why does swollen power exceed in honor, which in the flesh is equal weakness? He who does not fear death safely intimates death. But, if you fear that death with which you threaten, reflect and compare yourself with the one you threaten. Discover in him a common condition; and together with him ask the Lord for mercy. Because he is a man and he threatens a man, a creature to a creature; the one that puffs up before its Creator and the other that flees towards the Creator. 3. Let the mighty martyr therefore say, as a man standing before another man: "I am not afraid, because I am afraid." You will not execute (Mt 10,28). Ecce ubi monuit ne timeremus. Videte ubi monuerit ut timeremus. Sed eum, inquit, tímete, qui potestatem habet et corpus et animam occidere in gehenna (ib.). Ergo timeamus, ut non timeamus. Timor videtur ad ignaviam pertinere: timor infirmorum videtur esse, non fortium. Sed videte quid ait Scriptura: Timor Domini spes fortitudinis (Prov 14:26). Timeamus, ne timeamus: hoc est, prudenter timeamus, ne inaniter timeamus. Martyres sancti, propter quorum solemnitatem hoc ex Evangelio recitatum est, timendo non timuerunt: quia Deum timendo, nomines contempserunt. 2. Homini ab homine nil metuendum.—Quid enim ab hominibus homini metuendum est? Et quid est unde alterum terreat, homo hominem? Terret, et dicit: Occido te; et non timet, ne cum minatur, prius moriatur. West, worried. What did you say? cui dicit? Audio duos: unum terrentem, alterum metuentem; quorum unus est potens, alter infirmus, be both mortal. Quid se ergo extendit in honore inflatior potestas, in carne aequalis infirmitas?

Securus minetur mortem, qui non timet mortem. Si vero unde terret, timet; attendat se, et ei cui minatur comparet se. Inveniat in eo cui minatur, parem conditionem; et a Domino simul cum illo petat miserationem. Homo est enim, et homini minatur, creatura creaturae: sed una innata sub Creatore, altera fugiens ad Creatorem. CAPUT I I. — 3. Therefore, the invisible substance, that is, the soul that raised the prostrate earth from the earth, does not fear when you strike the earth. You can hurt the dwelling, but will you hurt the inhabitant? This one is bound, and if you break his bond, he flees and will be crowned in secret. Why threaten, if you can do nothing to the soul? By the merit of the soul, to which you can do nothing, that body to which you can harm will be resurrected. By merit of the soul, the flesh will also be resurrected. This will be returned to its inhabitant, not to fall, but to remain. I am repeating the words of the martyr: "Look, not even for the sake of the flesh do I fear your threats." The flesh depends on authorization, but even the hairs on the head are counted for the Creator. Why should I fear losing my flesh, since I do not lose a hair? How will he not attend to my flesh who thus knows the most vile thing that I have? The body itself, which can be wounded and killed, will be ashes for some time, and in eternity it will be immortal. And who will it be for? To whom will that dead, bruised, destroyed body be returned for eternal life? Who will it be returned to? To him who was not afraid to give his life, and is not afraid when his flesh is killed.

4. Brothers, the soul is presented as immortal, and is immortal in its own way: because it is a certain life, which with its presence can vivify the flesh, since the flesh lives through the soul. That life cannot die and that is why the soul is immortal. And why did I say "according to his own way"? Hear why. There is a certain authentic immortality, immortality that is total immutability: the Apostle says of it, speaking of God: He alone has immortality, and dwells in an inaccessible light; whom no man has seen, nor can see; to him honor and glory forever and ever. Amen. If only God possesses immortality, the soul is certainly mortal. That is why I said that the soul is immortal in its own way. In fact, he cannot die. Understand your charity and there will be no question left. I dare say that the soul can die and can be killed. Without a doubt it is immortal, but I dare say that it is immortal and that it can be killed; and that is why I said that it has a certain immortality, that is, not the total immutability that is proper to God alone, of whom it was said: He alone has immortality. For if the soul cannot be killed, how did the Lord Himself, threatening us, say: Fear him who has the power to kill the soul and the body in Gehenna. 5. I have confirmed the problem, but instead of resolving it I have not resolved it. I have shown that the soul can be killed.

If you already have some taste, if you are already intrigued by something, if you have already learned to warm yourself with a holy desire, weigh it against many other things, install the scales of justice, put in a saucer the gold, the silver, the precious stones, honors, dignities, powers, nobility, human praises (when will I mention them all?), place the whole world; See if you have any contemplation, see if you can place those two realities, even if only for the exam: the whole world, and the Creator of the world. 4. If he had interrupted the things he was dealing with and gone out to meet her, he would have built up in her heart a human affection, not a divine one. So that you would not listen to your mother when she withdrew you from the kingdom of heaven, he even disdained good Mary for talking about the kingdom of heaven. If Saint Mary, wanting to see Christ, is disdained, what mother will be heard when she prevents seeing Christ? Whoever does the will of the one who sent me is a brother, sister and mother to me. You have how to become a brother of Christ; loves with him the same inheritance. You have a way to become the mother of Christ, if you conceive in your heart what she conceived in her womb. In naming these needs, human feeling falls short; In carnal propagation no one can be the brother and mother of a man. Who doesn't know that this is not possible? But charity has no such limits. Without a doubt, the Church is the wife of Christ, but it is also the bride of Christ. We know with what mystery, in the first prophecy of the first man, it was said: there will be two in one flesh. We know how the Apostle explains this by saying: but I apply it to Christ and the Church. Therefore, if the Church is, without a doubt, the wife of Christ, it can be the mother of Christ although in another way, with another healthy explanation. If it can be said of anyone: He who does the will of him who sent me is brother, sister and mother, how much more can that be said of the universal Church, which in its catechumens conceives every day the members of Christ, and of those infidels gives members of Christ to the light? For you, said the Apostle, are the body and members of Christ. to you

I ask, members of Christ: Who gave birth to you? You will answer: "The mother Church." For how can the Church not be the mother of Christ, which gives birth to the members of Christ? This is the house in which he who asked for only one thing preferred to live. How will he not renounce his wife who desires to dwell in the wife of Christ? How will he who wants to dwell in the mother of Christ not disdain the mother? How will he not disdain the father who wants to have the Father of Christ as his father? Parents do not get irritated. They are highly esteemed when only God is put before them. If they do not want God to come before them, what do they want or what do they demand? Let's listen to them. I think they will not dare to tell us: Prefer us to God! They don't say it. Nobody says that, not even a crazy person. He does not say it to his son, not even the one who says in his heart: There is no God. In no way will the father or mother dare to say that: that they are preferred to God. I'm not saying that they should be put before them, but not even that they should be compared. What do they say then? God has told you. What has God told me? Honor your father and mother. I admit it, God told me so. Don't get irritated when, in front of you, I only prefer the one who said it. I love, I love decisively and I love you too. But the one who taught me to love you is better than you. It is enough that you do not turn me against him and that you love with me the one who taught me to love you, but not more than him. 8. If ergo sine dubio ecclesia is coniunx Christi, Potest tamen esse alio quodam moda, alio quodam sana intellectu ecclesia mater Christi. Si enim de una qualibet dici potuit: Qui facit uoluntatem eius qui misit me, frater, sóror, mater est, quanto magis hoc de uniuersa ecclesia dici potest, quae cotidie in cathecumenis concipit membra Christi et de infidelibus parit membra Christi? membra Christi (1 Cor 12:27). Interrogo uos, o membra Christi: Quae uos peperit? Respondetis: Mater ecclesia. Quomodo non est mater ecclesia Christi quae parit membra Christi? Multum enim eis defertur quibus solus Deus praefertur. Aut si nec Deum sibi uolunt praeferri quid sibi uolunt, quid suadent? Audiamus eos. Puto quod non audeant dicere nobis: Praefer nos Deo. Non dicunt. Nemo hoc dicit [nec] insanus. Non dicit hoc filio suo nec ille qui dicit in corde suo: Non est Deus (Ps 13,1). Nullo igitur moda uel pater uel mater hoc dicere audebit ut praeferatur Deo. charity. Love orderly so that you may be orderly. Distribute their weights and importance to things. Say to the wife: "If I did not love you, I would not have married you." Say to the children: "If I did not love you, I would not have begotten and educated you." But what do you want? Do you want to divert a martyr who is marching towards Christ and not to abandon you, and do you envy the crown of him whom you love? Correspond. He loves you, you love him too. Why should you hate him when he loves you? Look, if you deny Christ, you are condemned. See what you did. Would you like an earthly judge to condemn the one you love? If you wanted him, you wouldn't love him. And since you love him, you do not want him to be condemned by the earthly judge. If he denies Christ, he is not condemned on earth, but he is condemned by him who made heaven and earth. Why are you not afraid that the one you love will be condemned by a superior judge? The earthly judge is cruel to the point of death; he is cruel to the point of death; But the superior judge is going to me. Clamat tibi [46] sponsa eius: Ordinate in me caritatem (Song 2,4). Ama ordinate, ut sis ordinatus. Sua rebus et pondera et momenta distribue. Ama patrem et matrem, sed habes quod plus ames quam patrem et matrem. If illos plus amaueris, damnaberis, and if illos non amaueris, damnaberis. Deferamus honorem parentibus, sed eis creatorem nostrum quem plus diligimus praeferamus et timendo et amando et obtemperando et honorando et credendo et desiderando. Qui diligit patrem aut matrem plus quam me non est me dignus. Paululum ergo de medio patents non spreti sed ordinate honorati discedant. 9. Uxor est cuiquam; filii sunt cuiquam. Clamant: Love us. Pergentem martyrem ad Christum, non ut uos deserat, reuocare uultis, et ei quem diligitis coronam inuidetis? Reddit uicem. Amat uos, amate eum et uos.

Quare non eum quem diligitis damnari a maiori iudice formidatis? Terrenus iudex usque ad mortem saeuit, Saeuit iste usque ad mortem; post Ule et ultra mortem.

beyond death! What do you do when you cause the ruin of the one you love? From what do you separate him whom you love? He will go to Gehenna and will have no crown. And that is love! It is easy to satisfy your children. But the wife urges: Don't abandon me, she says. You will leave and I will be a widow. God united us, do not separate us. Respond to such voices. But that should not scare you, so that you separate yourself from God by wanting to be united with your wife. If you have to fear separation from your wife, how much more from the Creator? 11. Therefore, let no one love father, mother, children, wife, more than Christ. Those same things that are loved rightly, that are loved piously, in which it is sinful if they are not loved, no one loves them more than Christ, no one loves them as Christ. If you love like this, it will be said that you love according to the way of love, not according to the intensity. What does it mean according to the mode of love, not according to the intensity? It means: not carnally, but spiritually. Don't love like that, that is, with the same intensity and equality. Because it is a sin not only to love anyone more than Christ, but also not to love Christ more than anyone else. I love no one more, he says; You don't sin, but I have to hear the second part. How much do you love? You answer: as much as I love my parents, my wife, my children, I love Christ just as much. You still sin. If you would sin by preferring, you sin by comparing. Does it seem right to you to love Christ as much as you love your father, your mother, your wife? Is it right for you to equate the creature with the Creator? Is it straight? Where is that cry: Order love in me? Neither your father, nor your mother, nor your children have died for you. If an accident happens to you, they want you to live, but they want more to survive you. If we were to say to the father: You or your son must die, do you think we will find anyone who will say: "I, rather than my son?" Will we find such a father, such an old man, who would not rather choose a life that will end soon than to give it up for his son? There are only a few days left for an old man, a decrepit, tired, bent old man, and he doesn't want to give up those few days.

the many of his son. Under the sadness of old age he is close to the grave, and out of desire for light he chooses to see himself alone rather than dead. And what will that light be after his son's funeral? How annoying, how mournful, how bitter! And yet, the light is loved and the son is buried. 12. Christ loved you before you existed, he created you; before creating the world he predestined you; After he was created, he nourished you through your father and mother. Because what your parents give you is not theirs. He loved you, created you, nurtured you, gave himself for you, heard insults for you, accepted wounds for you, redeemed you with his blood. Don't you tremble? and you say: What shall I return to the Lord for all that he gave me? And what will you return to the Lord for everything he gave you? Listen to what he tells you: He who loves his father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. Listen to the one who speaks, fear the one who intimates, love the one who promises. What did you give back to the Lord for everything he gave you? Suppose you already returned it. And what did you return? Did you give him health, like he gave it to you? Did you introduce him to eternal life, as he introduced you? Did you create him, as he created you? Did you make him Lord, as he made you a man? What did you give back to him but things that revert to you? If you think true, you did not give him, but you provided for yourself. And you didn't even have that from yourself. Well, what do you have that you haven't received? Why can't you find something to give to the Lord? Give him back yourself, give him back what he did. Give him back yourself, not your things, his creature, not your iniquity.

[47] 11. Nemo ergo diligat plus quam Chtistum patrem, matrem, filios, uxorem. Ea ipsa quae recte diliguntur, quae pie diliguntur, in quíbus peccatum est si non diligantur, nemo diligat plus quam Christum, nemo diligat sicut Christum. Si diligit sic, secundum modum dilectionis, non secundum mensuram dicatur. Quid est secundum modum dilectionis, non secundum mensuram diligas sic? Hoc est non carnaliter, sed spiritaliter. Sed non diligas sic, hoc est tantum et aequaliter. Non solum enim peccatum est diligere aliquem plus quam Christum, sed peccatum est non plus quam aliquem diligere Christum. Non, inquit, plus diligo. Ecce non sins. Be aliud audiam. Quantum diligis? You answer: Tantum diligo quantum patents, quantum coniungem, quantum filios, tantum Christum. Adhuc sins. Qui peccares praeferendo, peccas conferendo. Rectum tibi uidetur ut tantum a te diligatur Christus quantum pater, mater, uxor? Tibi rectum est u t aeques creaturam creatori? Rectum est? Ubi est quod clamat: Ordinate in me caritatem? (Song 2,4). Non est pro te mortuus pater tuus, non mater tua, non filii tui. Si tibi periculum incurrat, uolunt te uiuere, sed plus tibi superuiuere. Si contingat ut dicatur patri: Aut morieris, aut filius tuus, putas inuenitur quisquam qui dicat: Ego potius quam filius meus? Putamusne talis pater, talis senex qui non potius eligat uitam etiam cyto finiendam quam pro filio impendendam? Pauci dies illi restant homini seni, homini decrepito, homini lasso, homini incuruo, et eosdem paucos dies non facile uult erogare

pro filii sui pluribus diebus. Iam pondere senectutis uicinus est sepulturae, desiderio lucis chose orbari quam morí. Qualis lux erit post filii funus? Quam insuauis, quam luctuosa, quam amara? Tamen lux amatur, filius sepelitur. 12. Christus dilexit te antequam esses; creauit you; ante constitutionem mundí praedestinauit te; iam creatum per patrem et matrem nutriuit te. Non enim parentes qui tibi tradunt de suo fecerunt. Dilexit te, creauit te, nutriuit te, tradidit semetipsum pro te, opprobia audiuit pro te, uulnera suscepit pro te, sanguine suo redemit te. Audi eum dicentem: Qui dilexit patrem aut matrem plus quam me, non est me dignus (Mt 10,37). Audi dicentem, time terrentem, ama promittentem. Quid retribuisti Domino pro omnibus quae retribuit tibi? Ecce iam retribuisti. What did you pay? Saluum eum fecisti quemadmodum te ipse? In aeternam uitam introduxisti sicut te ipse? Creasti sicut te ipse? Tu eum dominum fecisti sicut te ipse hominem fecit? Quid retribuisti nisi quod ad te rediret? Si uerum cogites, non illi tribuisti, sed tibi praestitisti. Nec tamen et hoc a te ipso habuisti. Have pity on your soul, pleasing God. You want God to please you and you do not want to please God yourself, because you are such that God cannot please you. For it will only please you if you favor your iniquities! You thought, he says, an iniquity: that I am like you. Have pity on your soul, pleasing God. It is not good that, being perverse, you please God. Correct yourself. Don't try to bend God. Please God and God will please you. Be upright, you, lest you desire perversity, not only for yourself, but also for God. You lie idle, and you compose a God according to your desires. You say: If God did this! Oh, if only I did! He will do nothing but good. But God displeases the wicked. How good is the God of Israel to the upright in heart. Let us therefore ask God, brothers, for the one thing. When I say it to you, I include myself. Let us all ask for the one thing. May we all hear it from each other. Let us ask the Lord for the one thing, let us claim this: to live in the house of the Lord all the days of our lives. All those days are an eternal day. When you hear about all the days of my life, do not fear that such days will end. Those days never really end, since even while they last we do not desire the human day. Not a single day remains with us; Not a single day remains with us, everyone flees. Before

come, go. When we stop to talk about this day, he has already fled. We do not even remember the time we are in. She also flees, another one comes who will not stop either, but will also flee. 3. We have heard a true and good testimony both from John about Christ and from Christ about John. What does it mean then that John sent his disciples to him, locked up in prison and already close to death, and said to the same disciples: Go and ask him: Are you the one who is to come or are we waiting for another? Is that what all the praise boils down to? What do you say, Juan? Who are you talking to? What are you talking about? You speak to the judge and you speak like a town crier. You extended your finger, you showed it, you said: Behold the Lamb of God, behold the one who takes away the sins of the world. You said: We all receive from his fullness. You said: I am not worthy to untie the thong of his shoes. And now you say: Are you the one who comes or are we waiting for someone else? Isn't it the same? And who are you? Are you not its precursor? Are you not he of whom it was prophesied: Behold, I send my angel before your face, and he will prepare your way? How do you prepare the way if you stray? So the disciples of John arrived and the Lord said to them: Go and tell John: the blind see, the deaf hear, the lame walk, the lepers are healed, the dead are raised, the poor are evangelized. And you ask if it's me? My words, he says, are my works. Go and answer. And they left. So that no one may say: John was once good, but the Spirit of God abandoned him; That is why he said this when the disciples whom John had sent left. After they had left, Christ praised John.

4. What does this dark problem mean then? May the sun in which that candle was lit shine upon us. Thus the solution is an obvious solution. John had his own disciples; he was not separated, but he was a prepared witness. It was fitting, therefore, that he should bear witness to Christ before them, who also gathered disciples: they might feel jealous if they could not see. And since John's disciples esteemed their teacher John so much, they heard John's testimony about Christ and marveled; That is why, before dying, he wanted him to confirm them. No doubt they said within themselves: this man says such great things about himself, but he does not say them about himself. Go and tell him, not because I doubt, but so that you may be instructed. Go and tell him; what I usually say, listen to him; You have heard the crier, now hear the judge confirm. Go and tell him: Are you the one who comes or are we waiting for another? They went and said it; for them, not for Juan. And for them Christ said: The blind see, the deaf hear, lepers are healed, the dead are resurrected, the poor are evangelized. You see me, recognize me. You see the facts, recognize the doer. And blessed is he who will not be scandalized by me. And I mean you, not Juan. Therefore, so that we could see that he was not referring to Juan, he said: When they had left, he began to tell the crowds about Juan. And the truthful, the Truth, sang his true praises. 5. I think that the difficulty has been sufficiently resolved. It is enough, then, to have prolonged the speech until the solution.

Theme: The kingdom revealed to the little ones (Mt 11:25; Luke 10:21). Location: Unknown. Date: After the year 400. 1. When reading the holy Gospel we have heard that the Lord Jesus exulted in the Spirit and said: I confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you hid this from the wise and prudent and revealed it to the little ones. Let us piously consider what comes first. We see, first of all, that when Scripture says confession, we must not always assume the voice of a sinner. It was of the greatest importance to say this to admonish your charity. Because, as soon as that word sounded in the mouth, habete pauperes: facite qui nondum fecistis: credite, non perditis; immo hoc solum perditis, quod non fertís ad quadrigam. Iam reddendum est pauperibus quod obtulistis, qui obtulistis: et multum minus habemus ad summam quam soletis offerre: excutite pigritiam. Ego factus sum mendicus mendicorum: quid ad me? CAPUT I. — 1. Confessio duplex est, peccatoris et laudatoris. Tundere pectus quid.—Sanctum Evangelium cum legeretur, audivimus exsultasse Dominum lesum in Spiritu, et dixisse: Confiteor tibi, Pater, Domine caeli et terrae, quia abscondisti haec a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis (Mt 11,25). Hucusque interim verba Domini, si digne, si diligenter, si quod primum est, pieconsiderus; invenimus primitus, non semper cum in Scripturis legimus confessionem, I shall owe us

of the reader, the murmur of the blows of your chest was followed, while what the Lord said was heard: I confess to you, Father. As soon as I confess, you hit your chest. And what is beating the chest if not to indicate that sin beats in the chest, and that the hidden one must be punished with an obvious blow? Why did you do that if not because you heard I confess to you, Father? I confess, you have heard, but you have not noticed who confesses. So repair now. If Christ said I confess, and all sin is far from him, such a word is not exclusive to the sinner, but also belongs to the exalter 2. We confess, then, either when we praise God or when we accuse ourselves. Both confessions are pious, either when you rebuke yourself who is not without sin, or when you praise him who cannot have sin. 2. If we think well, your rebuke is his praise. Well, why do you already confess in the accusation of your sin? Why do you confess, accusing yourself, if not because you were dead and you are alive? Thus says the Scripture: Confession perishes in the dead, as if it did not exist. If confession perishes in the dead, he who confesses lives, and if he confesses sin, he undoubtedly revived from death. And if the confessor of sin revived from the dead, who raised him? No dead person is resurrected from himself. Only those who did not die when their flesh died could be resurrected. Thus he resurrected what had died. He woke up, then, intellegere vocem peccatoris. Máxime autem hoc cerca In hoc ipso quod sonuit, Confiteor, pectora tutudistis. Tundere autem pectus quid est, nisi arguere quod latet in pectore, et evidenti pulsu oceultum punishre peccatum? Quare hoc fecistis, nisi quia audistis: Confiteor tibí, Pater? Confiteor, audístis: qui confitetur, non attendistis. Never warn yourself. Yes, Confiteor, Christus dixit, a quo longe est omne peccatum: non solius est pecatoris, sed etiam aliquando laudatoris. Confitemur ergo, sive laudantes Deum, sive aecusantes nos ipsos. Pia est utraque confessio, sive cum te reprehendis, qui non est sine peccato; sive cum illum laudas, qui non potest habere peccatum. 2. Peccatoris confessio etiam ipsa est Dei laudatio. Lazari suscitatio, peccatoris resurgentis figura.—Si autem bene cogitemus, reprehensio tua, laus ipsius est.

Quare enim iam confectioners in aecusatíone peccati tui? in aecusatione tui ipsius quare confiteris, nisi quia ex mortuo vivus factus es? Scriptura quippe ait: A mortuo, quasi qui non sit, perit confessio (Eccli 17 [434] 26). Si perit a mortuo confessio, qui confitetur vivit et si peccatum confitetur, utique a morte revixit. Si peccati confessor revixit a morte, quis eum suscitavit? Nullus mortuus est sui ipsius suscitator. Ule se potuit suscitare, qui mortua carne non mortuus est. Etenim hoc suscitavit quod mortuum fuet. Ule se suscitavit, qui vivebat in se, in

the one who lived in himself and had died in his flesh to resurrect it. The Father alone did not raise the Son, of whom the Apostle says: Therefore God exalted him. The Lord also resurrected himself, that is, his body, and therefore says: Tear down this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. The sinner, for his part, is a dead person, especially the one who is oppressed by the mass of custom and is like a buried Lazarus. It was little to be dead and also to be buried. He who is oppressed by the weight of bad custom, of bad life, that is, of earthly lusts, sees already realized in himself what a psalm unfortunately says: The fool said in his heart: There is no God. It was precisely said of him: In the dead, as if he did not exist, confession perishes. Who resurrected him but he who removed the stone and exclaimed: Lazarus, come out!? And what is going outside if not manifesting what was hidden? Whoever confesses goes outside, and he could not go outside if he did not live, and he would not live if he had not been resurrected. Then, in confession, to accuse oneself is to praise God. 3. Perhaps someone will say: What good is the Church if the confessor comes out resurrected by the voice of the Lord? What does it profit him who confesses the Church, to which the Lord said: Whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven? Observe Lazarus himself when he comes out with his bonds. He already lived confessing, but he still did not walk free, constrained by the same bonds. What then does the Church do, to which it was said: What you loose flesh autem sua suscitada mortuus erat. Non enim Pater solus Filium suscitavit, de quo dictum est ab Apostólo: Propter quod et Deus eum exdtavit (Phil 2,9); sed etiam Dominus se ipsum, id est, corpus suum; unde dicit: Solvite templum hoc, et in triduo suscitabo illud (lo 2,19). Mortuus is autem peccator, máxime ille quem moles consuetudinis premit, quasi sepultas est Lazarus. Parum enim erat, quia mortuus; etiam sepultus. Ioannes non lumen, sed luzern.—Sic et Ioannes amicus sponsi, Christus putabatur, lumen putabatur. Non erat Ule lumen; sed ut testimonium perbiberet de lumine. Quod autem erat lumen? Erat lumen verum. OF CHAPTER EVANGELII SECUNDUM MATTHAEUM UBI AIT DOMINUS: «CONFÍTEOR TIBÍ PATER DOMINE CAELI ET TERRAE. QUIA ABSCONDISTI HAEC A SAPIENTIBUS ET PRUDENTIBUS. ET REVELASTI EA PARVULIS. ITA PATER QUONIAM SIC PLACITUM EST CORAM TE» (Mt 11,25)

1. Istam sancti evangelii lectionem etiam hesterno dominico die, sicut meministis, audivimus: sed hodie ut legeretur nos voluimus, propterea quia herí multitudo constipata etiam angustiis aliquanto inquietior
LXVIII The kingdom revealed to the little ones

voice is only enough with great silence. Today, with the help of the Lord, I plan to discuss what I omitted yesterday and treat it according to the measure of my smallness: it is not that yesterday the crowd bothered me but because I could not satisfy them due to the weakness of my voice. Now, therefore, with your attention help me before the Lord our God, so that he may give me what I have to say and that you may hear it healthily. 2. The Son of God, Only Begotten of the Father, God always, man for us, done what he did—made man who made man—says to the Father: I confess you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth. It is for me, Father, the Lord of heaven and earth, Father of him by whom everything was created. Because the entire creation is contained in these two words: when we say heaven and earth. That is why the first book of God's Scripture says: In the beginning God made heaven and earth; and help also comes to me from the Lord, who made heaven and earth. With the name of heaven we understand everything that is in the sky, and with the name of earth we understand everything that is in it; Thus, in naming these two parts of creation, nothing of it is omitted. Everything is in one part or another. The Son says to the Father: I confess; and thus teaches us that confession is due to God and not only in sins. Almost always, when the Scriptures advance: Confess the Lord, many of the listeners beat their chest; It seems to them that confession can only mean that which penitents exercise when confessing their pecavoci nostrae non ibat facilitatem; quoniam non est talis ut sufficiat nisi magno silentio. Proinde hodie adiuvante domino quod heri praetermisimus discussiendum atbitror, ​​et pro nostri moduli infírmitate tractandum: non quia hoc hesterno die multitudini invidimus, sed quia infírmitate vocis multitudini non sufficimus. Nunc ergo intentione vestra adiuvate me apud dominum deum nosttum, quo nobis donet quod dicamus, et vobis ut salubriter auditatis. 2. Filius dei, unigenitus Patri, deus semper, homo propter nos, factus quod fecit—homo enim factus est, qui hominem fecit—dicit ad Patrem: confiteor tibi, Pater, domine caeli et terrae (Mt 11:25). Mihi Pater: domine caeli et terrae, Pater eius per quem facta sunt omnia. Omnis quippe creatura his duobus [502] vocabulis breviter explicatur, cum dicitur caelum et terra; ideo primus scripturae dei liber, in principle, inquit, fecit deus caelum et terram (Gen 1,1) et, auxilium meum a domino, qui fecit caelum et terram (Ps 120,2).

Sed nomine caeli intellegitur quicquid ín cáelo est, nomine terrae intellegitur quicquid in tetra est; ita duabus his creaturae partibus nominatis, nihil creaturarum praetermittitur: quoniam híc est, aut ibi est. Dicit autem Filius Patri, confiteor; et admonet nos, confessionem non in solis peccatis debeni deo. Plerumque enim cum audetur in scripturis, confitemini domino, multi qui audiunt This invitation to remain silent is not uncommon in Augustinian sermons. See Supplementary Note 49: The Health of Augustine vol. VII p.760.

two, expecting from God their merits, not those that they had to suffer, but those that he mercifully deigns to grant. But if praise did not imply confession, I would not say: I confess to you, Father, who had no sin to confess. It is also said in a certain book of Scripture: Confess the Lord and this you will say in confession: all the works of the Lord are very good. Here too we have confession of praise, not guilt. Therefore when you praise God, you confess God; and when you accuse your sins before God, you confess to God. And all this corresponds to the praise of the Creator, since you praise Him, since you accuse yourself. 3. No one doubts that what you praise in him belongs to the praise of God; but perhaps you ask how what you accuse in yourself also belongs to his praise. This is what can be briefly said and understood: when you accuse yourself of sin, you praise Him who made you without sin. For if he had created you with sin, you would not accuse yourself as a sinner, but rather him as the creator. Therefore in your preaching of God there is praise and your accusation is praise of God: both things correspond to confession. We have heard 2 the Son of God saying: I confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth. What do you confess to him? What do you praise him for? Because you hid this, he says, from the wise and prudent and revealed it to the little ones. Who are the wise and prudent? Who are the little ones? What has he hidden from the wise and prudent and revealed to the little ones? pectus tundunt: non eis videtur aliud aiiquid significare confessio, nisi qua solent uti paenitentes, peccata sua confitentes, a deo (}57) menta sua expectantes, non quod merentur pati, sed quod ille misericorditer faceré digntur. Quod si non esset in laude confessio, non diceret confiteor tibi Pater, qui nullum habebat peccatum quod confiteretur. Dicitur etiam in quodam scripturae libro: confitemini domino, et haec dicetis in confessione: opera domini universa quoniam bona valde (Eccli 39, 20-21). Etiam hic confessio laudis est, non culpae. Quando ergo laudas deum, confiteris deo; quando peccata tua accusas coram deo, confiteris deo: totum autem hoc ad laudem pertinet creatoris, et quod ipsum praedicas, et quod te accusas. 3. Sed quoniam ad laudem ipsius pertinet quod eum praedicas, nemo ambigit; quomodo autem ad laudem eius pertineat et quod te accusas, forsitan quareres.

Hoc est quod breviter dici et intellegi potest: cum in peccato accusas te, laudas eum qui sine peccato fecit te; nam si ille cum peccato te faceret, non accusares te peccanteni, sed il'um createm. Ergo in praedicatione dei laus est; et accusatio tua, laus dei: utrumque pertinet ad confessionem. Audivimus Filium dei dicentem: confiteor tibi, Pater, domine caeli et terrae. What is the confitetur? In quo eum laudat? Quia abscondisii haec a sapientibus, inquit, et prudentibus, et revelationsti ea parvidis (Mt 11,25). Who are wise and prudent? who

He calls wise and prudent those of whom Paul says: Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the researcher of this century? Has not God made the wisdom of this world foolish? You may still ask who this text refers to. Perhaps to those who, discussing many things about God, told falsehoods; inflated with their doctrines, they could not find and know God. Perhaps someone will say that the apostle Paul refers to these, when he says: Where is the wise man, where is the scribe, where is the researcher of this century? Let them also be these: let us also understand those who could not know God and instead of God, whose substance is incomprehensible and invisible, they thought that he was air, ether, sun, something that stands out sensibly in creation. Contemplating the greatness, beauty and strength of the creatures, they remained in them and did not find the Creator, admiring his works. Nothing prevents us from saying that these are also indicated. 4. However, dear ones, it is more admirable that in a certain place in Holy Scripture we find that those who knew him are rebuked and their stupidity and false wisdom are scolded and accused. In fact, the Book of Wisdom argues against those who did not know the Creator through the creature, saying: They thought that God was the orbit of the stars, the sun, the moon, the rulers of the globe of the earth. And it is said of them that, although they are preferred to those who worshiped idols, and thought they were gods, the works were not of God, but of men, without parvuli? Quae ille occultavit sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelavit parvulis? Sapientes et prudentes illos significat, de quibus Paulus dicit: ubi sapiens? ubi scribe? ubi inquisitor huius saeculi? nonne stultam fecit deus sapientiam huius mundi? (1 Cor 1:20). Etiam nunc adhuc fortasse quaeris, qui sunt isti. Forte illi sunt, qui multum de [503] deo disputantes false dixerunt; inflati doctrinis suis, deum invenire et cognoscere minime potuerunt. Hos fortasse quis dicat eos Fuisse significatos ab apostólo Paulo, qui dicit: Ubi sapiens? ubi scribe? ubi conquisitor huius saeculi?

Sint quidem et isti: intellegantur (358) etiam qui deum cognoscere minime potuerunt, et pro deo, cuius est incomprehensibilis invisibilisque substantia, putaverunt deum esse aerem, aetherem, deum esse solem, deum esse aliquid quod sublimiter eminet in creatura; attendentes enim magnitudeines et pulchritudines et fortitudines creaturarum, ibi remanserunt, creatotem non invenerunt, admirantes quae facta sunt. Nihil ab re est, etiam istos significatos accipere. 4. Verumtamen, carissimi, magis mirum est, quod invenimus in quodam scripturae sanctae loco, etiam illos reprehensos qui cognoverunt, et ipsorum accusatam stultitiam, falsamque inrisam esse sapientiam. Nam illos qui non cognoverunt ex creatura creatorem arguit liber ille Sapientiae, ubi dicit, quia siderum gyrum, quia solem, quia lunam, rectores orbis terrarum déos putaverunt (Wis 13,2). Et de his dictum est, quod, licet praeferantur eis qui idok coluerunt, et opera hominum, non opera

However, they are also accused saying: Nor do these deserve forgiveness. Compared to those who have the works of men as gods, those who have the works of God as gods are undoubtedly better. The idol was made by a carpenter, the sun was made by God: in comparison with the one who considers as god what the carpenter made, better is the one who considers as god what God made. But see how these too are rejected and rightly accused: Nor do these deserve forgiveness; Well, if they were able to calculate the century, how did they not find the Lord of the century more easily? He accuses those who consumed their time and the occupations of their discussions in studying and in a certain way measuring creatures: they investigated the orbits of the stars, the intervals of the stars, the paths of the celestial bodies; to such an extent that, with certain calculations, they achieved the science of predicting eclipses of the sun and the moon, and, as they predicted, they occurred on the day and hour, in the intensity and part announced by them. Great skill! Great talent! But when they looked for the Creator, who was not far from them, they did not find Him. If they had found it, they would have it with them. As if someone entering this basilica counted the columns, measured how many cubits you have, calculated the height of the ceiling, the width of the pavement and the height of the walls and gave you the whole number that you do not know; But if you knew who built the basilica and he did not know, and in his real and profound uncertainty he did not believe that the factory was built by someone, but rather he estimated that these columns, this roof, these dei, déos esse putaverunt; tamen etiam ipsi accusati sunt, ut diceretur: iterum nec ipsis est ignoscendum (Wis 13,8). Iam enim in comparatione eorum qui déos habent opera hominum, utique meliores qui déos habent opera dei. Idolum enim faber fecit, solem deus fecit: in comparatione eius qui deum putat quod faber fecit, melior est ille qui hoc putat deum quod deus fecit. Sed tamen attention quomodo arguantur etiam ipsi, et quam recte accusentur: iterum, inquit, nec ipsis est ignoscendum? si enim tantum potuerunt valere, ut possent aestimare saeculum, quomodo eius dominum non facilius invenerunt? (Wis 13,8-9).

Accusati sunt consumantes tempora sua et occupationes disputationum suarum in perscrutanda et quodammodo metienda creature: quaesierunt meatus siderum, intervalla stellarum, itinera caelestium corporum; ita ut computationibus quibusdam ad eam scientiam pervenirent, ut praedicerent defectum solis, defectum lunae, et quando praedicerent eveniret, eo die et ea hora, tantum, et tanta parte, ex quanta parte illi praedixerant. Great industry! great sollertia! Sed ubi creatorem scrutati sunt, positum non longe a se, non invenerunt; quem si invenissent, haberent apud se. Tamquam [504] si quisquam istam fabricam ingressus numeraret columns, metiretur quot cubitorum essent, colligeret altitudinem tecti, latitudinem pavi(359) menti, staturamque parietum, et renuntiaret tibi de omnibus numerum quem tuignores; sed tu tamen a quo esset fabrica constructa

walls are there by their own virtue and nature, without anyone making them; or else he attributed such power to some element of this factory that he believed that this element built everything else. And if when you said to him: "a man made this factory", he said: "what man? How could one man build this factory? That ceiling that you see so high, that ceiling made all this that you see below", I say that it would seem to you not a fool, but a madman. What would be the benefit of having computed the measurements of all the columns, and the numbers of the entire factory, and telling you what you don't know? You, endowed with better science, would know the maker of this factory. Because knowing that it was made by a man, that it was made with reason, that it was built with a rational mind, that a decision preceded this mass, is better than knowing how many cubits the column has, or how many the columns are, or how wide the floor and the roof. 5. I think that your charity discerns these sciences. At this point you don't know much, when you know that a man built it, even if you attribute this factory to the man's own body. But you already know something great if you know that he made it with a decision, with a rational mind, in which the factory was before it appeared in sight. The decision to manufacture preceded and then the effect followed. What you cannot see preceded, so that what you see could exist. Now you see the factory, you praise the decision; You pay attention to what you see and praise what you do not see; and what you don't see is more than what you see. Therefore, optimal and straight

Mostly those who could count the numbers of the stars, the time intervals and know and predict eclipses are denounced; They are rightly accused, since they did not find who did and ordered these things, because they were negligent in investigating it. And don't worry too much if you ignore the course of the stars and the celestial or terrestrial bodies; contemplate the beauty of the world and praise the decision of the Creator: look at what he made and love him who made it. And hold this above all: love him who made it; for he also made you, his lover, in his image. It is no wonder if those things that Christ said: You hid them from the wise and prudent remained hidden from these wise men who were busy with creatures, and who through negligence refused to seek the Creator, and could not find Him. What you are going to hear is more marvelous: that the wise and prudent who were able to know are rebuked. The wrath of God is revealed, he says, from heaven on all injustice and impiety of men who hold back the truth in iniquity. Perhaps you ask: What truth do they retain in iniquity? For what is known of God is manifest in them. How do I manifest? He goes on to say: God manifested it to them. Do you still ask how he manifested himself to them, since he did not give them the law? As? The invisible things of God since the creation of the world, understood, are discovered through the things that were created. This is how he manifested it, because the invisible things of God, understood, are perceived through the things created since the creation of the world.

scires, ille nesciret, et nimium rerum incertus non putaret hanc fabricam ab homine constitutam, sed aestimaret columns istas, hoc tectum, istos parietes, sua vi et natura, nullo actore extitisse; aut alicui parti fabricae huius eam ttibueret potentiam, ut ab ipsa ceteta consttucta esse sentimentale: et tu cum dixisses, Homo fecit hanc fabricam; ille diceret, Quis homo? when homo potuit hanc fabricam fabricare? Tectum hoc quod vides altum, ipsum tectum fabricavit ista omnia quae cernis humilia. Non dico desipiens, delirus tibi appareret. Et quid ei prodesset, quod tibi mensuram columnarum omnium totiusque fabricae computaret numbers, et diceret quod tu nescires? Homo meliore praeditus scientia, actorem huius fabricae scires: plus est enim nosse quia homo fecit, quia ratione factum est, quia rationali mente constructum est, quia consilium praecessit hanc molem; quam scire quot cubitorum columna sit, vel quot sint columnae, vel quam latum pavimentum aut tectum. 5. Puto quod caritas vestra discernat istas scientias. Non enim et in hoc magnum aliquid seis, quoniam nos ti hominem fecisse, si et ipsi hominis corpori tribuas hanc fabricam. Magnum aliquid nosti, si nosti factum esse consilio, rationali mente, ubi Fuit ipsa fabrica ante quam oculis videretur. Praecessit enim fabricandi consilium, ac deinde consecutus effectus est: praecessit quod non videres, ut esset quod videres. Nunc ergo vides fabricam, laudas consilium: intendis in quod vides, laudas quod non vides; et plus est quod non vides, quam illud quod vides.

Optime itaque rectissimeque aecusati sunt, qui potuerunt investigare numbers siderum, intervalla temporum, defectum luminum cognoscere, praedicere: recte aecusati sunt; quoniam, a quo ista facta atque ordinata sunt, non invenerunt, quia quaerere neglexerunt. Tu autem non valde cures, si gyros siderum et caelestium tierrarumve corporum ignores: vide pulchritudinem mundi, et lauda consilium creatoris: vide quod fecit, ama qui fecit. Dye hoc maxime, ama qui fecit; quia et te ipsum amatorem suum ad imaginem suam fecit. Ergo quid est mirum, quia talibus sapientibus oceupatis circa creaturas, qui creatorem neglegentes quaerere noluerunt, nec invenire potuerunt, abscondita sunt illa de quibus dixit Christus, [505] abscondisti (360) haec a sapientibus et prudenlibus? Mirabilius est quod audituri estis, sapientes et prudentes reprehensos etiam qui cognoscere potuerunt. Revelatur, inquit, ira dei de cáelo super omnem impietatem et iniustitiam hominum, qui veritatem in iniquitate detinent (Rom 1:18). Quaeris fortasse, quam veritatem detineant in iniquitate? Quia quod notum est dei, manifestum est in Mis. Unde manifestum? Sequitur et dicit: deus enim Mis manifestavit (ib., 19). Adhuc quaeris, quomodo manifestaverit eis, quibus legem non dedit? What ergo mode? lnvisibilia enim eius a constitutione mundi per ea quae facta sunt intellecta conspiciuntur (ib., 20). Sic ergo manifestavit, quia invisibilia eius a constitutione mundi per ea quae facta sunt intellecta conspiciuntur,

6. Someone, to find God, reads the book. It is, without a doubt, a great book, the very beauty of creation. Contemplate the upper and lower ones, pay attention, read. God did not make ink letters, wherever you knew him: he put before your eyes those same things that he made. Why are you looking for a greater voice? Heaven and earth cry out to you: "God made me." You read what Moses wrote. What does temporal man read, so that Moses himself would write? Piously contemplate heaven and earth. There were some not like Moses, servant of God; not like many prophets, who contemplated and understood these things with the help of the Spirit of God; They sipped the Spirit with faith, drank with the fauces of piety and belched with the mouth of the inner man. These men were not these, but very different. Through this creation, they were able to come to understand the Creator and speak of the things that God made: here is what He made, governs and contains; He himself, who made it, fills with his presence that which he made. They could say that. In the Acts of the Apostles the apostle Paul mentioned them, saying of God: In him we live, we move and we have our being. He was speaking before the Athenians, among whom those wise men were found, and he added at once: as some of you said. What they said is not a little: that in God we live, we move and we are. Why then are they dissimilar? Why reviled? Why rightly denounced? Listen to the words of the Apostle that I had begun to quote: The wrath of God, he says, is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness, namely, that of those who did not receive the law. Concerning all impiety and injustice of men who retain the truth in 6. Alius, ut inveniat deum, librum legit. Est quídam magnus liber ipsa species cteaturae: superiorem et inferiorem contuere, attende, lege. Non deus, unde eum cognosceres, de atramento litteras fecit: ante oculos tuos posit haec ipsa quae fecit. Quid quaetis maiorem vocem? Clamat ad te caelum et terra: Deus me fecit. Legis quod scripsit Moyses. Quid legit, ut scriberet ipse Moyses, homo temporalis? Attend pie caelum et terram. Fuerunt ergo quidam, non sicut Moyses famulus dei, non sicut prophetae multi ista intuentes et intellegentes, adiuti Spititu dei; quem Spiritum fide hauserunt, faucibus pietatis biberunt, ore intcrioris hominis ructaverunt. Non ergo such.

Sed fuerunt alii dissimiles, qui per istam creaturam potuerunt pervenite ad intellegendum creatorem, et dicere de his quae fecit deus: Ecce quae fecit, gubernat et continet; ille ipse, qui fecit, inplet sua praesentia ista quae fecit. Potuerunt hoc dicere: nam ipsos et in Actibus apostolorum commemoravit apostolus Paulus, ubi, cum dixisset de deo, in illo enim vivimus et movemur et sumus, quoniam apud Athenians loquebatur, ubi isti doctissimi extiterant, adiunxit continuo: sicut et quidam secundum vos dixerunt (Act 17,28). Non est leve quod dixerunt, quioniam in deo vivimus, et movemur et sumus. Unde ergo dissimiles? unde vituperati? unde recte accusati? Audi apostoli verba, quae dicere coeperam; revehtur, intjuitj ira dei de cáelo super omnem

the injustice. What truth? Because what is known of God is manifest in them. Who expressed it? Well, God showed it to him. How did he express it? For the invisible things of God from the creation of the world, understood, are perceived through the things that were made; also his everlasting virtue and divinity. What did he say it for? So that they are inexcusable. If he stated it so that they are inexcusable, why are they guilty? Because, knowing God, they did not glorify him as God. What are you saying, that they did not glorify him as God? They didn't even thank him. So, to glorify God is to thank him. Definitely. Is there anything worse than, made in his image and knowing him, being ungrateful? That is, by the way, that is glorifying God, giving thanks to God. The baptized know where and when it is said: "Let us give thanks to God our Lord." And who gives thanks to the Lord except he who has his heart lifted up to the Lord? 7. Among you there are those who hear and those who do not hear. Do not be angry with us if they differ. Those, then, are guilty; They are inexcusable, because, knowing God, they did not glorify him as God, nor give thanks to him. What did they do? They faded into thought. And why did they fade away if not because they were superb? Smoke also dissipates when it rises high; Instead, the fire shines and burns, remaining more humble. They faded away in their thoughts and their nascent heart darkened. Also impietatem, eorum scilicet qui legem non acceperunt; super omnem impie(631)tatem et iniustitiam hominum, qui veritatem in iniquitate detinent. Quam veritatem? Quia quod notum est dei, manifestum est [506] in illis. What protester? Deus enim Mis manifestavit. How did you manifest? Invisibilia enim eius a constitutione mundi per ea quae jacta sunt intellecta conspiciuntur, sempiterna quoque virtus eius ac divinitas. Quare manifestavit? Ut sint inexcusable (Rom 1,20). Si manifestavit ut sint inexcusabiles, unde ergo culpable? Quia cognoscentes deum, non sicut deum glorificaverunt. Quid est quod dicis, Non sicut deum glorificaverunt? Nec gratias egerunt (ib., 21). Hoc est ergo glorificare deum, gratias agere deo. Hoc sane: quid enim peius, si ad imaginem creatus, cognito deo eris ingratus? Hoc est, prorsus, hoc est glorificare deum, gratias agere deo. Norunt fideles, ubi et quando dicatur, gratias agamus domino Deo nostro. Quis autem gratias agit domino, nisi qui sursum cor habet ad dominum? 7.

Sunt in his verbis inter vos qui audiunt, et non audiunt: sed non nobis irascantur, quando ipsi se differunt. Ergo illi culpabiles: qui sunt inexcusabiles, quia cognoscentes deum, non sicut deum glorificaverunt, nec gratias egerunt. Be quid? sed evanuerunt in cogitationibus suis (ib.). Unde evanuerunt, nisi quia superbi fuerunt? Evanescit et fumus, in altum arising; et magis ignis luzet et roboratur, humilius apprehendendo. Evanuerunt in cogitationibus suis, et obscuratum est insipiens cor eorum

The smoke is dark, although it is over the fire. Finally, pay attention to what follows and see what the whole dispute was about: Calling themselves wise, they became fools. By assuming what God had lent them, God took back what he had given them. It is that it is hidden from the proud, since to those who diligently seek, through creatures, the Creator only suggests Himself. Thus says the Lord well: You hid this from the wise and prudent: and from those who with many discussions and keen investigation came to the knowledge of creation, but did not know the Creator; and to those who knew God, but did not glorify him as God or give thanks to him, and could not see him perfectly and healthily, since they were proud. You hid this from the wise and prudent and revealed it to the little ones. To what little ones? To the humble, for he says: On whom does my Spirit rest? About the humble, serene and fearful of my words. Peter feared these words, Plato did not fear them. Let the fisherman pick up what the most noble lost. discussed You hid this from the wise and prudent and revealed it to the little ones: you hid it from the proud and revealed it to the humble. What are we, no matter how much we are? If we are humble, we will deserve to enjoy the full vision of God if we deserve to be counted among the little ones. Thus, Father, said the Lord, exulting in the Holy Spirit; He approved it, he was pleased, he praised that it had been so: Thus, Father, so it was accepted before you. 8. We have heard that he said: You hid this from the wise and

wise and you revealed it to the little ones, and we saw who are the wise and prudent and who are those little ones to whom you revealed it. And what did it reveal? When he said: You hid this from the wise and prudent and revealed it to the little ones, did he not refer to heaven and earth, and as if he showed it with his hand, saying: This? Who doesn't see it? The good see it, the bad see it, because He made His sun rise on the good and the bad. What then is this, of which he says that he hid it from the wise and prudent and revealed it to the little ones? What can it be but what he indicates next, saying: Thus, Father, for thus was it accepted before you? He praised it, he liked it. And what is it? Everything has been given to me by my Father. This Christian grace, according to which all things were given to him by his Father, was ignored by all the wise men of this world; and not only of those who, occupied with excessive and intense curiosity in celestial or terrestrial creatures, neglected to search and did not manage to find the Creator, but also by those who, through the creatures and the things they saw, that is, through the visible things, were able to reach with their thoughts the One who made them: neither one nor the other knew what was said: All things have been given to me by my Father. Moses saw it, the prophets saw it, the patriarchs saw it; Those great wise men, sharp discussants, researchers, loud wasters of language, completely ignored him. This is the mystery hidden from eternity in God, and now revealed to his saints, to his little ones, to his humble ones, on whom his Spirit rests, calm and

(ib.). Etiam fumus, cum sit igne altior, obscuras est. Denique attende quod sequitur, et vide unde tota causa pendeat: Dicentes enim se esse sapientes, stulti facti sunt (ib., 22). Sibi adrogando quod praestiterat deus, tulit quod dederat deus. Ergo superbis ipse abscondit se, qui per creaturam diligenter scrutantibus creatorem insinuaverat non nisi se. Bene ergo dominus: Abscondisti haec a sapientibus et prudentibus: sive ab illis qui multiplicibus disputationibus et sollertissima inquisitione ad investigationem creaturae pervenerunt, sed creatorem minime cognoverunt; sive ab illis qui cognoscentes deum, non sicut deum glorificaverunt aut gratias egerunt, et videre perfecte ac salubriter non potuerunt, quia superbi fuerunt. Abscondisti ergo haec a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revealsti ea parvulis. Quibus parvulis? humilibus. Dicit: super quem requiescet (632) spiritus meus? super humilem et quietum et trementem verba mea (Is 66,2). Haec verba Petras tremuit, Plato non tremuit: teneat piscator, quod perdidit nobüissimus disputator. Abscondisti haec a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelationsti ea parvulis: [507] abscondisti superbis, et revelationsti humilibus. Quid ergo sumus, quantumcumque sumus? Si humiles sumus, merebimur plena conspectu dei beatificari, si meruerimus Inter pvulos numerari. Ita, Pater, inquit exultans spiritu sancto—approbavit, placuit ei, laudavit ita esse, laudavit ita factum esse—ita, Pater, quoniam sic placitum est coram te (Mt 11:26). 8. Audivimus, quod ait abscondisti haec a sapientibus et prudentibus,

et revealed this parvulis, which sunt parvuli quibus revealed. Quae sunt ipsa? Non enim, cum hoc diceret, abscondisti haec a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revealsti ea parvulis, caelum et terram attendebat, et quasi manu demonstrabat, cum diceret haec. Quis enim non videt haec? Vident boni, vident et mali, quia facit solem suum oriri super bonds et malo (Mt 5:45). Quae sunt ergo haec, de quibus ait, quia abscondisti haec a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revealsti ea parvulis? Quae, nisi quae deinceps adiungit, et dicit, ita, Pater, quoniam sic placitum est coram te? Hic laudavit, placuit ei. Quae sunt ergo ista? Omnia mihi tradita sunt a Paire meo (Mt 11:27). Gratia is ista christiana, quia omnia tradita sunt a Patre eius, omnes latuit sapientes huius mundi. Nec solum illi qui circa creatures vel terrestrials vel caelestes nimia et intentissima curiositate occupati neglexerunt quaerere nec valuerunt invenire creatorem, sed etiam nec illi qui ex creatura et ex his quae videbantur id est ex visibilibus ad eum a quo facta sunt in cogitatione pervenire potuerunt, agnoverunt quod dictum est, omnia mihi tradita sunt a Padre meo. Haec Moyses vidit, prophetae viderunt, patriarchae viderunt; sapientes illi magni, arguti disputatores, inquisitores, eloquii quasi tonantes profusores, omnino ignoraverunt. Hoc est mysterium quod absconditum Fuit a saeculis in deum, nunc autem manifestum est sanctis eius (Col 1:26), parvulis eius, ergo humilibus eius,

afraid of his words: All things, he says, have been given to me by my Father. 9. But among all these things we want and yearn vehemently to see God himself, and we desire it all the more as we are better, more pious, more faithful, better instructed in the progress of the mind, more firm: this desire dominates all others. Therefore, to his little ones, whom he allowed to know his grace: the fact that all things have been given to Christ by his Father, it seems that he speaks to them with affection, so that they do not become impatient because they do not see him now, so that they endure the medicinal wait, preparing for that vision. All things,' he says, have been given to me by my Father. The little ones were going to say: we want to see the Father himself, as Philip said: Show us the Father and it is enough for us. As if to say: I know what you are longing for and that you are too small for such great good: No one knows the Son but the Father. You thought you already knew me: No one knows the Son but the Father. As if, once you know me, you seek to see and know the Father. And no one knows the Father except the Son. But you are not going to be excluded from this vision, because it continues: and to whom the Son wants to reveal it. And who will the Son want to reveal it except to those whom he mentioned: And you revealed it to the little ones? Let us, therefore, be small: let us gather it and learn it from the great Master. Since you are nothing, will you not want to be small, when for you the Immense One became small? The Father reveals the Son to those he loves. For if the Son reveals the Father, will not the Father reveal

to the Son? Here we heard, here we read: And no one knows the Father except the Son and to whomever the Son wants to reveal him. We call the Son the revealer of the Father. And how do we know that the Father is the revealer of the Son? Listen to the Son himself. When Peter said: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God, he received this answer: Blessed are you, Simon Bariona, because it was not flesh and blood that revealed it to you, but my Father who is in heaven. Then the Father reveals the Son and the Son also reveals the Father. Well, how do you recognize the Son if you do not recognize that he has a Father? Or how do you recognize the Father if you do not recognize that he has a Son? He cannot be called Father if he does not have a son; nor can he be called Son if he does not have a Father. Therefore, if he is not a Father except insofar as he has a Son, the Father reveals the Son. By recognizing paternity, offspring are sought; If it is Father, you seek him who begat; and that is Christ God. And if Christ is a Son, you ask by whom he was begotten; and that is God the Father.
