Promittitur nobis conspectus Dei, veri Dei, summi Dei. Hoc enim bonum est, videntem videre. Nam qui colunt false déos, facile illos vident: sed eos vident, qui oculos habent et non vident. Nobis autem promittitur visio Dei vivirtis et videntís, ut illum Deum videre concupiscamus, de quo dicit Scriptura: Qui plantavit aurem, nonne audiet? who finxit oculum, nonneconsiderat? Non ergo audit, who tibi fecit unde audits? et non videt, qui creavit unde videos? Bene in ipso Psalmo praeloquitur et dicit, Intellegite ergo, qui insipientes estis in populo; et stulti, aliquando sapite (Ps 93,9.8). Multi enim propterea mala faciunt, dum putant quod non videantur a Deo. Et difficile est quidem ut eum credant videre non posse: sed putant nolle.

Pauci ínveniuntur tantae impietatis, ut impleatur in eis quod scriptum est: Dixit stultus in corde suo, Non est Deus (Ps 13,1). Insania ista paucorum est. Sícut enim magna pietas, paucorum est; ita et magna impietas, nihilominus paucorum est. Hoc autem quod dico, turba dicit: Ecce moda inde cogitat Deus, ut sciat quid fació in domo mea, et curat Deus quid velim agere in lecto meo? What did you say? Intellegite, qui insipientes estis in populo; et stulti, aliquando sapite (Ps 93,9.8). Tu homo cum sis, quia laboras si omnia domus tuae noveris et pertineant ad te omnia verba, omnia facta servorum tuorum, putas et Deum sic laborare ut attendat ad te, qui non laboravit ut creaet te? Qculum in te non intendit suum, qui fecit tuum? Non eras, et creavit te

You were not, and He made you to be; Will he not look at you, when you already are, the one who calls things that are not as if they were? Don't flatter yourself with such things. Whether you want it or not, he sees you; and there is nowhere you can hide from their eyes. Because if you go up to heaven, it is there, and if you go down to hell, it appears there. You tire yourself out by refusing to stop your bad works and pretending that God doesn't see you. Hard work! Every day you try to do evil, and do you suspect that he doesn't see you? Listen to the Scripture that says: He who planted an ear, will he not hear? Who created the eye, will he not see? Where do you hide your evil deeds from the eyes of God? If you don't want to give them up, look for a job. 4. Listen to him who says: Come to me, all you who labor. You won't end up shying away from work. Do you choose to run from him and not to him? Find where and run away. And if you cannot flee from him, because he is present everywhere, flee to God immediately, because he is present where you are. Run away. Behold, fleeing you scaled the heavens; there it is; you descended into hell, there it is. In whatever earthly solitudes you choose, there is the one who said I fill heaven and earth. If he fills heaven and earth, and there is nowhere you can flee from him, do not be weary; flee into his presence, and you don't have to feel him coming. Suppose you will see him living well, since he sees you when you live badly. Living badly, you can be seen, you can't see; but living well, you are seen and you see. With how much greater familiarity will he who crowns the worthy see you, since he saw mercifully to call the unworthy? Nathanael said ut esses: non te cutat, cum iam sis, qui vocat ea quae non sunt, tanquam sint? (Rom 4:17). Non ergo tibi hoc promittas. Velis, nolis, videt te; et ab eius oculis non est ubi abscondas te. Si enim you will ascend in caelum, ibi est; if de[442]scenderis in inferum, adest (cf. Ps 138,8). Laboras, nolens recedete a factis malis, et volens non videri a Deo. Magnus labor. Faceré vis mala quotidie, suspicaris te non videri? Audi Scripturam dícentem: Qui plantavit aurem, nonne auditet? who finxit occult, nonneconsiderat? (Ps 93.9). Ubi mala facta tua abscondis ab oculis Dei? Si non vis recedere ab ipsis, multum laboras. CAPUT III.—4. Peccatori fugiendum ad Deum.—Audi dicentem: Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis (Mt 11:28). Non finis laborem fugiendo. Ab íllo do you choose fugere, non ad illum? Inveni quo, et fuge. Si autem propterea non potes ab illo fugere, quia ubique praesens est; from next fuge ad Deum, qui praesens est, ubi stas. Escape.

Ecce fugiendo excessisti caelos, ibi est: descendisti ad inferos, ibi est: quascumque terrarum solitudeines elegeris, ibi est qui dixit, Caelum et terram ego impleo (Jer 23,24). Ergo si caelum et terram ipse implet, et quo fugere ab illo non est; noli laborare: fuge ad praesentem, ne sentias venientem. Praesume te visurum bene vivir, a quo videris et male vivir. Male enim vivirdo videri potes, videre non potes: bene autem vivirdo et videris, et vides. Quanto enim te familiarius videbit qui coronat dignum, qui misericorditer vidit ut vocaret indignum? Nathanael ait Domino, quem nondum sciebat:
The revelation made to the

to the Lord, whom I did not yet know: How do you know me? And the Lord said to him: When you were under the fig tree, I saw you. Christ sees you in your darkness, and will he not see you in his light? What does it mean then when you were: under the fig tree I saw you? What does that mean or what does it mean? Remember the original sin of Adam, in whom we all died. As soon as he sinned, he made a girdle of fig leaves, these leaves signifying the itching of libido, produced by his sin. From him we are born, so we are born, we are born in sinful flesh, which only finds cure in the image of sinful flesh. That is why God sent his Son in that likeness of sinful flesh. It came from there, but it didn't come like that. Because the Virgin did not conceive him in libido, but in faith.' He came to the Virgin who existed before the Virgin. He chose the one he had created, he created the one he was to choose. He offered the Virgin fertility, he did not take away her integrity. Therefore, he who came to you without the itching of the fig leaves saw you when you were under the fig tree. Prepare to see in sublimity the one who saw you in mercy. But since it is a very high peak, think about the foundation. And you will say: On what foundation? Learn from him who is meek and humble of heart. Dig in yourself that foundation of humility and you will reach the peak of charity. Turned towards the Lord... Unde me nosti? Ait ei Dominus: Cum esses sub arbore fici, vidi te (lo 1.48). Videt te Christus in umbra tua: non te videbit in luz sua? Quid est enim, Cum esses sub arbore fici, vidi te? Quid sibi hoc vult? What does it mean? I will remember originale peccatum Adae, in quo omnes morimur. Quando primo peccavit, de foliis ficulneis succinctoria sibi fecit (Gen 3:7), significans in illis foliis pruritum libidinis, quo peccando pervenit. Inde nascimur, sic nascimur, in carne peccati nascimur, quam sola sanat similaro carnis peccati. Ideo misit Deus filium suum in similarityinem carnis peccati (Rom 8:3). Inde come, sed sic non venit. Non enim eum virgo libidine, sed fide concepit. Come in virginem, qui erat ante virginem. Quam creavit elegit, quam chooseret creavit. Attulit virgini fecundítatem, non abstulit integritatem. Qui ergo sine pruritu foliorum ficus venit ad te, cum esses sub arbore fici, vidit te. Para te videre sublimiter, a quo visus es misericorditer. Sed quia magnum fastigium est, of cogita foundation. What, inquisitive, foundation? Disce ab illo, quoniam mitis est, et humilis corde. Hoc in te fodi fundamentum humilitatis, et pervenies ad fastigium caritatis.

Topic: The yoke of Christ (Mt 11,28-30). Place: Carthage. Date: In the year 413. 1. It seems strange to some, my brothers, to hear the Lord saying: Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened, and I will give you relief. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am meek and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is Command and my burden is light. They observe that those who accepted that yoke with a fearless neck and accepted that burden with very meek shoulders, see themselves agitated and exercised by so many difficulties of this century, that they do not seem called from work to rest, but from rest to work; and the Apostle says: All who want to live piously in Christ will suffer persecution. So someone will say: How easy is the yoke and the light burden, since to bear that yoke and that burden is nothing other than living godly in Christ? And how is it said Come to me, all you who work and are burdened, and I will give you relief, and not rather say: Come, you who are unemployed, and you will work? Because he found those he hired for his vineyard unemployed, to bear the burden.

choro of the day. And under that soft yoke and that light burden, we hear the Apostle say: In everything we recommend ourselves, as ministers of God, in great patience, in tribulations, needs, anguish, blows, etc. And in another place of the same epistle: From the Jews I received five times the forty lashes except one, three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I suffered shipwreck, I spent a day and a night in the depths of the sea, and the other dangers that can be counted, but cannot be tolerated except with the help of the Holy Spirit. 2. All those harshnesses and brokennesses that he mentioned, he suffered frequently and abundantly, but the Holy Spirit assisted him; This, in the corruption of the external man, renewed the interior day by day, and giving it a taste of spiritual rest in the abundance of the delights of God, softened everything present in the hope of future blessedness, and lightened everything heavy. That is how he bore the soft yoke of Christ and the light burden. This is how he calls light tribulation all those hard and terrible things that frighten any reader: he looked with interior and faithful eyes that, no matter how high the temporal price that must be paid for the future life, the eternal labors of the wicked are avoided and the eternal happiness of the righteous is enjoyed without request. Men tolerate being cut and burned to avoid the price of acute pain; not other eternal pains, but those of a somewhat lasting ulcer. To achieve a last retirement, a languid and uncertain life of very brief vacation, the soldier endures cruel wars; live restlessly perhaps for many years at work, better than waiting to rest

To what tempests and storms, to what horrible and tremendous fury of the sky and the sea, merchants expose themselves to acquire riches of air, full of dangers and storms greater than those with which they were acquired! What heat, what cold, what dangers from horses, from holes, from precipices, from rivers, from wild beasts, do hunters face! What scarcity of food and drink, what anguish of food and drink, vile and dirty, to capture a beast! And sometimes it is not even necessary to eat the meat of that beast, for which so many things are tolerated. Even if a wild boar or a deer has been hunted, it is more pleasant for the hunter's hobby to have hunted it than for the glutton's palate to have eaten it. To what punishments of bitter lashes are children not condemned at the tender age! With what annoyances of vigils and abstinence they are exercised not to learn wisdom, but for money and the honors of vanity, so that they learn to count, to read and to utter eloquent fallacies! '. 3. In all this, those who do not love suffer those same heavy things; Those who love suffer the same thing, it seems, but they are not heavy. Because all those fierce and atrocious things are made easy and almost null by love. Well, with how much greater certainty and ease, when it comes to authentic happiness?

Will charity do what, when it came to misery, cupidity did, as far as it could? How easily any temporary adversity is tolerated to avoid eternal punishment, to achieve eternal peace! No wonder the Vessel of Election said with immense joy: Temporary sufferings do not correspond to the future glory that will be revealed in us. You see why that yoke is soft, and the burden light. If it is difficult for the few who choose it, it is easy for all who love it. The psalmist says: By the words of your lips I have kept the hard ways. Those roads that are hard for workers are soft for lovers. Therefore the dispensation of divine providence made it so that the inner man, which is renewed day by day, no longer lives under the law, but under grace; freed from the burdens of innumerable observances that constituted a heavy yoke, but very convenient to tame a stiff neck, he now has the ease of simple faith, good hope and holy charity; All the annoyances that were outwardly imposed on the outward man by that prince who was cast out, are made light by the inward joy. Nothing is so easy for a good will as itself; and this is enough for God. No matter how cruel this world is, when the Lord was born in the flesh, the angels sang with all reason: Glory in the highest to God and on earth peace to men of good will. Because the yoke was easy and the burden of the one who had just been born was light. And, as the Apostle says, God is faithful, who does not allow a higher temptation

CAPUT III.—3. Amore dura quaeque mitescunt.—Sed in his omnibus qui haec non amant, eadem gravia patiuntur: qui vero amant, eadem quidem, sed non gravia pati videntur. Omnia enim saeva et immania, prorsus facilia et prope nulla efficit amor. Quanto ergo certius ac facilius In the City of God 21,14 remembers the same thing: "The same study that children are forced to do with punishments is so hard for them that sometimes they prefer to endure the punishments rather than study." And with notable rhetorical exaggeration, he continues: "Who will not feel horror and if they are offered the choice: die or return to childhood, will they not choose death?" For his bitter experience, consult Confessions I, 9,14.

Topic: Humility (Mt 11,28-30). Location: Unknown. Date: Unknown. 1. The tongue of the Lord, trumpet of justice and truth, rising as in a contest of the human race, calls and says: Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am meek and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy and my burden is light. He who is not weary, let him not listen; But whoever is weary with work, let him listen: Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened. He who is not loaded, does not listen; But whoever is laden, listen: Come to me, all you who work and are laden. So that? And I will relieve you. Everyone who works and is loaded, seeks relief, desires rest. And who does not get tired in this century? Tell me who doesn't work, either in work or in thought. The poor man works at work and works quod possumus ferré; sed facit cum temptatione etiam exitum, ut possimus sustinere (1 Cor 10:13). SERMO
ITEM EX EODEM CHAPTER EVANGELII. HUMILITATE (Mt 11,28-30)

1. Lingua domini, tuba iustitiae et veritatis, tamquam in generis humani contione consistens, vocat et dicit: come ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego vos reficiam. Tollite iugum meum super vos, et discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde, et invenietis requiem animabus vestris. Iugum enim meum gentle est, et onus meum leve est (Mt 11:28-30). Qui non laborat, non audit; qui autem laborat, audit: come ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis. Qui non est oneratus, non auditat; qui autem oneratus est, audiat: come ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis. Ut what? Et ego reficiam vos. Omnis qui laborat et oneratus est, refectionem quaerit, quietem desiderat. Et quis non laborat in hoc saeculo? Dicatur mihi, quis non laborat vel operand vel cogitando? Laborat in operibus pauper, laborat in cogitationibus dives:

pauper vult habere quod [513] non habet, et laborat; dives, timendo will lose quod habet, et volendo augere quod non habet, plus laborat. Onera vero sua portant omnes quaecumque peccata, quibus superba premitur cervix: et tamen sub tanta mole erigit se; et cum prematur peccatis, tumescit superbia. Ideo dominus ait, what? Ego, inquit, vos reficiam. Tollite iugum meum super vos, et discite me. Quid, domine, discimus a te? Scimus in principle te esse Verbum, et Vetbum (369) apud deum, et deum Verbum; scimus omnia per te esse facta, visibilia et invisibilia. What do you say? Caelumsuspenre, terram solidare, mare diffundere, aerem expandere, omnia elementa animalibus congruis implere, saecula ordinare, rotate tempora? What do you say? An forte, quae operatus es in terra, ipsa vis nos discere? haec vis túcere? Ergo discimus a te lepers mundare, daemonia peliere, febres fugare, mari et fluctibus imperare, mortuos suscitare? Necessary, restless. Say ergo, what? Quoniam mitis sum et humilis corde. Erubesce deo, superbia human. Verbum dei dicit, deus dicit, unigenitus dicit, altissimus dicit: discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde. So much altitude ad humilitatem descendit, et homo se tendit? Colíige te, et redige te, homo, ad humilem Christum, ne in tua extensione rumparis. 2. Psalmus cantabatur mode, Alleluia dicebatur mode: Quis sicut

and contemplate humble things? May I, when I look at you, find you humble, so that I may not condemn you. He said it, he proclaimed it, he called the human race to this salvation: Learn from me, he said, not to create the world, learn that I am meek and humble in heart. It existed in the beginning; Is there anything more excellent? The Word became flesh; Is there anything more humble? Rule in the world; Is there anything higher? Hangs from a tree; Is there anything more humble? If he suffers these things for you, why do you stand tall, puff up, inflated bellows? God is humble, and you are proud? Perhaps, since he said Excelso is the Lord and looks at humble things, you will say: he doesn't look at me. Would there be greater misfortune, if he did not look at you, but despised you? The look implies compassion, the contempt disdain. Or perhaps, as the Lord looks at humble things, you think that you go unnoticed, because you are not humble, you are great, you are proud. But you don't hide from the eyes of God. Look what it says there: Excelso is the Lord. Without a doubt He is excellent. Are you looking for stairs to climb to Him? Look for the wood of humility and you have arrived. The Lord is exalted and looks at humble things. And so that you do not think that you go unnoticed because you are arrogant, add: and know excellent things from afar. He knows them, but from afar. Salvation is far from sinners. How do you know the humble ones? Up close. Wonderful industry of the Almighty! He is exalted and looks at humble things closely; The proud are high and yet the Exalted knows them from afar. The Lord is near to those who have grieved their hearts, and will give salvation to those who are humble in spirit. Therefore, brothers, let pride not remain in

you swollen, but pruned. Feel horror of her and banish her. Christ seeks the humble Christian. Christ is in heaven, he is with us, he is in hell, not chained, but liberating. We have that captain. He is seated at the right hand of the Father, but he gathers us from the earth, one in one way and another in another; to one with a gift, to the other with a punishment; one with joy, the other with tribulation. Pick up what you pick up. Collect, so that we do not perish. Gather us there where there is no longer perdition, in that region of the living in which merits are recognized and justice is crowned.

The Apostle, rebuking, says to those who are proud and conceited of their own merits: Who discerns you? that is, "from the mass of perdition originating in Adam and from the vessels of wrath, who separates you?" 1. And so that no one answers: "My justice," add: What do you have that you have not received? And thus he says of himself: We too, of old, were naturally children of wrath, like the rest. He was also a vessel in the house of that evil strongman, when he was a persecutor of the Church, blasphemous, insolent, moved by malice and jealousy, as he himself confesses. But he who bound the strong man took from him the vessel of perdition and made it a vessel of election. 4. And so that the unbelievers and impious, enemies of the Christian name, would not believe, due to those various schisms and heresies that under the Christian name gather groups of the lost, that the kingdom of Christ is also divided against itself, he adds accordingly: He who is not with me is against me; and whoever does not gather with me scatters. Therefore, the kingdom of Christ is not divided against itself, although men insist on dividing what was purchased at the price of Christ's blood. For the Lord knows who his own are, and says: Let everyone who calls on the name of the Lord depart from iniquity. If you do not depart from iniquity, you do not belong to the kingdom of Christ, even if you mention the name of Christ. I will remember some things as an example: the spirit of greed and the

spirit of lust, since one withdraws and the other lavishes, they are divided against each other, and both belong to the kingdom of the devil. Among idol worshipers, the spirit of Juno and the spirit of Hercules are divided against each other, and both belong to the kingdom of the devil. The pagan enemy of Christ and the Jewish enemy of Christ are divided against each other and both belong to the kingdom of the devil. The Arian and the Photinian 2, both heretics, are divided against each other. The Donatist and the Maximianist 3, both heretics, are divided against each other; all the vices and errors of mortals that are contrary to each other, are divided against each other; and they all belong to the kingdom of the devil. That is why his kingdom will not stand. On the other hand, the righteous and the wicked, the faithful and the unbelieving, the Catholic and the heretic, are divided among themselves, but they do not both belong to the kingdom of Christ. The Lord knows who his people are. Nobody flatters himself with the title. If you want the name of the Lord to profit you, turn away from iniquity by calling on the name of the Lord. 5. These evangelical words, although they seemed somewhat obscure, I believe that with the help of God they are explained; but they were not as dark as those that follow seem to be: Therefore I tell you: men will be forgiven every sin or blasphemy; but the spirit of blasphemy will not be forgiven. Whoever says anything against the Son of man, it will be forgiven him; But whoever says it against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven either in this age or in the future. Sadducaei enim spiritum negabant; We see the same accusation appear in The Consensus of the Evangelists I, 14,22, and Treatises on the Gospel of Saint John 35,8. The problem surrounding the Holy Spirit was a derivation of the Arian controversy. In the beginning, the Holy Spirit was not at the center of the discussion, which revolved solely around the person of the Son; But it didn't take long for the consequences to be drawn: If the Son was not God, neither was the Holy Spirit; Furthermore, this was nothing other than the first creature produced by the Son. Historically, the problem became acute in the middle of the 4th century due to the work of the so-called pneumatomajoi (= those who fight against the Spirit). On the Orthodox side, the answer came from Saint Athanasius first and then from the Cappadocian Fathers, especially from Saint Basil, and culminated in the Second Ecumenical Council of Constantinople in the year 381, which declared God to the Spirit, although only indirectly: "who with the Father and the Son is adored and glorified."

For this reason, the Jews and all the heretics who confess the existence of the Holy Spirit deny that he dwells in the body of Christ, which is their only Church, which is their only Catholic Church. By the way, they are similar to the Pharisees; These confessed that there is a Holy Spirit, but denied that he dwelt in Christ, whose success in casting out demons they attributed to the prince of demons. I omit to say that there are heretics for whom the Holy Spirit is not a creator, but a creature, such as the Arians, Eunomians and Macedonians; or they deny him, affirming that God is not Trinity, but only Father, although sometimes he is called Son and sometimes Holy Spirit, like the Sabellians, whom they call Patripasians, since they say that the Father was crucified; By denying that he has a son, they undoubtedly deny the existence of the Holy Spirit. The Photinians also say that only the Father is God, that the Son is only man, and they deny the existence of a third person, the Holy Spirit. 6. It is, therefore, manifest that both pagans, Jews and heretics blaspheme against the Holy Spirit. It only remains for us, then, that, when writing Whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not have forgiveness eternally, it is applied to the one who does not blaspheme in any way, but in such a way that he never has forgiveness. 15. Thus it was said, God tempts no one; But we must understand that God does not tempt anyone with a certain type of temptation, not universally, otherwise what is written The Lord your God tempts you would be false and we would deny that Christ is God or we would say that the Gospel is false, since we read that He asked a disciple tempting him, although He knew what He was going to do. You know, brothers, that in the invisible and incorruptible Trinity, which the true faith and the Catholic Church maintain and preach, God the Father is not "father" of the Holy Spirit, but of the Son; and God the Son is not "son" of the Holy Spirit, but of the Father; and God the Holy Spirit is not the “spirit” of only the Father or only the Son, but of the Father and the Son 7; and this

Therefore, according to our ability, and as we are allowed to see these things through a mirror and in an enigma, especially to men like us, the origin is presented to us in the Father, in the Son the nativity, in the Holy Spirit of the Father and of the Son the community, and in all three the equality. Thus, what is common to the Father and the Son, they wanted to establish communion between us and with them; By that "gift" they gather us into one, since both have that one, that is, the Holy Spirit, God and gift of God. Through it we reconcile ourselves with divinity and enjoy it. What good would it be for us to know any good if we did not love it? Just as we understand through truth, we love through charity, to know more perfectly and happily enjoy what is known. And charity has been spread in our hearts by the Holy Spirit, who has been donated to us. And since because of sins we were kept from possessing authentic goods, charity covered the multitude of sins. The Father is, therefore, for the Son truth, true origin; the Son is the truth, born of the true Father; and the Holy Spirit is goodness, emanating from the good Father and the good Son; and the three are an equal divinity, inseparable unity. 19. Multi denique, qui uel corde ficto carnem illam manducant et sanguinem bibunt, uel cum manducauerint et biberint apostatae fiunt, numquid manent in Christo aut Christus in eis? Sed profecto est quidam modus manducandi illam carnem et bibendi illum sanguinem, quo moda qui manducauerit et biberit, in Christo manet et Christus in eo. Non ergo quocumque moda quisquam manducauerit carnem Christi et biberit sanguinem Christi, manet in Christo et in illo Christus, sed certo quodam moda; quem modum utique ipse uidebat, quando ista dicebat. Sic igitur et in eo quod ait Qui blasphemauerit in spiritum sanctum, non habet remissionem in aeternum (Mark 3,29), non quocumque moda blasphemauerit, reus est huius irremissibilis delicti, sed moda quodam, quem nos quaerere atque intellegere uoluit, qui hanc sententiam ueram terribilemque deprompsit. 18. Quisnam sit autem iste blasphemandi modus, uel potius immoderatio, quaenam sit ista blasphemia, et quod sit uerbum contra spiritum [82] sanctum, iam, quantum existimo, ipse ordo postulat ut dicamus, uestramque exspectationem tamdiu sed necessario detentam non ulterius differamus. Nostis, carissimi, in illa inuisibili et incorruptibili trinita(454)tc, quam fides uera et catholica ecclesia tenet et praedicat, deum patrem non spiritus sancti patrem esse, sed filíi; et deum filium non spiritus sancti filium esse, sed patris; deum autem spiritum sanctum non solius patris aut solius filii esse spiritum, sed patris et filii; et hanc Clearly. Augustine is a defender of the procession of the Holy Spirit, the Father and the Son, the famous Filiaque, which confronts the Catholic Church with the Orthodox Church.

trinitatem, quamuis seruata singularium proprietate et substantia personarum, tamen, propter ipsam indiuiduam et inseparabilem aeternitatis, ueritatis, bonitotis essentiam uel naturam, non esse tres déos, sed unum deum. Ác per hoc pro captu nostro, quantum ista per speculum et in aenigmate (cf. 1 Cor 13:12), praesertim talibus quales adhuc sumus uidere conceditur, insinuatur nobis in patre auctoritas, in filio natiuitas, in spiritu sancto patris filiique communitas, in tribus aequalitas. Quod ergo commune est patri et filio, per hoc nos uoluerunt habere communionem et inter nos et secum, et per illud donum nos colligere in unum, quod ambo habent unum, hoc est per spiritum sanctum deum et donum dei. In hoc enim reconciliamur diuinitati eaque delectamur. Nam quid nobis prodesset quidquid boni nossemus, nisí etiam diligeremus? [83] Sicut autem ueritate discimus, ita caritate diligimus, ut et plenius cognoscamus et beati cognito perfruamur. Caritas porro diffusa est in cordibus nostris per spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis (cf. Rom 5,5). Et quia peccatis alienabamur a possessione uerorum bonorum, caritas cooperuit multitudinem peccatorum (cf. 1 Petr 4,8). Est ergo pater filio ueritati origo uerax, et filius de ueraci patre orta ueritas, et spiritus sanctus a patre bono et filio bono effusa pretty; omnium est autem non impar diunitas, nec separabilis unitas. 19. Primum ergo in nos ad accipiendam uitam aeternam, quae in

of God, at the beginning of our faith, that gift which is the remission of sins. As long as they subsist, our enmity against God subsists in a certain way, our separation from him, which comes from our evil, since the Scripture does not lie when it says: I heard your sins separate you from God. That is why he does not infuse us with his good things without taking away our evils. And the former grow the more as the latter decrease; and only those are perfect when these disappear. And since Christ the Lord forgives sins in the Holy Spirit, as he casts out demons in the Holy Spirit, we can understand that, when he rose from the dead and said to his disciples Receive the Holy Spirit, he then added: If you forgive anyone's sins, they will be forgiven; and if you retain them, they will be retained. Thus this regeneration, in which the forgiveness of all past sins is carried out, is verified in the Holy Spirit, for the Lord says: If someone is not reborn of water and the Holy Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. But it is one thing to be born from the spirit and another to be nourished by the spirit; as it is one thing to be born of the flesh, which is verified in the mother's birth, and another thing is to be nourished by the flesh, which is verified when the mother breastfeeds the child; For in the same way, whoever converts must drink with delight from the principle from which he was born to live, so that he receives the food to live from the same principle from which he was born. The first benefit of believers, due to the kindness of God, is the remission of sins through the Holy Spirit. Thus began the nouissimo dabitur, de bonitote dei munus uenit ab initio fidei remissio peccatorum. lilis enim manentibus, manent quodammo inimicitiae aduersus deum, et ab illo alienatio, quae a nostro malo est, quoniam non mentitur scriptura say: Peccata uestra separant Ínter uos et deum (Is 59,2). Non itaque nobis ínfert bona sua, nisi mala auferat nostra. Et in tantum illa crescunt, in quantum ista minuuntur; nec illa petficientur, nisi ista finiantur. Iam uero, quod dominus Christus sic in spiritu sancto peccata_ dimittit quemadmodum in spiritu sancto daemones eicit, hinc intellegi potest quod, posteaquam resurrexit a mortuis, cum dixisset discipulis suis Accipite spiritum sanctum (lo 20,22), continuo subiecit: Si cui dimiseritis peccata, dimittentur My; si cui tenueritis, tenebuntur (ib., 23).

Nam et illa tegeneratio, ubi fit omnium praetetitorum remissio pecca[84]torum, in spiritu sancto fit, dicente domino: Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua et spiritu, non potest íntroire in regnum dei (lo 3,5). Be aliud est born of spirit, aliud passi de spiritu; sicut aliud est nasci de carne, quod fit cum partt mater, aliud est pasci de carne, quod fit cum lactat infantem, ad hoc conuersum ut cum uoluptate (455) biberet unde est natus ut uiueret, ut inde accipiat uiuendi alimentum unde nascendi accepit initium. Primum itaque credentium beneficium est benignitatis dei in spiritu sancto remissio peccatorum. Vnde ita coepit et praedicatio Iohannis baptistae, qui praecursor domini missus est. Sic enim scriptum est:

preaching of John the Baptist, sent as a precursor of the Lord. Thus it is written: In those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the desert of Judea, and saying: Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. And also the preaching of the Lord himself, as it reads: Then Jesus began to preach and say: do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. Among the other things that John said to those who came to be baptized by him is this: Indeed, I baptize you with water for repentance; but he who will come after me is more powerful than I, and I am not worthy to wear his shoes; He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire. The Lord also said: John baptized with water; but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit, whom you will receive in a few days, at Pentecost. When John says and fire, it could mean the tribulation that believers were going to suffer for the name of Christ; but it is not strange that the Holy Spirit himself appears designated by the name of fire. And for this reason, at his coming it was said: Different tongues appeared, like fire, and rested on each of them. Therefore the Lord also said: I came to bring fire into the world. The Apostle also says: Boiling in the Spirit, for that is why charity boils: because it is poured into our hearts by the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us. This boiling is opposed by what the Lord said: The charity of many will grow cold. Instead, perfect charity is the perfect gift of the Holy Spirit. But above all In diebus autem Mis uenit lohannes baptista, praedicans in deserto Iudaeae et dices: Paenitentiam agite, appropinquauit enim regnum caelorum (Mt 3:12). Hinc et ipsius domini, quod ita legitur: Exinde coepit Iesus praedicare et dicere: Vaenitentiam agite, appropinquauit enim regnum caelorum (Mt 4:17). Ait autem lohannes, inter cetera quae locutus est ad eos qui uenerunt ut ab illo baptizarentur: Ego quidem uos baptizo aqua in paenitentia; qui autem post me uenturus est, fortior me est, cuius non sum dignus calciamenla portare: ipse uos baptizabit in spiritu sancto et ígni (Mt 3,11). [85] Ait et dominus: lohannes quidem baptizauit aqua; Uos autem spiritu sancto baptizabimini, quem et accepturi eslis non post multos dies (Act 1,5), usque ad Pentecosten.

Quod autem dixit lohannes Et igni (lo 3,5), quamuis possit intellegi et tribulatio, quam pro nomine Christi credentes fuerant perpessuri, tamen non ab re est, eumdem spiritum sanctum etiam nomine ignis significatum uideri. Propter quod et in aduentu eius dictum est: Visae sunt Mis linguae diuisae, uelul ignis, qui et insedit super unumquemque eorum (Act 2,3). Hinc et ipse dominus ait: lgnem ueni mittere in mundum (Luke 12:49). Hinc et apostolus dicit: Spiritu feruentes (Rom 12:11), quoniam hinc feruet caritas. Diffunditur quippe in cordibus nostris per spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis (cf. Rom 5,5). Cui feruori contrarium est, quod dominus ait: Refrigescet caritas multorum (Mt 24:12). Be perfect caritas perfectum est donum spiritus sancti. Prius est autem illud, quod
Sin against the Spirit

There is what concerns the forgiveness of sins; By this benefit we are taken out of the power of darkness, and the prince of this world is cast out by our faith, since he does not work in the children of infidelity with any other force but by the union and bond of sin. And into that Holy Spirit, by which the people of God are gathered together in unity, the prince of this world is cast down, which is divided against itself. 20. Against this free gift, against this grace of God, the impenitent heart speaks. And that same impenitence is the spirit of blasphemy, which is not forgiven either in this century or in the future. Because he pronounces a very bad and too impious word against the Holy Spirit, in which those whose sins are all forgiven are baptized, that spirit that the Church receives so that the sins of the one to whom she will forgive them may be forgiven; and he pronounces it now with his thought, now also with his tongue; Although the patience of God calls for penitence, because of the hardness of his heart, because of his impenitent heart, he stores up wrath for the day of wrath and the revelation of God's just judgment, which will repay each person according to their works. With this special name of impenitence we can designate in some way the blasphemy and word against the Holy Spirit, which will never be forgiven. Against this impenitence the crier and the judge cried out, saying: Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand; against her the Lord opened the mouth of evangelical preaching, against her he announced that

He would preach the Gospel throughout the earth, saying to his disciples, after rising from the dead: It was fitting that Christ should die and rise from the dead on the third day and that repentance and forgiveness of sins should be preached in his name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. Such impenitence does not admit of remission either in this century or in the future, since it is penance that obtains in this century the forgiveness that is valid in the future. 21. This impenitence or impenitent heart cannot be judged while a subject lives in this flesh. There is no need to despair of anyone while God's patience invites penitence; He does not snatch the wicked from this life, since He does not want the death of the sinner, but rather that he convert and live. Today it is pagan; How do you know if tomorrow he won't be a Christian? Today he is an unfaithful Jew, what if tomorrow he believed in Christ? Today he is a heretic, what if tomorrow he adheres to the Catholic truth? Today he is schismatic, what if tomorrow he embraces Catholic peace? What if those whom you point out in any kind of error and that you condemn as desperate cases, do penance before ending this life and find true life? Therefore, brothers, let what the Apostle says serve as a warning: Do not judge anything before its time. This blasphemy of the spirit, which does not admit forgiveness and which we have said is not universal, but determined, and which we have characterized, or discovered, or shown, in my opinion, as the persevering hardness of an impenitent heart, cannot be verified in any subject in this life, as we have said.

ad remissionem pertinet peccatorum: per quod beneficium eruimur de potestate tenebrarum (cf. Col 1,13), et princeps huius mundi mittitur foras fide nostra (cf. lo 12,31), qui operatur in filiis infidelitatis (cf. Eph 2,2) nulla ui alia nisi societate et obligatione peccati. In spiritu enim sancto, quo in unum dei populus congregationtur, eicitur spiritus immundus, qui in se ipsum diuiditui. [86] 20. Contra hoc donum gratuitum, contra istam dei gratiam loquitur cor impaenitens. Ipsa ergo impaenitentia est spiritus blasphemiae, quae non remittetur ñeque in hoc saeculo ñeque in the future. Contra spiritum enim sanctum, quo baptizantur quorum peccata omnia dimittuntur, et quem accepit ecclesia, ut cuí dimiserit peccata dimittantur ei, uerbum ualde malum et nimís impium siue cogitatione siue etiam lingua sua dicit, quem patientía dei, (456) cum ad paenitentiam adducat, ipse secundum duritiam cordis sui et cor impaenitens thesaurizat sibi iram in die irae et reuelationis iusti iudicii dei, qui reddet unicuique secundum opera eius (cf. Rom 2:4-6). Haec ergo impaenitentia—sic enim uno aliquo nomine possumus utcumque appellare et blasphemiam et uerbum contra spiritum sanctum quod remissionem non habet in aeternum—haec, inquam, impaenitentia, contra quam clamabat et praeco et iudex, dicentes Paenitentiam agite, appropinquauit enim regnum caelorum (Mt 3,2; 4,17), contra quam dominus os euangelicae praedicationis aperuit, et contra quam ipsum euangelium in toto orbe praedicandum esse praedixit, ubi postea quam resurrexit a mortuis ait discipulis Oportebat Christum pati,

et resurgere a mortuis tertio die, et praedicari [87] in nomine eius paenu tentiam et remissionem peccatorum per omnes gentes, incipientibus ab Hierusalem (Luke 24,46-47), haec omnino impaenitentia non habet remissionem, ñeque in hoc saeculo ñeque infuture: quia paenitentia ímpetrat remissionem in hoc saeculo, quae ualeat in the future. 21. Sed ista impaenitentia, uel cor impaenitens, quamdíu quisque in hac carne uiuit, non potest judicari. De millo enim desperandum est, quamdiu patientia dei ad paenitentiam adducit (cf. Rom 2,4); nec de hac uita rapit impium, qui non uult mortem impii quantum ut reuertatur et uiuat (cf. Ezek 33:11). Paganus est hodie: unde seis, utrum sit futurus crastíno christianus? Iudaeus infidelis est hodie: what if you were credat in Christo? Haeteticus est hodie: what if you were sequitur catholicam ueritatem? Schismaticus est hodie: what if you were amplectitur cathoHcam pacem? Quid, si isti quos in quocumque generate erroris notes et tamquam desperatissimos damnas, ante quam finiant istam uitam, agunt paenitentiam et inueniunt ueram uitam? Proinde, fratres, etiam ad hoc uos admoneat quod ait apostolus: Nolite ante tempus quidquam iudicare (1 Cor 4,5). Haec enim blasphemia spiritus, cui numquam est ulla remíssio, quam non omnem sed quamdam intellegimus, eamque perseuerantem duritian cordis impaenitentis uel diximus uel inuenimus uel etiam quantum existi[88]mamus ostendimus, non potest in quoquam, ut diximus, dum adhuc in hac uita est, deprehendi.

22. And do not think it absurd that, while a subject perseveres to the end of his life in hard impenitence and does not cease to speak against this grace of the Holy Spirit, the Gospel is content to call "word", as if it were a passing thing, that long contradiction of the impenitent heart: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of man, it will be forgiven him; But whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will have no forgiveness either in this age or in the future. Although this blasphemy is prolix and long with many words, Scripture also usually calls those many words "word." No prophet spoke only one word and yet it reads like this: Word that was addressed to this or the other prophet. And the Apostle says: Let the priests be honored with a double honor, especially those who work in the word and doctrine. It does not say "in the words", but in the word. And James says: Be doers of the word and not just listeners. Nor does he say "of the words," but of the word, although there are so many words of Holy Scripture that are recited, read, and heard publicly and solemnly in the Church. No matter how much time one of us spends preaching the Gospel and no matter how much time one of you listens diligently and fervently to our preaching, he is not called a "preacher of words," but of the word, or a diligent hearer of words, but of the word. According to that way of speaking of Scripture, known from ecclesiastical custom, whoever throughout the life he spends in

this meat, no matter how long it lasts; Whatever words he says with his thoughts or even with his mouth, with an impenitent heart and against the forgiveness of sins that is granted in the Church, he speaks against the Holy Spirit. 23. Therefore, not only the word that is said against the Son of man, but every sin or blasphemy will be forgiven to men, for as long as there is no sin of the impenitent heart against the Holy Spirit, through whom sins are forgiven in the Church, all others are forgiven. But how is he going to forgive himself who prevents the forgiveness of others as well? They are all forgiven, then, as long as the one who will never be forgiven is not among them. If he is among them, since he is not forgiven, neither are the others, since the remission of all is prevented by his bond. Let it not be said, then, that whoever says a word against the Son of Man is forgiven, and that whoever says it against the Holy Spirit is not forgiven, because in the Trinity the Holy Spirit is greater than the Son: none of the heretics ever said that; What happens is that he who resists the truth and blasphemes against it, which is Christ, even after so long preaching among men, since the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and this is the Son of man, Christ himself, does not utter that word of the impenitent heart against the Holy Spirit, of which it was said: Whoever is not reborn of water and

22. Quod non ideo uideatur absurdum, quia cum homo usque in fínem huius uitae in dura impaenitentia perseuerans diu multumque loquatur aduersus hanc gratiam spiritus sancti, euangelium tamen tam longam contradictionem cordis impaenitentis quasi breue aliquid Verbum appellauít dices: Quicumque dixerit uerbum contra filium hominis, remittetur ei; qui autem dixerit contra spiritum sanctum, non remittetur ei, ñeque in hoc saeculo ñeque in future (Mark 3,29; Luke 12,10). Haec enim quamuis prolixa sit et plurímis uerbis contexta et produc blasphemia, solet tamen scriptura etiam fines uerba Verbum appellare. Ñeque enim unutn uetbum locutus est quicumque propheta, et tamen sic legitur: Verbum quod factum est ad «illum uel iilum prophetam» (passim ín proph.). Et apostolus: Presby(457)teri, inquit, duplici honore bonorentur, máxime qui laborant in uerbo et doctrina (1 Tim 5,17). Non ait «in uerbis», sed In uerbo. Et sanctus Iacobus: Estote, inquit, factors uerbi, et non auditores tantum (Iac 1,22). Non ait et ipse «uerborum», sed Verbi, quamuis tam fines uerba de scripturis sanctis in ecclesia celebriter et sollemniter legantur, dicantur, audiantur. Sicut ergo, quantocumque tempore quisquís nostrum in praedicando euangelio laborauerit, non «uerborum» sed «uerbi» dicitur praedicator, et quantocumque tempore quisque uestrum nostram praedicationem diligenter atque instantor audierit, non uerborum sed uerbi audiendi T89] studiosissimus nuncupatur: ita, eo more quo scripturae loquuntur et quero nouit eccle-

siastica consuetudo, quisquís uniuersa sua uita, qua istam gerit carnem, quantalibet longitudine ptotendatur, quaecumque uerba uel ore uel sola cogitatione locutus fuerit corde impaenitenti contra remissionem peccatorum quae fit in ecclesia, uerbum dicit contra spiritum sanctum. 23. Ideo autem non solum uerbum quod dictum fuerit contra filium hominis, sed omne prorsus peccatum et blasphemia remittetur hominibus, quia ubi hoc peccatum non fuerit cordis impaenitentis contra spiritum sanctum, quo in ecclesia peccata soluuntur, cuneta alia dimittuntur. Quomodo autem hoc dimittetur, quod etiam remissionem impedit aliorum? Omnia ergo dimittuntur eis, in quibus hoc non est quod numquam dimittitur; in quibus est autem, quoniam hoc numquam dimittitur, nec alia dimittuntur: quia omnium remissio uinculo istius impeditur. Non ergo propterea quicumque dixerit uerbum contra filium hominis, remittetur ei, qui autem dixerit contra spiritum sanctum, non remittetur, quia in trinitate maior est filio spiritus sanctus, quod nullus umquam uel haereticus dixit; sed quoniam quisquís restiterit ueritati et blasphemauerit ueritatem, quod est Christus, etiam post tantam sui praedicationem apud homines, ut uerbum caro firet et habitaret in nobis (cf. lo 1,14), quod est filius hominis, idem ipse Christus, si non dixerit uerbum illud cordis impaenitentis contra spiritum sanctum, de quo dictum est Qui non renatus fuerit ex aqua et spiritu (lo 3,5), et de [90] quo

Holy Spirit, and of whom it was also said: Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you forgive, they will be forgiven. This means that if he repents, he will receive through this gift the remission of all sins, and also of the word he has spoken against the Son of Man. Because to the sin of ignorance or contumacy or any other blasphemy, he did not add the sin of impenitence against the gift of God and the grace of regeneration and reconciliation, which is verified in the Church through the Holy Spirit. 24. Nor should we accept what some think, namely, that the word against the Son of man is forgiven, but not that which is said against the Holy Spirit, because Christ became the Son of man by assuming the flesh, and greater than this is undoubtedly the Holy Spirit, who by his own substance is equal to the Father and the Only Begotten Son according to his divinity, since according to this also the Only Begotten Son is equal to the Father and the Holy Spirit. If the text referred to that, it would not mention any other blasphemy, and only that which is said against the Son of man would be pardonable, as if thinking that he is only a man. But he began by saying: All sin and blasphemy will be forgiven to men, which is confirmed by the other evangelist, who says: All sins and blasphemies that they utter will be forgiven to the children of men. The blasphemy that is said against the Father is thus included in that generality; and forgiveness is only denied to that which is said against the Holy Spirit. Did the Father assume the form of a servant, item dictum est Acápite spiritum sanctum: si cui áimiseritis peccata, dimittuntur ei (lo 20,22-23), id est «si paenituerit eum, accipiet per hoc donum remissionem omnium peccatorum», simul et huius quod uerbum dixit contra filium hominis: quia peccato ignorantiae siue contumaciae uel cuiuscumque blasphemiae non addidít peccatum irnpaenitentiae contra donum dei et gratiam regenerationis uel reconciliationís, quae fit in ecclesia spiritu sancto. 24. Proinde nec illud sentiendum est, quod (458) quidam putant, ideo remitti uerbum quod dicitur contra filium hominis, non remitti autem quod dicitur contra spiritum sanctum: quia propter susceptam carnem factus est filius hominis Cbristus, qua carne utique maior est spiritus sanctus, qui substantia propria aequalís est patri et unigénito filio secundum eius diuinitatem, secundum quam et ipse unigenitus filius aequalís est patri et spiritui sancto.

Nam si hoc propterea dictum esset, proferto de omni cetera blasphemia taceretur, haec sola remissibilis uideretur, quae contra filium hominis dicitur, quasi cum homo solus putatur. Cum uero praemissum sit Omne peccatum et blasphemia remittetur hominibus—quod etiam apud alium euangelistam ita positum est: Omnia dimittentur filiis hominum peccata et blasphemiae, quibus blasphemauerint (Mark 3,28)—procul dubio et illa blasphemia quae contra patrem [91] dicitur, ista generalitate concluditur: et tamen haec sola irremissibilis definitur, quae dicitur contra spiritum sanctum. Numquidnam et
Sin against the Spirit

in which he would be inferior to the Holy Spirit? In no way. Therefore, after the general mention of all sins and all blasphemies, he wanted to strongly announce the blasphemy that is said against the Son of man. Men are guilty of this sin, and he mentioned it when he said: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; The Gospel according to John shows that this sin is very serious; when speaking of the Holy Spirit that he promised to send: He will accuse the world of sin, of righteousness and of judgment; of sin, because they did not believe in me. And, nevertheless, if that hardness of the impenitent heart has not said the "word against the Holy Spirit", what he says against the Son of Man will also be forgiven. 25. Perhaps someone will ask if it is only the Holy Spirit who forgives, and not the Father and the Son. We answer that the Father and the Son also forgive, since the Son says of the Father: If you forgive men's sins, your Father will forgive yours. And in the Sunday prayer we say to Him: Our Father, who art in heaven, and among other things we ask Him for this saying: Forgive us our debts. And he said of himself: And that you may know that the Chosen of man has power to forgive sins on earth. But you will tell me: «If the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit forgive sins, why is it said that this impenitence, which is never forgiven, belongs only to the blasphemy of the pater formam serui accepit, qua sit maior spiritus sanctus? Don't utique. Sed ideo post uniuersalem commemorationem omnium peccatorum omnisque blasphemiae eminentius uoluit exprimere blasphemiam quae dicitur contra filium hominis: quia, etiam si in illo peccato fuerint nomines obligati, quod commemorauit ubi ait Si non uenissem et locutus eis Fuissem, peccatum non haberent (lo 15,22)—quod etiam in euangelio secundum Iohannem ualde graue otendit esse peccatum, ubi ait de ipso spiritu sancto, cum eum se missurum esse promitteret: Ule arguet mundum de peccato, et de iustitia, et de indica; de peccato quidem, quod non crediderunt in me (lo 16,8-9)—tamen, si non dixerit illa cordis impaenitentis duritia uerbum contra spiritum sanctum, etiam hoc quod dictum est contra filium hominis remittetur. 25. Hic fortassis aliquis quaerat, utrum tantummodo spiritus sanctus peccata dimittat, an et pater et filius. Respondemus, quod et pater et filius.

Ipse enim filius de patre dicit: Si dimiseritis peccata hominibus, dimittet uobis et pater uester peccata uestra (Mt 6:14). Cui nos quoque dicimus in oratione dominica: Pater noster, qui es in caelis (ib., 9), atque inter cetera et hoc petimus dicentes: Dimitte nobis debita nostra (Mt 9,6). Those who possess the right faith and those who understand it as far as they can know very well that it is said of the Father that He does the works, because he is the origin of the works, inasmuch as he is the origin of the existence of the collaborating Persons, since the Son was born from Him and the Holy Spirit proceeds mainly from him, from whom the Son was born and with whom he has the Spirit in common. in them, but to the men who read those many miracles, and that none of them are performed except by the Son; In the same way, when the Apostle says about the Holy Spirit: All these things are done by one and the same Spirit, he does not speak as if the Father and the Son did not cooperate, but because in such works there are not many Spirits, but only one, and in these various operations he is not different from himself. 27. It was not therefore said in vain, but rationally and truthfully, that it was the Father, not the Son or the Holy Spirit, who said: You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. But we also do not deny that this miracle of the word that sounded from heaven, although it belonged only to the person of the Father, was verified by the cooperation of the Son and the Holy Spirit. Not because the Son, assuming flesh, was living with men on earth, did he cease to be in the bosom of the Father as the Only Begotten Word, when that voice from the cloud occurred. It cannot be wisely and spiritually believed that God the Father has separated the operation of his sounding and passing words from the cooperation of his Wisdom and Spirit. In the same way, when we say with all rightness that the Son, not the Father nor the Holy Spirit, walked on the sea, since his alone were the flesh and the feet that walked on the waves, who doubts that the Father and the Holy Spirit cooperated in the performance of so great a miracle? Thus we say with all truth that only the Son took the flesh, not the Father nor the Holy Spirit; However, he who denies that the Father and the

Holy Spirit cooperated in that same incarnation that belongs to only the Son. And in the same way we say that the Holy Spirit, not the Father or the Son, appeared in the form of a dove and in tongues like fire and granted those upon whom he came to proclaim in many and varied languages ​​the wonders of God; but in this miracle, although it belongs only to the Holy Spirit, we cannot separate the cooperation of the Father and the Only Begotten Word. Thus, in the Trinity, the Trinity works the works of each person; When one works, the other two cooperate, for a convenient operational harmony in all three, although operational efficiency is deficient in none of them. This being so, the phrase that the Lord Jesus casts out demons in the Holy Spirit is explained. It is not that he could not accomplish it alone, as if, not being sufficient on his own for such an undertaking, he sought such help from the Spirit; but it was fitting that the spirit divided in itself should be expelled through that Spirit which the Father and the Son, not divided in themselves, have in common among themselves. 28. In the same way, since sins are not forgiven outside the Church, it was appropriate that they be forgiven through that Spirit who brings the Church together in unity. Finally, if anyone repents of his sins outside the Church, but has an impenitent heart regarding that great sin for which he is a stranger to the Church of God, what good will that repentance do him? like those of whom the Apostle says: They have the form of piety, but they deny its virtuality. The visible form of the branch can occur even outside the vine, but invisible life cannot have roots except in the vine. Thus, the corporal sacraments, which are also carried and celebrated by those who have separated themselves from the unity of the Body of Christ, can show a form of piety; but the virtuality of invisible and spiritual piety cannot occur in them, just as sensation no longer accompanies the human organ when it has been amputated from the body. 33. This being so, since the remission of sins does not occur except in the Holy Spirit, it can only occur in that Church that has the Holy Spirit. This is verified in the remission of sins, so that the prince of sin, that spirit that is divided against itself, does not reign in us, so that, freed from the power of the unclean spirit, we then become temples of the Holy Spirit, who cleanses us by giving us forgiveness, and we receive that guest to act, increase and perfect justice. At his first coming, when those who received him spoke all the languages ​​of the nations, and the apostle Peter spoke to the stupefied curious who had come, they were distressed and said to Peter and the apostles: What shall we do then, brothers? Tell us. And Peter said to them: Do penance and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. In

In the Church both things were accomplished, that is, the remission of sins and the reception of that gift; The Holy Spirit was given in her. And they were baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, for he had promised that Holy Spirit, saying: Whom the Father will send in my name. For the Holy Spirit does not dwell in anyone without the Father and the Son, nor does the Son without the Father and the Holy Spirit, nor the Father without the other two. Inhabitation is inseparable, since its operation is inseparable. But, in general, they appear separated, due to the way of meaning of the creatures, not in their substance. This is how the words are pronounced, and the syllables separately occupy their temporal spaces, without being separated from themselves by intervals or moments of time. They cannot all be pronounced at once, but they cannot exist except all together. As we have already repeated, since in the remission of sins the kingdom of the spirit divided within itself is destroyed and eliminated, the society of unity of the Church of God, outside of which the remission of sins does not occur, is as it were the proper work of the Holy Spirit; but the Father and the Son cooperate, since the Holy Spirit is in a certain way the partnership of the Father and the Son. According to Luke, this is not said where the Lord responds to those who said that he cast out demons by the prince of demons, namely, that he who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit is not forgiven. forgiven men in this congregation that Christ gathers in the Holy Spirit, never divided against himself. But if the blasphemy against the Spirit, which is pronounced in the impenitent heart and opposes this great gift of God, continues until the end of life, it will not be forgiven. If anyone is so contrary to unity that he opposes God who speaks, not in prophecy, but in his only Son—since he wanted him to be the Son of man for us, to speak to us in him—he will be forgiven; It is enough that through penitence he be converted to the kindness of God, who, not wanting the death of the wicked, but rather that he should be converted and live, gave his Church the Holy Spirit, so that whoever's sins he forgives in him may remain forgiven. On the other hand, whoever declares himself an enemy of this gift in such a way that he does not ask for it with his penance, but contradicts it with his impenitence, keeps not just any sin insolvent, but the very remission of sins that is disdained or fought against. Thus, a word is spoken against the Holy Spirit when one does not come from the dispersion to the congregation, which received the Holy Spirit to forgive sins. If someone comes with a sincere heart to this congregation, even if he encounters a bad, reprobate and false clergyman, as long as he is a Catholic minister, he receives the remission of sins in the Holy Spirit. This Spirit works in the holy Church, even in this time in which, as in a threshing floor, it is crushed with chaff, so that it does not disdain an authentic confession from anyone, it is not deceived by anyone's simulation and it eliminates the reprobates,

while through their ministry he gathers the honest. The only remedy so that blasphemy is not irremissible is to avoid the impenitent heart. And let us believe that penance is only beneficial when the Church is accepted, in which the remission of sins is given and the society of the spirit is maintained in the bond of peace. 38. I have explained as best I could, if I could, a very difficult question for the mercy and help of the Lord. What I have not been able to explain in such difficulty is not imputed to the truth itself, which serves healthily as an exercise for the pious even when it is hidden, but to my deficiency, if I have not been able to see what was necessary or explain what I have seen. And from what I have been able to investigate by thinking, or explain by speaking, let us give thanks to Him from whom we seek, to whom we ask and to whom we call to have something to feed ourselves by meditating and to serve you by speaking.

De bis autem, quae forte potuimus et cogitando uestigare et expediré dicendo, illi sunt agendae gratiae a quo quaesiuimus, a quo petiuimus, ad quem (467) pulsauimus, ut haberemus unde et nos meditando alerentur et uobis loquendo ministraremus.

Topic: The tree and its fruit (Mt 12:33). Place: Carthage. Date: Between July 17 and August 10 of the year 397. 1. Our Lord Jesus Christ commissioned us to be good trees so that we can bear good fruit, saying: Make a good tree and its fruit will be good; or a bad tree and its fruit will be bad; because the tree is known by the fruit. When he says make a good tree and its fruit will be good, he does not give advice, but rather a healthy precept, to which necessary obedience is due. And when he says make a bad tree and its fruit will be bad, he does not give a precept for you to do it, but a warning for you to avoid it. Because he spoke against those who, being evil, believed they could say or do good things. That, says the Lord Jesus, is not possible. First you have to change the man, so that the works can be changed. If man remains evil, he cannot produce good works, and if he continues to be good, he cannot produce evil works. 2. Where is Isaac? where Jacob? quorum Dominum se dici uoluit, et cuius omnes gentes erant, quasi trium hominum deus esset, et: Ego sum, inquit, Deus Abraham et Isaac et Iacob (Ex 3,6). Sit ergo unusquisque arbor bcna. Non se arbitretur habere fructus bonds, si manet arbor mala. Non erit fructus bonus, nisi arboris bonae. Muta cor, et mutabitur opus. 5. Let us then discern these goods, if we can, since we speak of good trees. For if man is devoid of superior goods, why does he covet external goods? Consider: what good is an ark full of goods if the conscience is empty? Do you want to have goods, and don't you want to be good? Don't you see that you should be ashamed of your goods if your house is full of them and only you are bad? Or if scires quid est bonum! Quod habere uis, non est ualde bonum. Quod esse non uis, hoc est bonum! Vis enim habere sanitatem corporis: est bonum; nec tamen putes magnum bonum esse, quod habet et malus. Aurum et argentum habere uis; ecce et hoc dico: bonum est: sed si bene usus fueris; bene autem non uteris, si malus fueris. Ac per hoc aurum et argentum malis malum est, bonis bonum est: non quia eos bonds facit aurum et argentum, sed, quia eos bonds inuenit, in usum bonum conuertitur. Honorem habere uis: bonum est; sed et hoc si bene utaris. Quam multis honor occasio exitii Fuit! Quam multis honor ministerium boni operis Fuit! 5. Discernamus ergo bona ista, si possumus: quia de bonis arboribus loquimur. Et hic nihil est, quod sic quisque cogitare debeat, nisi ut in semetipsum oculos conuertat, in se discat, se discutiat, se inspiciat, se quaerat, et se inueniat; et quod displicet, necet; quod placet, aptet et plantet. (469) Cum enim se homo inanem inuenerit meliorum bonorum, ut quid est auidus exteriorum bonorum? Ecce, quid prodest plena bonis arca, si est inanis conscientia? Nihil omnino: non uxorem, non filium, non filiam, non seruum, non ancillam, non uillam, non tunicam, postremo non caligam; et tamen

the slave, nor the property, nor the tunic, nor even the shoes. And yet you want to lead a bad life. Please put your life before your shoes. All the elegant and neat things that you have in sight are expensive to you. And you are vile and ugly for yourself! Perhaps someone, admonished and even repentant by these words of mine, asks what good is, what good is and where good comes from. You understood well that that is what you should ask. If I possent tibi I will answer bona, quibus plena domus tua est, quae habere optati, quae will lose timuisti, nonne tibi clamarent: «Sicut tu nos bona uis habere, sic et nos uolumus bonum habere dominum»? Tacita uoce interpellant contra te Dominum tuum: «Ecce bona tanta dedisti huic, et ipse malus est! "Quid eí prodest quod habet, quando eum qui omnia dedit non habet?" 6. Quaerit ergo aliquis, admonitus his uerbis meis, et forte compunctus, quaerit quid sit bonum, quale bonum, unde bonum. Bene intellexisti hoc te quaerere debené. I respond quaerenti, et dicam: «Hoc est bonum, quod non potes inuitus amittere.

Potes enim aurum will lose, et nolens: potes domum, potes honores, potes ipsam carnis salutem: bonum uero, quo uere bonus es, nec inuitus accipis, nec inuitus amittis. Quaero ergo quale sit hoc bonum. Psalmus quidem adrnonet nos rem magnam, forte quam quaeiimus. Ait enim: Filii hominum, quousque granes corde? (Ps 4,3). What arbor illa in triennio? Iam clamat ueritas, et adhuc quaeritur uanitas! What graues corde? 1. Merit fortiter flagellatur hic mundus: cognouit enim iam uerba Domini mundus: Et seruus, inquit, nesciens uoluntatem domini sui, et faciens dignified plagis, uapulabit paucis (Luke 12:48). Quare? Vt quaerat uoluntatem domini sui. Seruus ergo nesciens uoluntatem: hoc erat mundus, antequam magnificaret Dominus sanctum suum: seruus erat nesciens uoluntatem domini sui; et ideo uapulabat paucis.

1. A text of the holy Gospel has been read to us, my brothers. If we want to explain everything, there will barely be enough time for each point; How much less for everyone! The Savior himself showed that the prophet Jonah, thrown into the sea and swallowed in the belly by a sea monster and vomited up alive on the third day, is a figure of the Savior himself. The Jewish people were denounced by comparison with the Ninevites, because when the prophet Jonah was sent to them to punish them, they did penance, appeased God's anger and deserved mercy. So he said: And here is one who is greater than Jonah, referring to himself. The Ninevites heard the servant and corrected their ways; The Jews heard the Lord, and not only did they not correct themselves, but they also murdered him. Therefore he said: The queen of the south will rise in judgment against this generation and condemn it; for he came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and here is one who is greater than Solomon. Ionam prophetam, qui deiectus in mare beluae marinae uterus exceptus est, et die tertia vivus evomitus, figuram gessisse salvatoris, qui passus est et die tertio resurrexit, ipse salvator ostendit. 156 Christus. Audierunt illi servum, et vias suas correxerunt; audierunt isti dominum, et non solum se non correxerunt, sed insuper illum occiderunt. Solomon; He was Lord and they were servants. But what would those who despised the present Lord be like, when strangers listened to his servants? 2. Then he continues: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it wanders through arid places in search of refuge and does not find it. Then he says: I will return to my house, from which I left; and arriving, he finds it free, clean of obstacles and prepared; then he goes and taking with him seven other spirits worse than him, they enter and settle in it: and the last moments of man are worse than the antecedents; This is what will happen to this terrible generation. To understand this, it will take a long time, if it is explained sufficiently. However, I will touch on it briefly, as soon as the Lord allows me, so as not to leave you in the dark about the intelligence of the text. When the remission of sins is given in the sacraments, the house is cleansed; but it is necessary that the Holy Spirit dwell, who dwells only in the humble of heart. The Lord says: On whom will my Spirit rest? And it answers the purpose: About the humble and quiet, and who fears my words. When the Spirit dwells, fills, governs, works, restrains evil, excites good, makes justice gentle, so that man does good for the love of righteousness, not for fear of punishment. Man by himself is not totally suitable to execute all that I have said. But if he has the Holy Spirit as a guest, he finds him as an assistant in every good work. On the other hand, the proud, if when their sins are forgiven they presume to be tamen quales sunt, qui praesentem dominum contempserunt, quando alienigenae servos eius audierunt? 2. Deinde sequitur: Cum autem spiritus immundus exierit ab homine, ambulat per loca arida quaerens requiem, et non invenit. Tune dicit: revertar in domum (933) meam, unde exivi. Hoc ut intellegatur, si congruenter exponatur, multum sermo immorabitur: breviter tamen attingam, quantum dominus donat, ne vos ab huius rei intellectu ieiunos dimittam. When fit in sacramentis remissio peccatorum, mundatur domus; sed habitator est necessarius Spiritus sanctus: Spiritus autem sanctus non habitat nisi humiles corde. that to live well the free will of the human will is enough, because of their pride they cast out the Holy Spirit 1: the house was clean of sins, but empty of all good. Your sins were forgiven, you lacked evil; but only the Holy Spirit will fill you with good things, and your pride rejects him. You brag about yourself and he leaves you; you trust yourself, you give yourself. But cupidity, for which you were evil, and which was expelled from man, from your mind, when your sins were forgiven, wanders through the wastes seeking refuge; Finding no refuge, Cupidity returns to the house, finds it clean, and brings with it seven other spirits worse than her; and that man's consequences are worse than his antecedents. He brings with him seven others. What does Seven Others mean? Is the unclean spirit also septenary? What does that mean? The number seven indicates the universal. Whole he had gone, whole he returns, and I wish he came alone! What does Bring another seven with you mean? Those that he did not have when he was bad, he will have when he is falsely good. Pay attention, and you will help me, as much as I can, to explain what I am saying. The Holy Spirit is recommended for his septenary operation, since he is in us the spirit of wisdom and understanding, counsel and strength, knowledge and piety and fear of God. To this septenary you can well oppose a septenary opposite evil: spirit of stupidity and error, spirit of recklessness and cowardice, spirit of ignorance and impiety, and spirit of pride against the fear of God. These are the seven evildoers. Which seven still libero humanoe voluntatis arbitrio, [157] ipsa superbia a se excludunt Spiritum sanctum; et remanet sleep quasi mundata a peccatis, sed inanis omnibus bonis. Dimissa sunt peccata tua, caruisti malis; sed non te nisi Spiritus sanctus implebit bonis. Hunc repellit superbia. Praesumis de te, dimittit te; Confidis tibi, donaris tibi. Sed illa cupiditas, qua malus eras, repulsa ab homine, hoc est a mente tua, quando remissa sunt peccata tua, vagatur per deserta quaerens requiem; et non inveniens requiem redit ad domum illa cupiditas, invenit mundatam, adducit secum alios spiritus septem nequiores se; et erunt peiora hominis illius novissima, quam erant prima. Septem alios adducit secum. What is it, alios septem? Ergo et ipse immundus spiritus septenarius est? Quid est hoc? Per septem universitas significatur. Totus ierat, totus venit; et utinam solus vinoet!

Quid est, adducit secum alios septem? Quos non habebat, quando erat malus, habebit alios false bonus. Intendite, ut, si possum, quantum adiuvor, explanem quod dico. Huic septenario bono constitutes a contrary septenarium malum: spiritum stultitiae et erroris, spiritum temeritatis et ignaviae, spiritum ignorantiae et impietatis, et spiritum superbiae contra timorem dei.

worse? I just wanted to talk about this; but since I did not want to ignore the above, I think I have consumed no small amount of time. more mother, since she offered her fertility without taking away her integrity, her virgin mother when she conceived, when she gave birth, a virgin perpetually? How could he do without the father? Sed noluit hominem habere patrem, ne per concupiscentiam carnalem vinoet ad homines; voluit tamen matrem, ut matrem haberet inter homines, quam pro dei opere contemnendo doceret homines. Etenim antiquitus et femina peccaverat, et viro peccatum propinaverat; utrumque coniugium diaboli fraud deceptum est. Si vendeet Christus vir non cum feminei sexus commendatione, despair of se feminae, maxime quia

nes, since Christ deigned to be male; Do not despair, women, for Christ deigned to be born of a woman. Both sexes concur in the salvation brought by Christ: come the man, come the woman; In faith there is no male or female. Christ teaches you to despise your parents and love your parents. Because then you love them orderly and piously, when you don't put them before God. These are the words of the Lord: Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. It seems as if with these words he is encouraging you not to love them; but, if you listen, he exhorts you to love them. He could have said: he who loves his father or his mother is not worthy of me. But he did not say this so as not to speak against the law which he gave, for he gave it through his servant Moses, and in it it is written: Honor your father and your mother. Therefore, he does not now promulgate a contrary law, but recommends the old one; It tells you the order, it does not take away your pity, by saying: Whoever loves his father or his mother, but more than me. Love them, then, but not more than me. God is God and man is man. Love parents, respect them, honor them; But if God calls you to a higher enterprise, in which the affection of parents may be an impediment, keep order, do not break charity. 5. Given so much truth of the doctrine of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, who will believe that the Manichaeans dared to seek slander, trying to affirm that the Lord Jesus Christ had no mother? They know this, or rather they resent it: that the Lord Jesus did not have a human mother, against the Gospel, against the light of

same truth. And see how they argue: Didn't he say it himself? So what did he say? Who is my mother or who are my brothers? He denies, they say, and you want to impose on us what he denies. He says: Who is my mother or who are my brothers? You deny that Christ had a mother and you try to prove what you want, because he said: Who is my mother or who are my brothers? If someone comes and tells you that the Lord Christ did not say that at all, how will you convince him? Answer, if you can, the man who denies that Christ said that. With what you convince him, you will be convinced. Has Christ himself whispered in your ear that he said that? Answer so that he is convinced with your answer, answer and show that Christ said it. I know what you are going to say: I am going to take the codex, I will open the Gospel, I will recite to you the words written in the holy Gospel. Good, good; With that Gospel I will catch you, with that Gospel I will tie you and with that Gospel I will strangle you. Recite what in your opinion favors you, open, read: Who is my mother? Read before why he said that; Someone announced to him: Behold, your mother and your brothers are outside. I haven't squeezed you yet, I haven't had you yet, I haven't strangled you yet; you can still say that the message was false and not true; and that he told a lie and that is why the Lord refuted a false message. In fact, upon giving him the message, he responded: Who is my mother? As if to say: you say my mother is away and I say, who is my mother?

per illam lapsus est homo: utrumque honoravit, utrumque commendavit, utrumque suscepit. De femina natus est. Nolite desperare, viri: vir esse dignitatus est Christus. If you try to convince me that the Lord said: Who is my mother? because the evangelist affirms that he said it, you will not convince me that the Lord said it, if you do not believe the evangelist. What does Who is my mother mean then? I ask that question too. Who is my mother? Suppose that a ut cita vincaris. Attende, inspice, lege. Video te nolle. Da codicem, ego layman: haec eo loquente ad turbas. Quis hoc dicit? Evangelist, cui si non credis, nihil Christus dixit. Si nihil Christus dixit, quae est mater mea? Christus non dixit. Si autem quae est mater mea? Christus dixit, verum est (937) quod evangelista scripsit.
