Absit! intellege: non negavit, sed aliquid quod faciebat matri praeposuit. Postremo sola causa est, quaerere quare dominus dixerit quae est mater mea? Prima causa est, videre quod habuerit de quo diceret quae est mater mea? Habuit: foris stabat, loqui cum eo volebat. Dec mihi, one of six? Evangelista dicit, cui si non credidero, nihil dominus dicit. Ergo habuit matrem. Sed quid est, quae est mater mea? Ad ista, quae ego fació, quae est mater mea? If you say alicui periclitanti,

someone who is in danger and has a father, you say to him: May your father save you!, when he knows that his father is not in a position to save him; Will he not reply to you with utmost pity and complete truth: Who is my father? For this thing that I want, for this thing that I feel I need, what does my father have to do with it? Well, for what Christ was doing: releasing the prisoners, enlightening blind minds, building inner men, building a spiritual temple, what did his mother mean? If you believe that Christ had no mother on earth because he said: Who is my mother?, then neither did the disciples have fathers, because the Lord himself told them: Do not call anyone father on earth, for one is your father, God. They are words of the Lord. They had parents. But when it comes to regeneration, we must look for a father of regeneration; Let us not condemn the father of generation, but we must put before him the Father of regeneration. 7. Be more concerned, my brothers, be more concerned, please, about what the Lord said, stretching out his hand over his disciples: This is my mother and my brothers; and whoever does the will of my Father, who sent me, is a brother, sister and mother to me. Was not the Virgin Mary, who in faith believed, in faith conceived, chosen so that from her might be born salvation among men, created by Christ before Christ was created in her, did not the Father's will? Without a doubt, Saint Mary did the will of the Father; That is why it is more for Mary to be a disciple of Christ than to have been

mother of Christ. Having been a disciple of Christ brings her more joy than having been his mother. That is why Mary was blessed, because before giving birth she carried the master in her womb. See if what I say is not true. As the Lord walked with the crowds that followed him, performing divine miracles, a woman shouted: Blessed is the womb that carried you! Blessed is the womb that carried you. But, so that happiness should not be sought in the flesh, what did the Lord reply? Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it. That is why Mary was blessed, because she heard the word of God and kept it: she kept the truth in her mind better than the flesh in her womb 2. Truth is Christ, flesh is Christ; Christ Truth was in the mind of Mary, Christ flesh was in Mary's womb: what is in the mind is more than what is carried in the womb. Holy is Mary, blessed is Mary, but the Church is better than the Virgin Mary. Because? Because Mary is a portion of the Church, a holy member, an excellent member, a super-eminent member, but ultimately a member of an entire body. If it is part of the entire body, it is more the body than one of its members. The Lord is Head and the total Christ is head and body. What will I say? We have a divine Head, we have God as Head. 8. Therefore, dear ones, look at yourselves. You too are members of Christ, you are the body of Christ. See what you are like, what he said: Behold my mother and my brothers. I married you to a man, presenting you as a chaste virgin to Christ; But I fear, lest just as the serpent seduced Eve with his cunning, so your minds may lose the chastity that is in Christ Jesus. Keep virginity in your minds; The virginity of the mind is the integrity of the Catholic faith. Where Eve was raped by the word of the serpent, there the Church must be a virgin with the gift of the Omnipotent. Therefore, let the members of Christ give birth in the mind, as Mary gave birth to Christ in the womb, without ceasing to be a virgin, and in this way you will be the mother of Christ. Parable of the sower and the tares
Topic: The parable of the sower and the tares (Mt 13:4-30). Location: Probably Hippo. Date: After the year 425 (according to others, in 410).

1. Both yesterday and today we have heard the parable of the sower from the mouth of our Lord Jesus Christ. Those of you who came yesterday, remember it today. Yesterday the text was read about that sower who scattered his seed, and some fell on the road and the birds ate it; Some of it fell on rocky ground and dried up in the heat; part fell among brambles and was drowned and could not be fertilized; and some fell on good ground and bore fruit of a hundred, sixty and thirty, times one. And today the Lord narrated again another parable of the sower, who sowed good seed in his field; The men fell asleep, the enemy came and sowed tares on them. While it was grass, it was not noticeable; But when the fruit of the good seed began to appear, the fruit of the tares also appeared among the good seed and they wanted to uproot the tares, but they did not obtain permission, for it was said to them: Let them both grow until the harvest. The Lord Jesus Christ himself expounded this parable; He said that he was the sower of good seed; indicated that the enemy sower of tares was the

CAPUT I. — 1. Mali inter deben.—Et hesterno die et hodie, loquente Domino nostro Iesu Christo, parabolas seminantis audivimus. Qui adfuistis heri, rememberamini hodie. Heri lectum est de irlo seminante qui cum semina spargeret, aliud cecidit in viam, quod Aves collegerunt; aliud in petrosis locis, quod aestu exaruit; aliud Inter spinas, quod suffocatum est, et fecundari non potuit; aliud in terram bonam, et attulit fructum centenum, sexagenum, tricenum (Mt 13:3-23). Hodie autem alliam parabolano rursus Dominus de seminante narravit, qui seminavit bonum semen in agro suo. Dormientibus hominibus venit inimicus, et superseminavit zizania. Quando herba erat, nondum apparebat: ubi coepit fructus boni seminis apparere, ibi etiam zizania claruerunt. Offensi sunt servi patrisfamilias, videntes in bona segete fines zizania, et voluerunt eradicare, et permissi non sunt: ​​sed dictum est eis, Sinite utraque crescere usque ad messem. Exposuit autem etiam Dominus Iesus Christus istam parabolam: et boni seminis seminatorem se esse dixit, seminatorem ziza-

devil; that harvest time was the end of the century and that the field was the whole world. And what did he say? Antea enim dictum est ex voce passionis eius, quia secundum carnem cum demonstraret humilitatis exemplum, evanuerunt adversus eum fluctus maris, quibus cessit volúntate pro nobis, ut impleretur illa prophetia; Come in alti-

tudinem maris, et tempestas demersit me (Ps 68,3). Non enim repulit false tests, nec saevientem clamorem digantium: Crucifigatur (Mt 27,23). Rábida corda et ora furentium non potestate compressit, sed patientia toleratevit. Fecerunt ei quanta voluerunt: quia factus est oboediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis (Phil 2,8). Postea vero quam resurrexit a mortuis, ut pro discipulis in Ecclesia tanquam in navi constitutis, et fide crucis suae tanquam ligno portatis, et tentationibus huius saeculi tanquam fluctibus maris periclitantibus, solus oraret; coepit nomen eius honorari et in hoc saeculo, in quo contemptus, accusatus, occisus est: ut qui venerat secundum passionem carnis in altitudinem maris, et tempestas demerserat eum, iam superborum cervices tanquam spumam undarum sui nominis honore calcaret. Sicut nunc Dominum videmus tanquam ambulantem super mare, sub cuius pedibus totam huius saeculi rabiem subiectam esse conspicimus. CAPUT VIL—8. Error discipulorum errors figurat haereticorum.—Sed accessunt periculis tempestatum etiam errors haereticorum; et non desunt qui sic tentent spirits eorum qui sunt in navi, ut dicant Christum non Fuisse natum de virgine, nec verum corpus habuisse, sed oculis visum esse quod non erat. Et istae opinions haereticorum nunc natae sunt, quando iam nomen Christi per omnes gentes clarificatur, tanquam The Manichaeans affirmed that the body of Jesus had only been apparent and therefore denied that he had been born of Mary. On Manichean Christology, see Supplementary Note 3: Manichean Christology vol. VII p.743.

tation the disciples said: It is a ghost. But he encourages us with his voice against these pests saying: Trust, it is I, do not fear. Out of vain fear men conceived these things about Christ seeking his honor and majesty; They do not think that someone who deserved to be honored in this way could have been born in this way, as if they were scared that he would walk on the sea. Therefore, due to the excellence of his honor, they make him a figure, and thus they consider him to be a ghost. But when he says It is I, what else does he say except that it is not what it is not? If he shows us meat, it is meat; If bones, they are bones; If scars, they are scars. Because there is no Yes and No in him, but, as the Apostle says, in him there is only Yes. And hence his voice: Trust, it is I, do not fear; That is, do not be so frightened by my dignity that you want to take away my truth; Although I walk on the sea, although I have secular pride and ostentation under my feet, like a raging wave, I appeared as a true man, my Gospel tells the truth about me, affirming that I was born of a virgin and that the Word became flesh. What I said is true: Feel and see, that the spirit has no bones, as you see that I have; and that the hands of the one who doubted touched the true scars of my wounds. Therefore, it is I, do not fear. 9. But this point does not designate only the disciples who thought it was a ghost; It not only designates those who deny that the Lord had true flesh and sometimes disturb those who are in the boat with their blind evil; also designates those

who think that the Lord lied in some way, and do not believe that what he threatened the wicked will be accomplished. As if he were partly truthful and partly a liar, like a ghost that appears in words, like a Yes and a No. But those who understand the voice of him who says: It is I, do not fear, believe all the words of the Lord, and as they hope for the rewards he promises, they fear the penalties he commands. As it is true what he will say to those who are on the right: Come, you who are blessed by my Father, to receive the kingdom that has been prepared for you since the beginning of the world, so it is also true what those who are on the left will hear: Go into the eternal fire, which is prepared for the devil and his angels. That opinion by which people think that Christ did not intimate real things to the wicked and lost has originated because it is seen that many peoples and innumerable multitudes have submitted to his name; That is why it seems to many that Christ is a ghost who walked on the sea; In other words, it seems to them that he lied when he intimated the penalties, since he cannot lose such innumerable peoples, who have submitted to his name and honor. But listen to him who says: It is I. And those who believe that Christ is true in everything, do not fear; They not only desire what he promised, but avoid what he threatened; because, although he walks on the sea, that is, although all men in this century are subject to him, he is not a ghost, and that is why he does not lie when he says: Not everyone who calls me Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven.

Christo iam itinerant super mare. Tentati discipuli dixerunt: Quia phantasma est (Mt 14,26). Sed Ule nos adversus istas pestes sua voce confirmat, they say, Fidite, ego sum; nolile timere (ib., 27). Vain enim timore nomines de Christo ista senserunt, attendentes honorem eius et maiestatem: et non putant quod sic potuerit nasci, qui sic meruit clarify, tanquam expavescentes super mare ambulantem. Quo facto, honoris eius excellence figuratur. Atque ita quod phantasma esset, existimant. Sed cum ille dicit, Ego sum; quid aliud dicit, nisi non in se esse quod non est? Itaque si carnem otendit, caro erat; si ossa, ossa erant (cf. Lk 24:39); If scars, they were scars (cf. 20:27). Non enim erat in illo, Est, et Non; thirst, Est in illo erat, sicut Apostolus dicit (2 Cor 1,19). Inde est vox illa, Fidite, ego sum; nolite timere (Mt 14,27). Hoc est, Nolite sic expavescere meam dignitatem, ut mihi velitis auíerre veritatem. Etsi super mare ambulo, etsi elationes et fastus saeculares tamquam rábidos fluctus sub pedibus habeo, tamen verus homo apparui, tamen verum de me Evangelium meum praedicat, quod ex virgine natus sim, quod Verbum caro factus sim; quod verum dixi: Pálpate, et videte, quia spiritus [478] ossa non habet, sicut me videtis habere (Luke 24:39): quod manus dubitantis vera vulnerum meorum vestigia tractaverunt. Itaque, Ego sum; nolite timere (Mt 14,27). CAPUT VIII.—9. Error alius itidem figuratus.—Non autem illos solas significat ista res, quod putaverunt discipuli quia phantasma est; non illos solos designat, qui humanom carnem habuisse Dominum negant, et

aliquando etiam eos qui in navi sunt caeca pravitate perturbant: sed etiam illos qui Dominum putant in aliquo Fuisse mentitum, et ea quae minatus est impiis, eventura esse non credunt. Quasi in parte sit verax et in parte mendax, veluti phantasma apparens in verbis, quasi quod est et non est. Sed qui bene intellegunt vocem dicetis: Ego sum; nolite timere (ib.): iam credunt omnia verba Domini, ut quemadmodum sperant praemia quae promittit, ita poenas timeant quas minatur. Sicut enim verum est quod dicturus est ad dexteram posais: Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est ab initio mundi; Ita verum is quod audituri sunt ad sinistram constituti: Ite in ignem aeternum, qui paratus est diabolo et angelis eius (Mt 25,34.41). Nam et ista opinio, qua putant nomines Christum non vera Fuisse miquis et perditis comminatum, ex hoc nata est, quia vident populos multos et innumerable mobs nomini eius esse subiectas: ut ex eo illis videatur Christus phantasma esse, quia super mare ambulabat; Id est, ideo video lieri in comminatione poenarum, quia quasi non potest will lose tam innumerabiles populos, qui nomini eius et honori subiecti sunt. Sed audiant dicentem: Ego sum (Mt 14:27). lili ergo non timeant, qui veracem in omnibus Christum credentes, non solum id quod promisit appetunt, sed etiam fugiunt quod minatus est: quia etiamsi super mare ambulat, id est, omnia genera hominum in ísto saeculo constituta illi subiecta sunt; tamen non est phantasma, et ideo non mentitur cum dicit: Non omnis qui mihi dicit, Domine, Domine, intrabit in regnum caelorum (ib., 7,21).

10. And what does it also mean that Peter dared to reach him on the water? Peter often represents the role of the Church 5. When saying: Lord, if it is You, command me to come to You on the waters, what else does he say but: "Lord, if You are truthful and do not lie in anything, let Your Church also be honored in this age, for that is what the prophecy preached about You"? Let her therefore walk on the waters and so may she come to you of whom it was said: The magnates of the people will desire to see your face. But human praise does not tempt the Lord, and, on the other hand, men in the Church are often disturbed by the praises and honors of men, and almost shipwreck; Therefore, Peter trembled in the sea, terrified by the strong violence of the storm. For who will not fear that voice: Those who call you happy mislead you and make the paths of your feet difficult? And since the spirit fights against the concupiscence of human praise, it is good that in such danger it resorts to prayer and supplication; lest he who is softened by praise be surprised and overwhelmed by reproach. In the waves let the wavering Peter cry out and say: Lord, save me. The Lord extends his hand and seems to rebuke him, saying: O man of little faith, why did you doubt? Why did you not walk straight, looking to Him to whom you tended, and glorifying only in the Lord? However, he takes him out of the waves and does not let him perish, because he confesses his weakness and requests CAPOT IX.—10. Petrus ambulans super mare.—Quid ergo significat etiam quod Petrus ausus est ad illum vinore super aquas? Gestat enim Petrus Ecclesiae plerumque personam. Quid ergo aliud dictum putamus: Domine, si tu verax es, iube me vinore ad te super aquas (ib., 14,28) nisi: «Domine, si tu verax es, et in millo lieris, clarifícetur etiam Ecclesia tua in isto saeculo, quia hoc de te ptophetia praedicavit?» Ambulet ergo super aquas, et sic ad te veniat illa cui dictum est: Vultum tuum deprecabuntur divites plebis (Ps 24,13). Sed quoniam Dominum laus humano non tentat, homines autem saepe in Ecclesia humanis laudibus et honoribus perturban tur, et prope merguntur; ideo Petrus trepidavit in mati, magnam vim tempestatis exhorrens. Quis enim non timet illam vocenv. Qui vos felicitas dicunt, in errorem vos mittunt, et conturbant semitas pedum vestrorum? (Is 3:12).

Et quia luctatur animus adversus concupiscentiam laudis humanoe, bonum est in tali periculo ad orationem et deprecationem convertatur: ne forte qui laude mulcetur [479] vituperatione subruatur atque mergatur. In one he exclaimed titubans Petrus, et dicat: Domine, save me (Mt 14,30). Porrigit enim Domínus manum; et quamvis increpet, they say: Modicae fidei, utquid dubitasti? (ib., 31) quare non recto itinere illum intuens ad quem tendebas, nonnisi in Domino gloriatus es? tamen a fluctibus rapit, et confitentem infirmitatem suam atque illius auxilium postulantem, perire non sinit. divine help. Once the Lord is received in the boat, faith confirmed, all hesitation eliminated, the storm of the sea calmed, to reach the stability and security of the land, everyone worships Him saying: Truly, you are the Son of God. And that is the eternal joy, with which the naked truth is known and loved, the Word of God, the Wisdom by which all things were created and the eminence of his mercy.
Theme: Peter walks on the waters (Mt 14,24-33). Location: Unknown. Date: Between the year 410 and 412.

1. They have just recited to us the Gospel of the Lord Christ, who walks on the waters of the sea, and of the apostle Peter, who also walked, but feared and hesitated, and for fear of seeing himself submerged, he confessed and came out again; That Gospel warns us that the sea is the present century and Peter the Apostle is a type of the one Church.' This Peter, first in the choir of the Apostles, always ready in the love of Christ, often responds alone on behalf of everyone. Finally, when the Lord Jesus Christ asked who the people said he was, and the disciples picked up Domino in navi, confirmata fide atque omni dubitatione sublata, sedatisque tempestatibus maris, ut iam ad terrae stabilitatem securitatemque veniatur, adorant omnes dicentes: Veré Filius Dei es tu (ib., 33). Hoc est enim gaudium sempiternum, quo perspicua veritas, et Verbum Dei, et Sapientia per quam facta sunt omnia (cf. lo 1,3), et eminentia misericordiae eius, et cognoscitur et amatur.
RURSUS IN MATTHAEI CAP. 14.24-33, BY DOMINO AMBULANTE SUPER AQUAS MARIS, ET BY PETRO TITUBANTE

CAPUT I. — 1. Mare, saeculum. Petrus Ecclesiae typus.—Evangelium quod recentíssime recitatum est de Domino Christo, qui super aquas maris ambulavit; et de apostólo Petro, qui ambulans timendo titubavit, et diffidendo mersus, confitendo rursus emersit; admonet nos intellegere mare praesens saeculum esse, Petrum vero apostolum Ecclesiae unicae typum. Ipse enim Petrus in Apostolorum ordine primus, in Christi amore promptissimus, saepe unus respondert pro omnibus. Ipse demque

various opinions of men, the Lord asked again saying: And you, who do you say that I am? Peter answered: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. One gave the answer for many, unity in the crowd. Then the Lord said to him: Blessed are you, Simon Barlona, ​​because it was not flesh and blood that revealed it to you, but my Father who is in heaven. Then he added: And I say to you, as if to say: since you have said to me: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God, I also say to you: You are Peter. Because before his name was Simon; That name, by which we call him Peter, was imposed on him by the Lord, and that so that in figure it would mean the Church. If Christ is the stone 2, Peter is the Christian people. Stone is the main name; That is why Peter comes from a stone, not a stone from Peter, just as Christ does not come from a Christian, but the Christian is called that way because of Christ. That is why he said: You are Peter, and on this rock, which you have confessed, on this rock, which you have known, saying: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God, I will build my Church, that is, on me, the very Son of the living God, I will build my Church. I will build you on me, I will not build myself on you. 2. Men not wanting to build on men, said: I am of Paul, I of Apollo, I of Cephas, that is, Peter. And others, who did not want to be built on Peter, but on the rock, said: I am Christ's. When the apostle Paul saw that he was chosen and Christ postponed, he said: Has faith divided

did Christ? Has Paul been crucified for you? Or have you been baptized in the name of Paul? If you were not in the name of Paul, neither in that of Peter, but in that of Christ; so that Peter would be built on the rock, not the stone on Peter. 3. Peter was named after the stone, representing the role of the Church, maintaining the primacy of the apostolate 3. But then, after hearing that he was blessed, that he was Peter, who was going to be built on the stone, when the future passion of the Lord was mentioned to him, since he already presented it as imminent to his disciples, it displeased him. He feared losing the one who was going to die, the one he had confessed to be the source of life. Troubled, he said: Far be it from you, Lord; that won't happen. Have mercy on you, God, I don't want you to die. Peter said to Christ: "I don't want you to die," but Christ said better to Peter: "I want to die for you." Then the Lord rebuked him whom he had previously praised, and whom he had called blessed, he called Satan, saying: Get back, Satan, for you are a scandal to me, since you do not like the things that are of God, but those that are of men. What does he want us to do with who we are, since he blames us for being men? Do you want to know what he wants us to do? Listen to the psalm: I said “you are gods”, all children of the Exalted One. But if you taste human things, you will die like men. Peter himself was first blessed, and then Satan, in a moment, with the interval of a few words.

Domino Iesu Christo requirente, quemnam homines dicerent eutn esse, et opinions various hominum discipulis respondertibus, rursusque Domino interrogante et dicente: Vos autem quent me esse dicitis? answered Petrus, You are Christus Filius Dei viví. Unus pro multis dedit responsum, imitates in multis. Tune ei Dominus ait: Beatus es, Simón Bar-lona, ​​quia non revelavit tibi caro et sanguis, sed Pater meus qui est in caelis. Deinde addidit: Et ego dico tibi. Tanquam diceret: Quia tu dixisti mihi: Tu es Christus Filius 'Dei viví: et ego dico tibi, Tu es Petrus (Mt 16,13-18). Simón quippe antea vocabatur. Hoc autem ei nomen, ut Petrus appellaretur, a Domino impositum est: et hoc in ea figura, ut significaret Ecclesiam. Quia enim Christus petra, Petrus populus christianus. Petra enim principale nomen est. Ideo Petrus a petra, non petra a Petro: quomodo non a christiano Christus, sed a Christo christianus vocatur. You are ergo, inquit, Petrus; et super hanc petratn quam confessus es, super hanc petram quam eognovisti, they say, Tu es Christus Filius Dei viví, aedificabo Ecclesiam mean (ib.); id est, Super me ipsum Filium Dei vivi, aedificabo Ecclesiam meam. Super me aedificabo te, not me super te. CAPUT II.—2. Ecclesia non super homines, sed super Christum aedificata.—Nam volentes homines aedificari super homines, dicebant: Ego quidem sum [480] Paull, ego autem Apollo, ego vero Cephae, ipse est Petrus. Et alii qui nolebant aedificari super Petrum, sed super petram,

Ego autem sum Christi. Apostolus autem Paulus ubi cognovit se eligi, et Christum contemni: Divisus est, inquit, Christus? Numquid Paulus pro vobis crucifixus est? aut in nomine Pauli baptizan estis? (1 Cor 1,12.13). Quomodo non in Pauli, sic nec in Petri; sed in nomine Christi: ut Petrus aedificaretur super petram, non petra super Petrum. 3. Petrus primo beatus, et mox satanás dictus.—idem ergo Petrus a petra cognominatus beatus, Ecclesiae figuram portans, apostolatus princípatum tenens, continuo post paululum iam audito quod beatus esset, iam audito quod Petrus esset, iam audito quod supra petram aedifícandus esset, posteaquam audivit Futuram Domini passionem, quia praedixerat eam cita futurem discipulis suis, displicuit ei. Timuit ne seguiret morientem, quem confessus fuet vitae fontem. Turbatus est, they say: Absit a te, inquit, Domine; non fiet istud. Propitius this tibi, Deus; I didn't die for you. Petrus saysbat Christo: «Nolo te mori»; sed melius dicebat Christus: “He flew pro te mori.” Denique continued reprehendit, quem paulo ante laudaverat; et quem beatum dixerat, satanam appellat. Redi, inquit, post me, satana; scandalum mihi is: non enim sapis quae Dei sunt, sed quae sunt hominum (Mt 16,22.23). Quid nos vult faceré ex hoc quod sumus, qui sic culpat quod homines sumus? Vultis scire quid nos velit faceré? Audite Psalmum: Ego dixi, Dii estis, et filii Excelsi omnes. Human thirst knowing: Vos autem sicut homines moriemini (Ps 81,6.7). ditto ipse

bras. If you are surprised by the difference in names, pay attention to the difference in causes. Why do you marvel that he was blessed first and then Satan? Look at the reason why he was blessed: Because it was not flesh and blood that revealed it to you, but my Father who is in heaven. If flesh and blood had revealed it to you, you would have expressed yours; And since flesh and blood did not reveal it to you, but my Father who is in heaven, you gave of mine, not of yours. Why mine? Because everything the Father has is mine. You have already heard the reason why he was blessed and why he was Peter. And why was it what terrifies us and we don't want to repeat? Why, if not because he gave of his own? You do not like the things that are of God, but those of men. 4. As we, members of the Church, consider this, we discern what is God's and what is ours. Thus we will no longer hesitate, we will base ourselves on the stone, we will remain firm and stable against the winds, rains, rivers; that is, to the temptations of the present century. But look at that Peter who then represented us; Now he trusts, now he hesitates; He already confesses the immortal, he already fears that he will die. The Church of Christ has strong and weak men; It cannot be maintained without the strong and without the weak, and that is why the Apostle says: We the strong must bear the burden of the weak. In saying: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God, it means the strong; but in trembling and hesitating, not wanting Christ to suffer, fearing

Death, not recognizing life, means the weak in the Church. In a single apostle, in Peter, first and principal in the order of the Apostles and who represented the Church, the two groups had to be meant, that is, the strong and the weak; because without both there is no Church. 5. And from there comes what was just read: Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you over the waters. If it is you, send me: because it cannot be done for me, but for you 4. He recognized what was by itself and what was by Him by whose will he believed he could do what no human weakness could. Therefore, if it is you, send me, because as soon as you send it, it will be done; What I cannot do by showing off, you can do by commanding. And the Lord said: Come. And under the word of the one who commanded, under the presence of the one who supported, under the presence of the one who disposed, Peter without hesitation and without delay jumped into the water and began to walk. He was able to do the same as the Lord, not for himself, but for the Lord. For once you were darkness, but now you are light; but in the Lord. What no one can do in Paul, or in Peter, or in any other of the Apostles, he can do in the Lord. Therefore Paul, usefully lowering himself, exalts the Lord, saying very well: Has Paul been crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul? Not, then, in me, but with me; not under my power, but under his. 6. Peter therefore walked on the water at the command of the Lord, knowing that he could not do it by himself. By faith

Petrus paulo ante beatus, post satan, in momento uno, infra pauca verba. Miraris differentiam nominum, differentias attende causaum. Will you look, quia paulo ante beatus, does satan post? Attende causam quare beatus. Quia non tibi revelavit caro et sanguis, sed Pater meus qui in caelis est (Mt 16,17). Ideo beatus, quia tibi non caro et sanguis revelavit. Si enim cato et sanguis hoc tibi revealet; de tuo: quia veto non caro et sanguis tibi revelavit, sed Pater meus qui in caelis est; de meo, non de tuo. Quare de peo? Quia omnia quae habet Pater, mea sunt (lo 16,15). Ecce audisti causam, quare beatus, et quare Petrus. Quare autem illud quod horrescimus, et repetere nolumus? Quare, nisi quia de tuo? Non enim sapis quae Dei sunt, sed quae sunt hominum (ib., 23).

vult, mortem timendo, vitam non agnoscendo, infirmos Ecclesiae significat. In illo ergo uno apostólo, id est, Petro, in ordine Apostolorum primo et praecipuo, in quo figurabatur Ecclesia, utrumque genus significandum Fuit, id est, firmi et infirmi: quia sine utroque non est Ecclesia. 5. Homo in se infirmus, potens in Domino.—Hinc est ergo et quod moda lectum est: Domine, si tu es, iube me come ad te super aquas (ib., 14,28). If you are, iube me: non enim possum hoc in me, sed in te. Agnovit quid sibi esset a se, quid ab illo, cuius volúntate credidit se posse, quod nulla infirmitas humano possit. Ergo, If you are, iube: quia cum iusserit, fiet. Quod ego non valeo praesumendo, tu potes iubendo. Et Dominus: Veni (ib., 29), inquit. Et sine ulla dubitatione Petrus ad verbum iubentis, ad praesentiam sustainantis, ad praesentiam regentis sine ulla cunctatione desiluit in aquas, et atribulare coepit. Potuit quod Dominus, non in se, sed in Domino. Fuistis enim aliquando tenebrae, never autem lux; thirst in Domino (Eph 5,8). Quod nemo potest in Paulo, nemo in Petro, nemo in alio ullo Apostolorum, hoc potest in Domino. Ideo bene Paulus utiliter se contemnens, illum commendans: Numquid Paulus, inquit, pro vobis crucifixus est? aut in nomine Pauli baptizan estis? (1 Cor 1:13). Non ergo in me, sed mecum; non sub me, sed sub illo. CAPUT IV.—6. Infirmitatis propriae cognitio necessaria ad gratiam obtinendam.—Ergo ambulavit Petrus super aquas in iussu Domini, sciens

CAPUT III.—4. In Petro firmi et infirmi figurati.—Hoc intuentes nos Ecclesiae membrum, discemamus quid dei, quid de nostro. Tune enim non titubabimus, tune in petra fundabimut, fixi et stabiles erimus adversus ventos, imbtes, illuminates, temptationes videlicet praesentis saeculi. Illum tamen videte Petrum, qui tune erat figura nostra: fidit mode, titubat mode; moda immortalem confitetur, moda timet ne moriatur. Proinde quia Ecclesia Christi habet firmos, habet et infirmos; nec sine firmis potest esse, nec sine infirmis; unde dicit Paulus apostolus: Debemus autem nos firmi, infirmorum onera sustinere (Rom 15,1); in [481] eo quod Petrus dixit: Tu es Christus Filius Dei vivi (Mt 16,16), firmos significat; in eo autem quod trepidat et titubat, et Christum pati non
'Anti-Pekgian apostille.

He could do what human weakness could not. These are the strong ones in the Church. Attend, listen, understand, act. Because we do not have to deal here with the strong so that they are weak, but with the weak so that they may be strong. Many are prevented from being firm by their presumption of firmness. No one obtains firmness from God, but he who recognizes his weakness in himself. The Lord pours voluntary rain on his inheritance. Why do you get ahead of yourself, those of you who know what I'm going to say? Temper the speed so that the slower ones follow us. This I said and this I say: hear, understand, act. No one achieves firmness from God if he does not recognize his weakness in himself. As the psalm says, it is voluntary rain; not the result of our merits, but voluntary. Topic: The faith of the Canaanite woman (Mt 15,21-28). Location: Unknown. Date: Unknown. 1. This Canaanite woman, whom the Gospel reading has just recommended to us, offers us an example of humility and a path of piety. It teaches us to rise from humility to height. Apparently, he did not belong to the people of Israel, to which belonged the patriarchs, the prophets, the fathers of our Lord Jesus Christ according to the flesh, and also the Virgin Mary herself, who gave birth to Christ. The Canaanite woman did not belong to this people, but to the Gentiles. As we have heard, the Lord withdrew to the area of ​​Tire and Sidon, and the Canaanite woman, leaving those surroundings, eagerly requested the benefit of healing her daughter, who was mistreated by the devil. Tire and Sidon were not cities of the

CAPUT I.—1. Chananaea mulier humilitatis exemplum.—Chananaea ista mulier, quae moda nobis lectione evangélica commendata est, praebet nobis humilitatis exemplum, et pietatis viam: ab humilitate in alta surgere otendit. Erat autem, sicuti apparet, non de populo Israel, unde Patriarchae, unde Prophetae, unde patents Domini nostri Iesu Christi secundum carnem; unde ipsa virgo Maria, quae peperit Christum. Non ergo ex isto populo erat haec mulier: sed erat ex Gentibus. Nam, sicut audivimus, secessit Dominus in parts Tyri et Sidonis, et inde mulier Chananaea de finibus illis egressa, petebat beneficium instantissime curan-

people of Israel, but of the Gentiles, although neighbors of Israel. She shouted, eager to obtain the benefit, and called loudly; He dissembled, not to deny mercy, but to stimulate desire 1, and not only to increase desire, but also, as I said before, to recommend humility. So she cried out to the Lord, who was not listening, but who was silently planning what he was going to execute. The disciples prayed to the Lord for her and said to Him: Send her away, for she cries after us. But he replied: I was not sent except to the sheep that perished of the house of Israel. 2. Here the problem of these words arises. How have we come from the Gentiles to the fold of Christ, if he was not sent except to the sheep that perished of the house of Israel? What does the profound manifestation of this secret mean? The Lord knew why he had come, that is, to have a Church in all nations. Why does he say that he has not been sent except to the sheep that perished of the house of Israel? We understand that he had to manifest in that town the presence of his body, his birth, the exhibition of his miracles and the virtue of his resurrection -, we understand that this was how it had been planned, proposed from the beginning, predicted and carried out; We understand that Christ Jesus had to come to the people of the Jews to be seen, killed and to recover from among them those whom he pre-established. Because that people were not condemned, but cursed. There was a crowd of straw there, but

also a hidden dignity of grains; There was material for the bonfire, and also to fill the barn. Where did the Apostles come from if not from there? Where did Peter come from? Where did the others come from? 3. And where did Paul come from, before Saul, that is, first proud and then humble? When he was Saul, his name came from Saul2.And Saul was a proud king; In his kingdom he persecuted the humble David. When he was Saul, who later became Paul, he was arrogant, a persecutor of the innocent, a destroyer of the Church. He collected letters from the priests, as if burning with zeal for the synagogue and persecuting the Christian name, to drag all the Christians he could find to suffer the torture. And when he walked, when he longed to kill, when he smelled blood, the persecutor was prostrated by the heavenly voice of God and arose as a preacher. In him was fulfilled what is written in the prophet: I will wound and I will heal. God wounds what in man rises up against God. The doctor is not cruel when he opens a tumor, when he cuts or burns what is rotten. It produces pain, it intervenes, but to lead to health. It's annoying; but, if it were not, it would not be useful either. So Christ with a voice prostrated Saul and raised up Paul. What was the reason for the name change, since before he was called Saul and then Paul, if not the one who recognized the name of Saul in himself, a name of pride, when he was a persecutor? So he chose a humble name, calling himself

dae filiae suae, quae male a daemonio vexabatur. Tyrus et Sidon noneront civitates populi Israel, sed Gentium; quamvis vicinae lili populo. CAPUT X.—14. Moriendi necessitas ab ipso exortu. Vera semitas, immortalitas.—Nam ex quo nascimur, necesse est ut moriamur. Morbus hic necesse est ut ad mortem perducat. "Phthisicus est", quis hoc curat? Necesse est ut pereat, necesse est ut moriatur. Ecce iam dixit medicus: "Phthisicus est, non potest nisi moriatur"; et tamen aliquando et hydrops non inde moritur, et elephantiosus non inde moritur, et phthisicus non inde moritur: et tamen necesse est ut quisquís natus fuerit, inde moriatur. Moritur inde, non potest aliter. Hoc et medicus et imperitus pronuntiat; sed et si tardius moritur, numquid ideo non moritur? Quando ergo vera sanitas, nisi quando vera immortalitas, si ergo vera immortalitas, nulla corruptio, nulla defectio, quid illie alimentis opus erit? 1. You have already heard how that woman who cried out after the Lord searched, asked, knocked, and how they opened it to her. Huius enim olivae radices sunt, Abraham et Isaac et Iacob: filii autem regni, hoc est Iudaei increduli, ibunt in exterior tenebras (ib., 12). Praecidentur rami naturals, ut inseratur oleaster. Meanwhile, while we arrive at that peace, in which we will have no enemy, let us fight long, faithfully and bravely, to deserve to be crowned by the Lord God. The apostle James says: Let no one, when he is tempted, say that he is tempted by God. Here he calls temptation that which implies seduction. God is neither tempted by evil, nor does he tempt anyone; each one is tempted by his concupiscence, which drags and seduces him. Therefore lust, when it conceives, gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is consummated, engenders death. Therefore each one is tempted by his lust. Therefore, fight, resist, do not consent, do not let yourself be carried away, do not allow her to conceive what she would have to give birth to. Behold, concupiscence requests, stimulates, insists, demands, so that you do something bad; do not consent and she will not conceive. If you think about it with pleasure, she will conceive, give birth, and you will die. Look what the Apostle says: Sin, when it is consummated, engenders death. Sin is sweet, but death is bitter. Avoid concupiscence, if not in deeds, at least in words. You gladly hear something you shouldn't hear, you say something you shouldn't say, you think what you shouldn't think. Domine deus noster, pacem da nobis: omnia enim reddidisti nobis. 3. Interim doñee ad illam pacem veniamus, ubi nullum hostem habebimus, diu et fideliter strenueque pugnemus, ut a domino deo coronan mereamur. Apostolus Iacobus ait: nemo, cum temtatur, dicat quoniam a deo temtatur (Iac 1,13). Temtationem dicit, quae est ad seductionem. Deus, inquit, intemtator malorum est, ipse autem neminem temtat; unusquisque autem temtatur a concupiscentia sua abstractus et (579) inlectus. Dein concupiscentia cum conceperit, parit peccatum; peccatum autem cum consummatum fuerit, generat mortem (ib., 13-15). Ergo unusquisque temtatur a concupiscentia sua: ideo pugnet, resistat, non consentiat, non peitrahatur, non eam permittat conripere quod pariat. Ecce blanditur concupiscentia, stimulat, instat, exigít, ut mali aliquid facias: noli consentiré et non concipit. Si libenter cogitaveris, concipit: pariet, ut tu moriaris. Dulce est peccatum, sed mors amata est: cave peccati dulcedinem, ne mortis tristes amaritudinem: cave concupiscentiam, et si non ad factum, certe ad verbum. Avoid, therefore, brothers, usury and abusive interest and do not say: And on what shall we live? That is not seeking life, but death. Do not say: What will we live on? There are many other means by which men support themselves. But what God prohibits, do not do it, do not live on it. Oh wretched, miserable and unhappy! et aliquando multum temporis inpendit, et nullam horam invenit in accipiiendo, et dicit sibi: Quid est, quod voíuit dominus dicere, petite et accipietis, quaerite et invenietis, púlsate et aperietur vobis; omnis enim qui petit accipit, et qui quaerit invenit, et pulsanti aperietur? will you see? Isn't it better for him to cry healthy than for him to cry hurt? If you, being bad, know how to give your child what is good, how much more does the father, who is always good, favor you when he does not give you, even if you ignore it? It is necessary that you be a son: he does not disdain you, you are safe being a son. When the apostle Paul was buffeted by the angel of Satan, so that he would not become arrogant, as he himself confesses—since when would we dare to say that about the Apostle?—he said of the angel of Satan: Therefore three times I besought the Lord to take him away from me; But he said to me: My grace is enough for you, since virtue is perfected in weakness. Why do you pray, Pablo? So that things go well for you? Let the architect do what you don't know, so that it goes well for you. Does the plaster bother you when it itches? 1. Perhaps some of you will say: what did Idito mean with this expression, receive my tears in your ears? Tears are seen, not heard; Tears flow, they do not sound. But they have their voice, as Abel's blood had its voice. If the blood of a dead man had a voice for the Lord, the tears of one who prays also have it, they have it for certain. Tears are blood from the heart. Therefore, when you ask for eternal life, when you say your kingdom come, in which you live securely, in which you live always, in which you never regret your friend or fear your enemy; When you ask for that, cry, shed your inner blood, immolate your heart to your God. That means it is advisable to always pray and not give up; what the Sunday Prayer teaches: Hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done on earth as it is in heaven, so that we may be like your angels. Oh wish! What man would dare to desire if God had not deigned to promise? Pray: great thing is what you pray, but greater is the one who promised. Difficult is what he promised, namely, that man be an angel; There is nothing more difficult, but everything is possible with God. You think it is something very great and difficult for man to be an angel 5. And doesn't it seem difficult to you, much more difficult, much more incredible, that the Only One of God became a man? And the man, through whom God became man, doubts that man will ever become an angel! Do you doubt that you will receive what you ask for, having such a pledge, the same one who deigned to become a debtor gratuitously?

yours? You did not give a loan, or offer any amount, or lend any benefit to your God. Is not all that you have his, and will you not receive from Him whatever you receive? He has deigned to become a debtor and what a debtor! He signed the deed, advanced the pledge. His writing is divine Scripture; His pledge is the death of Christ, his promise is the death of Christ. And he who offered the death of his Son to the wicked, will he deny the death of his Son to the pious and faithful? 8. Be sure, brothers, that you will receive. Ask, seek, knock; you will receive, you will find, it will be opened to you. But do not only ask, seek, call with your voice, but also with customs; perform good works, without which this life must not pass at all. Erase sins with good works every day. Do not disdain the same venial sins. Because although they are not large, they accumulate, they constitute a mass; They accumulate and make mass. Do not disdain them because they are small, but fear them when they are many. Is there anything smaller than raindrops? And with them the fields are flooded and the rivers are filled. Do not disdain your small and light sins, lest they oppress you with their weight. See how the sea water filters through the cracks of the ship and yet fills the holds; If it doesn't shrink, it submerges the ship. A wave, if it is huge, arrives like a mountain, covers the ship and sinks it. So are homicides, that is, serious sins, adulteries, fornications, blasphemies, perjury. They are great sins, they ruin at once. On the other hand, those petty sins, without which human life does not exist, filter insensitively

Ita veto habent voices suas, sicut sanguis Abel habuit vocem suam. Si habuit ad dominum sanguis occisi, habent etiam lacrimae precantis, habent omnino. Nam et lacrimae sanguis cordis est. Ergo, quando postulas vitam aeternam, quando dicis, adveniat regnum tuum (Mt 6:10), ubi securus vivas, ubi semper vivas, ubi numquam doleas amicum, numquam timeas inimicum, quando hoc poscis, plora, funde (657) sanguinem interiorem, immola deo tuo cor tuum: hoc est, quod oportet orare, et non deficere; hoc est, quoddocet dominica oratio: sanctificetur nomen tuum, adveniat regnum tuum, fiat voluntas tua sicut in cáelo et in terra (ib., 9-10), ut simus aequales angelis tuis. O desiderium! Quis auderet homo desíderare, si deus non esset dignitatus promittere? Ora: magnum est quod oras, sed maior est qui promisit. Magnum aliquid whores et difficile, ut homo angelus fiat: illud non tibi videtur difficile, et multo difficilius mukoque incredibilius, ut unicus dei homo firet? gradually through the cracks of human fragility and gather in the cellar. Imitate the sailors, whose hands are always active so that nothing is left in the hold. Qui autem pastor est, et est ei cura pro ovibus, non euro dimittat, et facit quod ait Apostolus: Compete restless, consolamini pusillanimes (1 Thes 5,14), etc. Non ergo putet quis pium pastorem, vel qui se dicit pastorem, quia non reddet malum pro malo, cum reddat potius malum pro bono. 1. Dearly beloved brothers, we must contemplate and comment on this vision that the Lord made manifest on the mountain. In fact, he was referring to her when he said: Truly I say to you, there are some of those present here who will not taste death until they see the Son of man in his kingdom. With these words began the reading that has been proclaimed. After six days, as he said this, he took three disciples, Peter, John and James, and went up the mountain. These three were of those who had said there are some here who will not taste death until they see the Son of man in his kingdom. It is not a simple question. Well, the mountain should not be taken as if it were the kingdom. What is a mountain to one who owns the sky? We not only read this, but in a certain way we see it with the eyes of the heart. He calls his kingdom what in many passages he calls the kingdom of heaven. The kingdom of heaven is the kingdom of the saints. The heavens, in fact, proclaim the glory of God1. Of those heavens it is said next in the psalm: There is no speech nor

1. Regnum Christi.—Inspicienda nobis et tractanda est, carissimi, visio ista, quam Dominus demonstravit in monte. Ipsa est enim de qua dixerat: Amen dico vobis, quia sunt hic quidam de circumstantibus, qui non gustabunt mortem, doñee videant Filium hominis in regno suo (Mt 16:28). Inde coepit lectio quae recitata est. Dum hoc dixisset, post dies sex assumesit three disciples, Vetrum, Ioannem et Iacobum, et ascendit in montem (Mt 17,1). Ipsi tres werent quidam de quibus dixerat: Sunt hic quidam qui non gustabunt mortem, doñee videant Filium hominis in regno suo (Mt 16,28). Non parva quaestio est. Ñeque enim ille mons, regnum erat comprehensum. Quid est mons ei qui possidet caelum? Quod non solum legimus, sed etiam oculis cordis quodam moda videmus. Regnum suum dicit, quod multís locis appellat regnum caelorum. Regnum autem caelorum est regnum sanctorum. Caeli enim enarrant gloriam Dei. De quibus caelis dictum is continuous in Psalm: No« sunt

their word may not be heard. His proclamation reaches the entire earth and his language reaches the ends of the earth. From whom, but from the heavens? Therefore, of the apostles and of all the faithful preachers of the word of God. The heavens will reign with him who made the heavens. See what he did to manifest this. 2. The Lord Jesus himself shone like the sun; His clothes became white as snow and Moses and Elijah spoke with him. Jesus himself shone like the sun, to signify that he is the light that illuminates every man who comes into this world. What this sun is to the eyes of the flesh, that one is to those of the heart; and what this is to the flesh, that is to the heart. His clothes, however, are his Church. Dresses, if they do not have those who wear them inside, fall. Paul was like the last hem of these garments. He himself says: I, indeed, am the least of the Apostles, and in another place: I am the last of the Apostles. The border is the last and lowest part of a dress. Therefore, just as that woman who suffered from an issue of blood and touched the border of the Lord was saved, so the Church from the Gentiles was saved by Paul's preaching. What is strange about pointing out the Church in white garments, hearing the prophet Isaiah say: And if your sins are like scarlet, I will make them white as snow? What are Moses and Elijah worth, that is, the law and

loquelae ñeque sermons, quorum non audiantur voices eorum. In omnem terram exiit sonus eorum, et in fines orbis terrae verba eorum (Ps 18, 4, et 5). Quorum, nisi caelorum? Ergo Apostolorum, et omnium verbi Dei fidelium praedicatorum. Regnabunt caeli cum eo qui fecít cáelos. Hoc ut ostenderetur, videte quid factum est. 2. Domínicae transfigurationis allegoria. Vestment Christi.—Dominus ipse Iesus resplenduit sicut sol; clothing eius facta sunt candida sicut nix: et loquebantur cum eo Moyses et Elias. Ipse Iesus quidem, ipse splenduit sicut sol, se lumen esse significans quod illuminat omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum (cf. lo 1,9). Quod est iste sol oculis carnis, hoc ille oculis cordis: et quod iste carnibus, hoc ille cordibus. Clothing autem eius, Ecclesia [491] eius. Clothing enim nisi ab induto contineantur, cadunt. Horum vestimentomm quaedam quasi novissima fimbria Paulus Fuit. Ipse enim dicit: Ego enim sum minimus Apostolorum (1 Cor 15:9); et alio loco: Ego sum novissimus Apostolorum (ib.). In vestimento autem fimbria est new and minimal. Proinde sicut illa mulier quae sanguinis fluxum patiebatur, tacta Domini fimbria, salva facta est (Lk 8:44); sic Ecclesia quae ex Gentibus venit, Paulo praedicante salvata est. Quid mirum si per candida ropa signatur Ecclesia, cum audiatis Isaiam prophetam dicentem: Et si fuerint peccata vestra sicut phaenicium, tanquam level dealbato? (Is 1,18). Moyses et

the prophets, if they do not speak with the Lord? If you do not bear witness to the Lord, who will read the law? Who the prophets? See how briefly the Apostle says: By the law, therefore, the knowledge of sin; but now without the law the justice of God was manifested: behold the sun. Witnessed by the law and the prophets: behold its splendor.

They are my beloved children. The One and Only One is one thing, and the adopted are another. He was recommended to him from whom came glory to the law and the prophets. This is, he says, my beloved son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him, since you heard him in the prophets and the same in the law. And where did you not hear him? Hearing this, they fell to the ground. The kingdom of God is already manifested to us in the Church. In it is the Lord, the law and the prophets; but the Lord as Lord; the law in Moses, the prophecy in Elijah, in the condition of servants, ministers. They, like vessels; him, as a source. Moses and the prophets spoke and wrote, but whatever flowed from them, they took from him.

3. Peter sees this and, judging from human to human, says: Lord, it is good for us to be here. He suffered the tedium of the mob, he had found the solitude of the mountain. There I had Christ, bread of the soul. Why leave there for fatigue and pain, having the holy loves of God and, therefore, good habits? He wanted it to go well, so he added: If you want, let's make three tents, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah. The Lord answered nothing to this, but Peter received, yes, an answer. For as he said this, a bright cloud came and covered them. He was looking for three stores. Heaven's response stated that for us what human sense wanted to divide is one thing. Christ is the Word of God, Word of God in the law, Word of God in the prophets. Why do you want to divide, Pedro? It's better for you to join. Look for three, but also understand unity. 4. When the cloud covered them all and made in a sense a single tent, a voice sounded from it saying: This is my beloved Son. There was Moses, there was Elijah. His relics were found in Palestine in the year 415 thanks to a revelation received in dreams by a priest named Lucian. These relics arrived in Africa, specifically Hippo, in 425; In this city an altar and a Church are dedicated to him (S. 318). Miracles attributed to the saint's thaumaturgic power multiply everywhere. This fact forces Augustine to order that they all be put in writing to be read in the church (The City of God XII, 8,21). In The City of God XXII, 8,22 we have Augustine's account of one of them, and in sermon 322 the account of one of those cured. These events change Augustine's way of thinking about miracles, since until then he thought that they were something typical of the early days of the Church, when it was in its founding period, but that now they were no longer necessary.

Topic: The transfiguration of Jesus (Mt 17,1-8). Location: Unknown. Date: Unknown.

Before the Lord revealed himself on the mountain, as we have heard in the reading of the holy Gospel, he had said: There are some of those present here who will not taste death until they see the Son of man in his kingdom. We know, in fact, that at the end of the world Jesus Christ the Lord will come and will give the kingdom to those on his right and torment to those on his left, he who, as we believe and profess, will come to judge the living and the dead. All those who surrounded him when he spoke, because of his mortal condition, fell asleep; but only when the time of resurrection arrives will they see the Lord as judge in his kingdom. What then does it mean that he says: There are some here present who will not taste death until they see the Son of man in his kingdom? Without a doubt the holy Gospel raised a question that refers to what follows. He took three with him to the mountain: Peter, James and John, and was transfigured in their presence, to the point that his face shone like the brilliance of the sun. Therefore, since in saying: Because of your unbelief you could not expel this demon, the Lord was trying to exhort us to prayer, he concluded thus: This genus cannot be cast out except by fasting and prayer. If a man prays to cast out a foreign demon, how much more must he pray to cast out his own greed! How much more to expel its violence! How much more to expel his lust and his impurity! How many things there are in a man that, if he perseveres in it, will close the doors of the kingdom of heaven to him! See, brothers, how one seeks a doctor for bodily health; How, if someone becomes sick to the point of losing hope, they lose their shame and feel no qualms about throwing themselves at the feet of a very expert doctor and washing away his traces with tears. And if the doctor said to you: "I can only heal you by bandaging, cauterizing and cutting," what will you say? His answer will be: “Do what you want; The only thing I ask of you is that you heal me. How ardently does he desire the temporary health of a few days, to the point that for it he wants to be bandaged, cut, cauterized, and deprive himself of eating what he likes,

to drink what you like when you like it! You suffer all this to die later, and you don't want to suffer a little and never die! If God, who is the celestial doctor who takes care of us, said to you: "Do you want to be healed?", what would you say to Him but: "I want to"? Maybe you don't say it believing you are healthy. Here is the worst disease. 4. Now imagine two sick people: one who asks the doctor with tears and another who, in his illness, losing his mind, laughs at him. The doctor, while giving hope to those who cry, cries for those who laugh. Why, if not because his illness is all the more dangerous because he considers himself healthy? The Jews were of this style. Christ came to the sick; He found them all sick. Let no one boast of his health, lest the doctor abandon him. He found them all sick; is the Apostle's statement: All, in fact, have sinned and are deprived of the glory of God. He found everyone sick, but there were two types of sick people. Some approached the doctor, adhered to Christ, listened to him, honored him, followed him and converted. He received everyone, without repugnance, to heal them, because he healed them freely, he healed them with his omnipotence. And upon receiving them and associating them with Himself to heal them, they leaped for joy. On the other hand, the other type of sick people who had already lost their reason due to the disease and were unaware that they were sick, insulted him because he received the sick and said to his disciples: See what a teacher you have, who eats with sinners and publicans. But he, who knew what they were and who they were, answered them.

2. It has been proposed to us, then, to see or seek or learn how we should be meek; and in what I have recently recalled from the Scriptures we are admonished to find what we seek. Give your charity a little attention; It is about an important thing: being meek; necessary thing in the face of adversity. But the adversities of this world are not called scandals; notice what scandals are. For example: a certain gentleman is under the pressure of an urgent need. The scandal does not lie in being surrounded by pressure. The martyrs were also pressed by some hardship, but not oppressed. Beware of scandal, but not of pressure. The pressure squeezes you, the scandal oppresses you. What is the difference between pressure and scandal? In the first case you prepare yourself to maintain patience, to be steadfast, not to abandon faith, not to consent to sin. Whether you do it now or in the future, no amount of pressure will lead to ruin; On the contrary, it will have the same function in you that it has in the winepress: the aim is not to crush the olive, but to distill the oil. Finally, if in that tribulation you praise God, how useful is this press, through which that liquor flows from you! The Apostles were seated and tied as if in a vise and in it they sang a hymn to God. What was being squeezed? What did it distill? Job was under a great pressure in the middle of dung, needy, without help, without riches, without children; full, but of worms, which certainly belongs to the external man. But since inwardly he was full of God, he praised Him and that situation

It was no scandal to him. Where, then, is the scandal? When the woman approaches him and says: Say something against God and die. In fact, after having taken all things from her, the devil, now exercised, was left with Eve, not for consolation, but for the temptation of man 1. That is the scandal. She exaggerated his miseries, adding hers to his, and began to persuade him to blaspheme. But he, who was meek, because God had indoctrinated him with his law and had softened his evil days, as a lover of God's law, had great peace in his heart and there was no scandal for him. She was a scandal, but not for him. Therefore, look at this meek man; observe him instructed in the law of God, and I mean the eternal law, since the law given to the Jews on the tables did not yet exist then, but the eternal law still remained in the hearts of the pious, in which the other law given to the people was inspired. Since the law of God had softened his bad days and as a lover of that same law he enjoyed great peace in his heart, pay attention to his meekness and his response. Learn here what I proposed to you, namely, who are the meek. You have spoken, he said, like a foolish woman. If we receive good things from the hand of God, are we not going to endure the bad? 3. Topic: Fraternal correction (Mt 18,15-18). Location: Probably Milevi. Date: Between the year 408 and 409.

1. It is the advice of our Lord that we should not mutually disregard our sins; not that we look for what to rebuke, but that we see what needs to be corrected. He said, in effect, that only he who does not have a beam in his eye is able to remove the speck from his brother's eye. What this is, I am going to briefly indicate to your charity. The speck in the eye is anger; the beam, the hate. When he rebukes the angry person who feels hatred, he wants to remove the speck from his brother's eye, but he is prevented from doing so by the beam in his own. The straw is the beginning of the beam, for when the beam is formed, at the beginning it is like a straw. By watering the straw, you turn it into a beam; By feeding anger with bad suspicions, you lead it to hatred. 2. Let us exactly what we have been advised today: If your brother sins against you, correct him alone. Why do you correct him? Why does it hurt you that he has sinned against you? In no way. If you do it for self-love, you do nothing. If you do it out of love for him, you work excellently. Consider in the same words for whose love you should do it, whether for yours or his. If I would listen to you, he said, you have won over your brother. So do it for him, to win him. If you win by doing it, by not doing it you lose. What is the reason why many men despise these sins and say, “What have I done when I am great? "I have sinned against a man"? Don't despise them. You sinned against a man; Do you want to know that by sinning against a man you perished? If the one against whom you sinned had corrected you alone and you had listened to him, he would have won you. What does it mean that I would have won you, but that you would have perished if I had not won you? For if you had not perished, how would I have won you? Let no one, therefore, despise the sin against his brother. In a certain place the Apostle says: Thus you who sin against your brothers and hurt their weak conscience sin against Christ, precisely because we have all been made members of Christ. How can you not sin against Christ if you sin against a member of Christ? 5. Let no one say: "I have not sinned against God, but against a brother, against a man; slight or almost zero sin. 7. This, then, is what he who committed an injury must do. What should someone who suffered it do? What we have heard today: If your brother sins against you, correct him alone. If you neglect to do it, the worse you are. He committed the insult and with it he seriously injured himself; Do you despise your brother's wound? You see him perish or that he has perished, and you neglect him? It is worse for you to remain silent than for him to insult you. Therefore, when someone sins against us, let us feel great concern, but not for ourselves, since it is something worthy of glory to forget injuries; But forget the injury he did to you, not your brother's injury. Correct him, then, alone, with an eye toward correction, respecting his shame. Maybe because of her he begins to defend his sin and the one you wanted to do better you do worse. Correct him, then, alone. If I listened to you, you have gained a brother, for he would have perished had he not done so. If, however, he does not listen to you, that is, if he defends his sin as something just, take two or three with you, because in the testimony of two or three witnesses Every word stands. If I don't even listen to them, tell it to the Church; If I do not even listen to the Church, let me be to you like a pagan and a publican. Do not count him in the number of your brothers. But that does not mean that their salvation should be neglected. For although we do not count among our brothers the ethnics, that is, the Gentiles and the pagans 2, nevertheless, we always seek their salvation. We hear this from the mouth of the Lord, who thus

He advised and commanded us so carefully that he then added this: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will also be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will also be loosed in heaven. You began to consider your brother as a publican: you bound him to the ground; but be careful to bind him with justice, since unjust ties are broken by justice. Once you had corrected him and agreed with your brother, you unleashed him on the ground. Once; Whatever you have loosed on earth, it will also be loosed in heaven. You concede a lot not to yourself, but to him, because he hurt a lot, not to you, but to him. 8. Things being this way, what does it mean when Solomon says, as we heard today in the first reading: Whoever maliciously shows signs with his eyes, accumulates sadness for men; Who, on the other hand, openly censures, engenders peace? If, then, he who openly censures engenders peace, how does he command: Correct him alone? We must fear that divine precepts will contradict each other. We must note, however, the utmost concord that exists there and not think like certain vain people 3 who in their error believe that the two Testaments of Scripture, the Old and the New, are in contradiction, so that we judge that they are contrary because one testimony is in the book of Solomon and the other in the Gospel. Therefore, if any ignorant and slanderer of the Holy Scriptures should say: “Behold, the two Testaments are opposed; says the Lord:

Correct him alone; and Solomon: He who censures openly, begets peace..." So, does the Lord not know what he commanded? Solomon wants to strike the forehead of the sinner; Christ has consideration for the modesty of those who are ashamed. There it is written: He who censures openly, engenders peace; here, however: Correct him alone, not in public, but secretly and hidden. You who think such things, do you want to know that the two Testaments do not contradict each other even though this is found in the book of Solomon and this is found in the Gospel? Listen to the Apostle. Certainly the Apostle is a minister of the New Testament. Listen, then, to the apostle Paul who commands and says: Censor sinners in the presence of everyone so that others may also feel fear. It is no longer the book of Solomon, but the letter of the apostle Paul that seems to be in conflict with the Gospel. Without insulting him, let us leave Solomon aside a little; Let us listen to Christ the Lord and his servant Paul. What do you say, Lord? If a brother of yours sins against you, correct him alone. What say you, oh Apostle? He censures sinners in the presence of everyone so that others may also feel fear. To do? Do we hear this controversy as judges? In no way; Furthermore, placed under the judge, let us knock and ask him to open it to us; Let us flee under the wings of the Lord our God. He did not say anything contrary to his Apostle, because it was he himself who spoke in him, as demonstrated by these words: Or do you want to have proof that Christ speaks in me? It is Christ who speaks in the Gospel and in the Apostle; Christ said one and the other;

one thing through his own mouth, the other through that of his crier. In fact, when a crier says something about a court, it is not written in the minutes: "The crier said," but rather it is written that it was said by the person who ordered the crier to say it. 9. Let us listen, brothers, to these two precepts in order to understand them and place ourselves in a plan of peace between one and the other. Let us agree with our hearts, and the holy Scripture will not appear discordant in any of its parts. They are totally true; Both are true, but we must discern when we have to do one thing and when another; Sometimes you have to correct your brother alone, and other times you have to correct him in the presence of everyone so that others also feel afraid. If we have to do this once and that once, we have the agreement of the Scriptures and, putting it into practice and obeying the precepts, we will not err. But someone will tell me: "When should I behave in one way and when in another, lest I correct alone when I have to correct in public, or correct in public when I have to correct in secret?" 10. more secretly those that are committed more secretly. Diversify the moments and the Scripture agrees. 11. Let us act like this; This is how we must act not only when people sin against us, but also when any man sins, in such a way that his sin is unknown to others. We must correct and censure in secret, lest by wanting to do it in public we betray the man. Our intention is to censor and correct; What if the enemy wants to hear something that will lead to punishment? Suppose that the bishop, and only he, knows that someone is a murderer. I want to correct him publicly, but what you are looking for is to put him on the list of those accused. I neither betray him, nor ignore him in any way; I correct him in secret, I put before his eyes the judgment of God; I terrorize him with a conscience stained with blood; I persuade him to do penance. We must be imbued with this charity. Therefore, sometimes men blame us for barely correcting them; either they judge that we do not know what we really know, or they think that we are silent about what we know. But perhaps what you know I know too, although I do not make the correction before you, because I want to heal, not accuse. entangled in such sin and burdened with a stained conscience, that that wound is mortal; something that, sometimes, driven by I don't know what perversity, those who commit it despise. Where is what we have heard today: God judges fornicators and adulterers? Pay attention, therefore, whoever you are who suffers from such a disease.
